“If you understand something in only one way, then you don't really understand it at all. The secret of what anything means to us depends on how we've connected it to all other things we know. Well-connected representations let you turn ideas around in your mind, to envision things from many perspectives until you find one that works for you. And that's what we mean by thinking!”

“如果你只用一种方式理解某件事，那你根本就没真正理解它。任何事物对我们意味着什么，取决于我们如何将它与我们已知的一切联系起来。良好的关联性能让你在脑海中反复思考，从多个角度设想事物，直到找到一个适合你的角度。这就是我们所说的思考！”

-Marvin Minsky

-马文·明斯基

Introduction

介绍

What makes somebody smart?

什么使人聪明？

Is it raw brainpower? Accumulated knowledge? Is it just academic learning or does it also include your experiences, people skills and intuition?

是纯粹的脑力？还是积累的知识？仅仅是学术学习，还是也包括你的经验、人际交往能力和直觉？

Intelligence is difficult to define. Although IQ tests and various exams try to measure it, deciding what makes somebody smart is hard to do. I prefer to avoid universal definitions and focus on a more practical one: Being smart means being able to learn quickly, remember a large amount of information and be able to sort that information in a way that achieves your goals.

智力难以定义。尽管智商测试和各种考试试图衡量智力，但要确定一个人是否聪明却并非易事。我倾向于避免使用普适的定义，而更注重实用性：聪明意味着能够快速学习、记住大量信息，并能有效地利用这些信息来实现目标。

This is a much more personal definition. Learning goals can differ from person to person. You might just want to get A’s in all your courses. John might want to become a master at computer programming. Susan might want to retain more from 7

这是一个更加个人化的定义。学习目标因人而异。你可能只想在所有课程中都拿到A。约翰可能想成为计算机编程大师。苏珊可能想记住更多7个知识点。

the books she reads in her spare time. Another person might want to be able to apply concepts to business situations.

她利用空闲时间阅读的书籍。其他人可能希望能够将概念应用于商业情境中。

It’s up to you to decide what being smart means.

聪明的定义由你来决定。

This book isn’t about reaching an arbitrary definition of intelligence. Rather, it’s about giving you a strategy for learning. From this strategy, called holistic learning, I’ll provide a set of different tools to put that theory into practice.

这本书并非旨在对智力下一个武断的定义，而是旨在为你提供一种学习策略。基于这种名为“整体学习”的策略，我将提供一系列不同的工具，帮助你将理论付诸实践。

Some of these tools won’t fit your learning style or goals. That’s fine. My hopes is to provide a large assortment of tools that, with the backing of the holistic learning strategy, you can use to tailor your own approach. With practice many of these techniques can become powerful weapons in your learning arsenal.

有些工具可能并不适合你的学习风格或目标。没关系。我希望提供种类丰富的工具，并结合整体学习策略，帮助你量身定制学习方法。通过练习，许多技巧都能成为你学习的有力武器。

This book has two major goals. First, the holistic learning strategy should give you a model for how to learn better. Without an easily understandable theory of learning, it is difficult to make improvements. By seeing the holistic learning strategy you have a basis for identifying your weaknesses and improving the way you learn.

本书有两个主要目标。首先，整体学习策略旨在为你提供一个更有效的学习方法模型。如果没有易于理解的学习理论，就很难取得进步。通过了解整体学习策略，你可以找到自身学习弱点并改进学习方法的基础。

The second objective of this book is to provide a variety of learning techniques.

本书的第二个目标是提供多种学习技巧。

Throughout the book I’ll explain what these techniques are and how they fit within the holistic learning strategy. Included with this book are exercise printouts so you can 8

本书中，我将解释这些技巧是什么，以及它们如何融入整体学习策略。本书附有练习题打印件，以便您可以进行练习。

practice these methods.

练习这些方法。

I wish you the best of luck in all your learning efforts and hope you enjoy the book.

祝你学习一切顺利，希望你喜欢这本书。

It took a great deal of effort, tweaking and experimentation to write. Hopefully that effort has been well invested and you can improve the way you think.

写作过程耗费了大量精力，需要反复调整和试验。希望这些努力没有白费，并且能够帮助你改进思维方式。

9

My Story

我的故事

I’ve always been able to learn quickly. Getting A’s and A+’s with little studying before tests wasn’t a challenge for me throughout school. While in University, I’ve maintained an average that sits between A and A+. Despite this, I don’t spend more than the average person on homework. In fact, I might even spend less.

我一直都学得很快。从学生时代起，考试前几乎不用怎么复习就能拿到A或A+，这对我来说轻而易举。上了大学之后，我的平均成绩也一直保持在A到A+之间。尽管如此，我花在作业上的时间并不比一般人多。事实上，我花在作业上的时间可能还更少。

Once, I wrote an inter-provincial test (I’m Canadian) for chemistry. The only problem: I didn’t know I was supposed to write the test until a pencil and bubble sheet were sitting in front of me. On top of this, the test was on material I wasn’t familiar with and topics that were never covered in my class. I was given an hour and a half to write the exam. I left after forty minutes because I wanted to eat lunch.

有一次，我参加了一场跨省化学考试（我是加拿大人）。问题是：直到铅笔和答题卡摆在我面前，我才知道自己要参加考试。更糟糕的是，考试内容我完全不熟悉，而且有些知识点课堂上根本没讲过。考试时间是一个半小时。我考了四十分钟就离开了，因为我想吃午饭。

I won first place and received a check for $400.

我获得了第一名，并收到了一张 400 美元的支票。

Self-learning has also occupied my time. I’ve taught myself several programming languages, business and writing skills and my bookshelf has hundreds of books I’ve read 10

自学也占据了我不少时间。我自学了好几种编程语言、商业和写作技能，我的书架上摆放着数百本我读过的书。

in just the past two years. I’ve also dabbled in graphic design, musical composition and anything I could get my hands on.

仅仅在过去的两年里，我还涉猎了平面设计、音乐创作以及任何我能接触到的东西。

Learning has always come easily to me.

我学习一直都很轻松。

Up until this point, I’d just be another smart kid. “Gifted” might fit as well, although there are people whose mental feats would put my small achievements to shame. I’d be just another kid who got a more favorable genetic cocktail, had pushy parents or some sort of glandular accident.

在此之前，我不过是个聪明的孩子。“天才”或许也算贴切，尽管有些人的智力成就远超我。我可能只是个基因更好、父母管教更严或者遭遇某种腺体疾病的孩子。

And if you read this far, you could probably slap on arrogant and boastful.

如果你读到这里，你大概可以给这个词加上“傲慢自大”和“爱吹牛”的字眼了。

Until recently I probably would have agreed with you. But then something strange happened. I began to notice something different about myself and people even smarter than me. It wasn’t just that smart people learned better or faster.

直到最近，我可能都会同意你的观点。但后来发生了一件奇怪的事。我开始注意到自己和比我聪明的人身上有些不同。不仅仅是聪明人学得更好更快。

They learned differently.

他们的学习方式不同。

Smarts requires a different strategy. Smart people had picked up different tactics, 11

聪明人需要不同的策略。聪明人会采取不同的战术，11

sometimes intentionally but usually completely without awareness of them. It was these different strategies that made the difference in understanding.

有时是有意为之，但通常是完全无意识的。正是这些不同的策略造成了理解上的差异。

That different strategy I called holistic learning. I call it holistic learning because it challenges you to view learning as a comprehensive whole, instead of a list of memorized facts. Smart people tend to make fewer distinctions between branches of knowledge and can easily relate one set of understandings to another.

我把这种不同的学习策略称为整体学习。之所以称之为整体学习，是因为它挑战你将学习视为一个整体，而不是一堆需要记忆的事实。聪明的人往往较少区分知识分支，并且能够轻松地将不同的理解联系起来。

By learning holistically, smart people are able to quickly integrate new information. More importantly, this information sticks. They actually “get” the concepts and see how the concepts relate to far more than just the problems given.

通过整体学习，聪明的人能够快速整合新信息。更重要的是，这些信息能够牢记于心。他们真正理解了概念，并且明白这些概念与实际问题之外的诸多方面有何关联。

Once I was told a story that demonstrates this point perfectly: Once upon a time, a student was in a physics class. He had achieved an otherwise perfect score, but the marker had graded him poorly on one question. The question had asked him how he would measure the height of a building using a barometer.

我曾经听过一个故事，完美地诠释了这一点：从前，有个学生在上物理课。他其他题目都得了满分，但有一题老师给他打了低分。那道题问的是，如何用气压计测量建筑物的高度。

The student had written down, “Go to the top of the building. Drop the barometer and count the seconds until it smashes on the sidewalk below. Then use the formula for 12

学生写下：“到楼顶去。扔下气压计，数秒直到它摔碎在下面的人行道上。然后用公式计算12。”

acceleration by gravity to determine the height of the building.”

利用重力加速度来确定建筑物的高度。

Of course, having referenced a barometer, the

当然，既然提到了晴雨表，那么……

tester expected the student to use air pressure as a tool for measuring height. Since this answer did not

考官期望学生使用气压作为测量高度的工具。由于这个答案不符合要求。

demonstrate that the student knew how to solve

证明该学生知道如何解决问题

questions about air pressure, he couldn’t pass that

关于气压的问题，他答不上来。

portion of the test.

测试的一部分。

When the student brought up that his answer did solve the question being asked, the professor made a compromise. He said that he would let the student answer the question again with a different method. And if the student solved the problem again, he would award him the marks for the question.

当学生指出他的答案确实解决了问题时，教授做出了妥协。他说他允许学生用不同的方法重新回答这个问题。如果学生再次解决了问题，他将给学生这道题的分数。

Immediately the student responded that he would use the barometer to bang on the door of the landlord in the building. When the landlord answered the door, he would ask, “How tall is this building?”

学生立即回答说，他会用气压计敲房东的门。房东开门后，他会问：“这栋楼有多高？”

At once, the professor saw what the student was doing. He asked him if he knew of any other methods to reach the answer. The student said that he did.

教授立刻看穿了学生的思路，问他是否知道其他解题方法。学生回答说知道。

13

He recommended tying a long string to the barometer and measuring the length of the string. Or swinging the string as a pendulum and inferring the height by the motion it created.

他建议将一根长绳系在气压计上，测量绳子的长度；或者像摆锤一样摆动绳子，通过摆动产生的运动来推断高度。

The professor decided to award the student the marks. As the story goes, the student was a young Niels Bohr, later becoming the famous physicist and discovering the nature of electrons inside atoms.

教授决定给这位学生打分。据说，这位学生就是年轻的尼尔斯·玻尔，他后来成为著名的物理学家，发现了原子内部电子的本质。

This student didn’t just know how to get the answer. He also understood the entire scope for which the problem existed. Instead of seeing the problem in the same terms he had been taught, he could easily view it a number of ways.

这位学生不仅知道如何得出答案，他还理解了问题的全部内涵。他没有局限于之前所学的思维方式，而是能够轻松地从多个角度看待问题。

The goal of holistic learning is to replicate this process with the information you want to learn.

整体学习的目标是将这一过程复制到你想要学习的信息中。

14

How to Use This Book

如何使用本书

This book isn’t designed to be read once, instantly making you a superior learner.

这本书并非旨在让你读一遍就能立刻成为学习高手。

Instead, think of it as a handbook. While the broader concepts of holistic learning might be understood the in the first reading, all techniques require practice. Expecting to master these techniques immediately is like trying to hit a bulls-eye with an arrow, when you’ve never held a bow before.

相反，不妨把它看作一本手册。虽然初读或许就能理解整体学习的基本概念，但所有技巧都需要练习。期望立刻掌握这些技巧，就像从未摸过弓箭就想射中靶心一样。

That is why, I've included with this book supplemental exercises and printouts.

因此，我在本书中附上了补充练习题和打印材料。

They can provide starting points the types of learning challenges these techniques are meant to solve.

它们可以提供一些切入点，说明这些技巧旨在解决哪些类型的学习挑战。

Initially adopting these techniques may slow your learning down. Any transition to a new method will have an adjustment period. But once you become comfortable with these techniques you can learn more effectively without wasting as much time trying to relearn material you didn’t understand the first time.

刚开始采用这些技巧可能会减慢你的学习速度。任何新方法的过渡都需要一个适应期。但是，一旦你适应了这些技巧，你就能更有效地学习，而不会浪费那么多时间重新学习你第一次没理解的内容。

These techniques can’t rest just within an academic setting. Holistic learning needs to encompass anything you want to understand. The more broadly you can apply these 15

这些技巧不能仅仅局限于学术环境。整体学习需要涵盖你想要理解的一切。你越能广泛地应用这15种技巧，就越能更好地理解和运用它们。

methods, the better they function as a tool for increasing your understanding.

方法越好，它们就越能有效地帮助你加深理解。

So the next time you pick up a book, attend a class or learn something new, think about the strategy of holistic learning. Ask yourself how you can apply it and what techniques you want to use. As the techniques become habits, it will be easier to permanently integrate any new idea.

所以，下次当你拿起一本书、参加一堂课或学习新知识时，不妨思考一下整体学习策略。问问自己如何运用它，以及你想使用哪些技巧。当这些技巧成为习惯后，就能更容易地将任何新理念永久地融入你的生活中。

Quick Tip!

小贴士！

Holistic learning introduces many new concepts and techniques.

整体学习引入了许多新的概念和技巧。

You'll get the best results if you focus on learning only one skill at a time.

如果你一次只专注于学习一项技能，就能取得最佳效果。

Throughout the second half of the book, you will see Mind Challenges.

本书后半部分将探讨思维挑战。

These challenges are set up specifically to help you adopt these new learning methods.

这些挑战旨在帮助你适应这些新的学习方法。
