◦ Part I ◦

第一部分

The Holistic

整体

Learning Strategy

学习策略

What is Holistic Learning?

什么是整体学习？

Holistic learning is the opposite of rote memorization.

整体学习与死记硬背截然相反。

Rote memorization involves repeating information enough times with the hopes that it will stick. Trying to remember a physics formula by repeating it to yourself dozens of times is learning by rote. This also a poor way to learn.

死记硬背是指反复重复信息，希望能够记住它。试图通过反复默念几十遍来记住一个物理公式就是死记硬背，这也是一种糟糕的学习方法。

If you read the story about the student from the last section, you can probably see that smart people don't learn by rote. Do you think Niels Borh, as a young physics student, had formulas memorized in his head? Coming up with so many unique ways to solve a physics problem, it was the opposite. He understood what every symbol in the formula meant, and knew why it was there. He knew the rules so he knew how to break them.

如果你读过上一节中关于那个学生的故事，你大概就能明白，聪明人并非靠死记硬背来学习。你认为年轻的物理系学生尼尔斯·玻尔会把公式牢记于心吗？恰恰相反，他能想出那么多独特的解法来解决物理问题。他理解公式中每个符号的含义，也明白它们存在的意义。他了解规则，所以也知道如何打破规则。

Holistic learning is a theory for learning that more accurately describes how your brain works. Your brain isn’t the same as a computer filing system. Computer files are stored in strips of 1's and 0's in locations on a hard drive. Your brain stores information 18

整体学习理论是一种学习理论，它更准确地描述了大脑的运作方式。你的大脑并不等同于电脑文件系统。电脑文件以 1 和 0 组成的条带形式存储在硬盘上的不同位置。而你的大脑则以另一种方式存储信息。

as associations between billions of neurons.

作为数十亿神经元之间的关联。

Rote memorization might work if we had computer

如果我们有电脑，死记硬背或许可行。

brains. All it would take is an accurate copy of

大脑。只需要一份精确的副本……

information and you could memorize anything.

信息量很大，你可以记住任何东西。

Unfortunately, we don’t have computer brains and that is why rote memorization is a less effective way to

遗憾的是，我们没有电脑般的大脑，这就是为什么死记硬背是一种效率较低的学习方法。

learn.Holistic learning takes a different approach.

学习。整体学习采取不同的方法。

Instead of trying to memorize information by making a perfect copy in your brain, it uses the web of neurons you have. Holistic learning creates webs of information. One idea relates to another idea. That interrelating of ideas allows you to easily navigate through complete understandings.

整体学习并非试图通过在大脑中完美复制信息来记忆，而是利用你大脑中已有的神经元网络。整体学习构建信息网络，一个概念与其他概念相互关联。这种概念间的相互联系使你能够轻松地理解整体概念。

With holistic learning, ideas aren’t learned in isolation. If you follow holistic learning closely enough, you’ll soon realize that it is impossible to learn an idea in isolation. Learning anything requires associations. The more associations you can create and the stronger those associations are, the better.

整体学习法认为，概念并非孤立地学习。如果你认真践行整体学习法，很快就会意识到，孤立地学习任何概念都是行不通的。学习任何事物都需要联想。你建立的联想越多、越牢固，效果就越好。

Rote memorization would suggest learning fits into neat little boxes. A box for math containing algebra, arithmetic and calculus. Your calculus box contains more 19

死记硬背会让人觉得学习应该被装进整齐的小盒子里。比如数学盒子里装着代数、算术和微积分。你的微积分盒子里装的远不止这些。

boxes for how to find the derivative of a function, and a few common applications of those rules. Nowhere does your calculus box contain information on biology, history or the plot of a science fiction movie.

教材里有关于如何求函数导数的方框，以及这些规则的一些常见应用。你的微积分教材里绝对不会包含生物学、历史或科幻电影的剧情信息。

But learning doesn’t fit into boxes. Learning fits into webs.

但学习并非要被框定在固定的模式中，而是要融入错综复杂的网络之中。

A holistic learner wouldn’t take such an organized approach to storing information (which might explain why so many smart people have horrible organization skills).

一个整体学习者不会采用如此系统化的方式来存储信息（这或许可以解释为什么很多聪明人组织能力很差）。

Instead holistic learners connect everything. A derivative isn’t just a formula, it’s a feeling, an image and you can relate it to flying a supersonic jet.

相反，整体学习者会将所有事物联系起来。导数不仅仅是一个公式，它是一种感觉，一种图像，你可以把它比作驾驶超音速喷气式飞机。

Rote memorization seems to make sense

死记硬背似乎有道理。

when you can’t see the alternative. When you

当你看不到其他选择的时候。当你

don’t know the steps learning should follow

不知道学习应该遵循哪些步骤。

and lack techniques to move through those

并且缺乏应对这些问题的技巧。

steps, simply pounding information in your

步骤，简单地将信息灌输到你的……

skull seems to work. This is like a caveman

头骨似乎能用。这就像个穴居人。

using a rock to hunt mammoths instead of a

用石头而不是……来猎杀猛犸象

rifle. Until you understand the steps and

步枪。直到你理解了步骤和

techniques for learning, rote memorization is

学习技巧，死记硬背是

20

crude and inefficient, but it still works better than nothing.

虽然粗糙且效率低下，但总比没有强。

How You Store Information

您如何存储信息

Holistic learning is my hypothesis for how learning actually works. I say hypothesis because holistic learning is less scientific fact and more practical metaphor.

整体学习是我关于学习实际运作方式的假设。之所以称之为假设，是因为整体学习与其说是科学事实，不如说是一种实用的比喻。

Science still has a long way to go to discover the physical connections in the mind.

科学在揭示大脑中的物理联系方面还有很长的路要走。

Holistic learning simply suggests one way of viewing how smart people manage to learn.

整体学习法只是提供了一种看待聪明人如何学习的方式。

Whether electrons actually exist as billiard balls or violin strings jumping around a cloud of protons is less important than the implications of these metaphors. Holistic learning, similarly, is about providing an easily accessible theory that seems to fit how information is stored, rather than a description of the biological processes buried in your mind.

电子究竟是以台球或琴弦的形式在质子云中跳跃，远不如这些比喻所蕴含的意义重要。同样，整体学习旨在提供一种易于理解的理论，这种理论似乎符合信息的存储方式，而不是描述你大脑中深藏的生物过程。

Holistic learning is based on three main ideas:

全人式学习基于三大理念：

1) Constructs

1）构造

2) Models

2）模型

3) Highways

3）高速公路

21

As I’ll explain, seeing how these three elements fit together makes applying the holistic learning strategy easier. Just as knowing the different chess plays is useless without knowing that a bishop moves diagonally, knowing the holistic learning strategy is useless unless we both operate from the same points of reference.

正如我将要解释的，了解这三个要素如何相互关联，能使整体学习策略的应用更加容易。正如了解不同的国际象棋走法却不知道主教斜线走法毫无用处一样，如果我们双方没有相同的参照点，了解整体学习策略也毫无意义。

Quick Tip!

小贴士！

Holistic learning is based on linking ideas as a way of remembering and applying them. The best techniques to start learning are metaphor, visceralization, flow-based notetaking and diagraming. These methods form the foundation of holistic learning.

整体学习的核心在于将各种概念联系起来，以此来记忆和应用它们。最佳的学习入门技巧包括比喻、具象化、流程式笔记和图表绘制。这些方法构成了整体学习的基础。

22

23

Constructs

构造

A construct defines a set of tightly interlinked understandings. For example, if you’ve tried your hand at learning to create programs with C++, you probably have a C++ construct. This construct defines all your knowledge about C++ and is the sum total of all the interconnected ideas about C++.

概念定义了一组紧密相关的理解。例如，如果你尝试过学习用 C++ 编写程序，那么你可能已经掌握了一个 C++ 概念。这个概念定义了你所有关于 C++ 的知识，是所有关于 C++ 的相互关联的想法的总和。

Think of a construct as being like a city in your mind. Within a city you have thousands of buildings you can travel between. Some are big and important and are linked by roads to hundreds of other buildings in your city. Others are less important and only have a few dirt paths leading to them.

把建筑想象成你脑海中的一座城市。在这座城市里，有成千上万栋建筑供你穿梭。有些建筑规模宏大、举足轻重，通过道路与其他数百栋建筑相连。而另一些建筑则相对次要，只有几条土路通往那里。

In the landscape of your knowledge, your mind is full of these cities. Your basic math and language skills are probably large, efficient cities. You have no problem navigating from 3+4-10 to 10*3+7. These questions are easy because your constructs for basic math are highly developed.

在你的知识版图中，你的脑海中充满了这些城市。你的基础数学和语言技能就像一座座规模宏大、高效运转的城市。你能够轻松地从 3+4=10 过渡到 10*3+7。这些问题对你来说很简单，因为你的基础数学概念已经非常成熟。

Understanding is the result of a highly developed construct.

理解是高度发达的认知结构的结果。

Are there certain subjects you just “get”? These subjects are easy for you to understand and seem obvious. Chances are this is because those subjects lie within 24

你是否对某些科目“特别擅长”？这些科目对你来说很容易理解，而且似乎显而易见。这很可能是因为这些科目属于你熟悉的范畴。

highly developed constructs. They are like cities where the roads are clean and free of traffic congestions. The buildings are maintained and rarely are entire pathways blocked off.

高度发达的建筑群。它们就像城市一样，道路干净整洁，交通畅通无阻。建筑物维护良好，很少出现整条道路被封锁的情况。

In contrast, are there certain subjects you have difficulty understanding. These would be like newly constructed or poorly designed cities. The roads don’t lead to many places. It is easy to get lost and there are many buildings which need to exist but either haven’t been built yet or have been lost in the maze of roads and wrong directions.

相反，你是否有一些难以理解的领域？比如新建或设计糟糕的城市。道路通往的地方不多，很容易迷路，而且有很多应该存在的建筑要么还没建，要么淹没在错综复杂的道路和错误的方向中。

Ask yourself this question: In a city which building would be the easiest to locate?

请扪心自问：在一座城市里，哪栋建筑最容易找到？

A) One that is connected to many other buildings through hundreds of roads, or B) One that has a single dirt path connecting it to only one other building.

A) 通过数百条道路与其他许多建筑物相连的建筑物，或者 B) 只有一条土路与其他一个建筑物相连的建筑物。

The building in A would be much easier to find. If you got going down the wrong path, you wouldn’t have much trouble eventually reaching your destination. With the situation in B, you are relying on chance that you stumble upon the only building that connects with your final location.

A处的建筑更容易找到。即使走错了路，最终也能顺利到达目的地。而B处的情况则不同，你只能靠运气碰巧找到唯一一座通往最终目的地的建筑。

25

When building constructs, your goal is to create as many possible interconnections as possible between ideas. Smart people tend to do this process naturally. As each concept comes up, it is automatically linked with other ideas.

构建概念时，你的目标是在各种想法之间建立尽可能多的联系。聪明的人往往能自然而然地做到这一点。每个概念一出现，就会自动与其他想法联系起来。

You probably use this process already, but perhaps not as effectively as people who learn effortlessly. The holistic learning strategy has many different techniques for manually linking ideas. Once those methods become habits, it doesn’t take long before new connections are made.

你可能已经在使用这种方法了，但或许不如那些学习毫不费力的人那样有效。整体学习策略包含许多不同的技巧，可以用来手动连接各种想法。一旦这些方法成为习惯，很快就能建立起新的联系。

Quick Tip!

小贴士！

Your constructs weren't built in a day. There is no magical technique to immediately “get” any subject. Having a powerful construct comes from linking concepts together, one idea at a time.

你的理论体系并非一日建成。没有任何神奇的技巧可以让你瞬间“掌握”任何学科。构建强大的理论体系源于将各种概念串联起来，一次一个想法。

26

27

Models

模型

If constructs are the door to holistic learning, then models are the key. Models are simplified constructs. They are snapshots of larger understandings designed to be portable and easy to store. Models are essential when trying to learn new concepts quickly.

如果说概念是通往整体学习的大门，那么模型就是钥匙。模型是对概念的简化，是对更宏观理解的概括，便于携带和存储。在快速学习新概念时，模型至关重要。

To understand what a model is, think about this book. A model for this book would be the table of contents. In a few pages, they summarize the thousands of words contained in the book. If you wanted to describe the contents of this book quickly, you would probably start there instead of reading the entire book word-for-word.

要理解什么是模型，不妨想想这本书。这本书的模型就是目录。目录用寥寥数页就概括了书中数千字的内容。如果你想快速描述这本书的内容，你很可能会从目录入手，而不是逐字逐句地阅读全书。

Models can take a variety of forms. The goal, however, is always the same: compressing information. By taking several core concepts and linking them together into one form, you create a model. Models are essential when you are just starting to build a construct or making large additions to current constructs.

模型可以采取多种形式，但其目标始终如一：压缩信息。通过将几个核心概念连接起来，形成一个统一的模型。在构建新结构或对现有结构进行重大扩展时，模型至关重要。

I used a model when I was first learning what a subspace was. A subspace is a mathematical term defining a portion of a larger vector space. An example of a vector space might be three dimensions. A subspace within that vector space could be a two dimensional plane.

我最初学习子空间概念时使用了一个模型。子空间是一个数学术语，它定义了一个较大向量空间的一部分。例如，三维向量空间就是一个三维向量空间。该向量空间中的一个子空间可以是二维平面。

28

The model I used to represent this subspace was a

我用来表示这个子空间的模型是

bright, blue infinite background. This was the three dimensional vector space. Then I visualized a red

明亮的蓝色无限背景。这就是三维向量空间。然后我想象出一个红色

translucent grid slicing through the background. This was my subspace.

半透明的网格穿过背景。这就是我的子空间。

This model only represents some possibilities for

该模型仅代表一些可能性

subspaces. A subspace could also be a line within a plane, or a section of an entire matrix of numbers. Models do not need to have perfect accuracy, they only need to combine several ideas to make them more manageable. As my understanding of subspaces grew, I made adjustments to my previous model and created new models.

子空间。子空间也可以是平面内的一条直线，或者整个数字矩阵的一部分。模型不需要完美精确，只需要结合几个概念使其更易于管理。随着我对子空间理解的加深，我对之前的模型进行了调整，并创建了新的模型。

Once I had a construct, I could build out that understanding and correct any errors.

一旦我有了概念框架，我就可以不断完善理解并纠正任何错误。

Another time I used a model was when teaching myself computer programming.

我另一次使用模型是在自学计算机编程的时候。

Programming languages make use of a concept known as a variable. Variables are used to store information that might change throughout the running of a program. A username, counter or key could all be stored with variables.

编程语言使用一种称为变量的概念。变量用于存储程序运行过程中可能发生变化的信息。用户名、计数器或密钥都可以存储在变量中。

I created a clear image of the variables as being types of jars, and the concept made sense. Since most variables are broken into various types (some store numbers, others 29

我把变量形象地理解为不同类型的罐子，这个概念很有道理。因为大多数变量都被细分为各种类型（有些存储数字，有些存储29个罐子）。

words or letters) I could imagine different jars with different openings for holding different types of data.

（文字或字母）我可以想象用不同开口的罐子来盛放不同类型的数据。

This model for variables stored several key ideas into one image or concept. This compression formed the seed for which future understandings could be linked and

这种变量模型将几个关键概念存储到一个图像或概念中。这种压缩为未来的理解奠定了基础，并使其得以联系起来。

refined.

精制。

A model doesn’t need to be an image. It only needs

模型不一定要是图像。它只需要

to be an existing understanding that compresses several key ideas into one. There are many ways to generate and expand models which I’ll discuss later in the book. Visualization is only one method.

它指的是将几个关键概念压缩成一个整体的现有理解。生成和扩展模型的方法有很多，我将在本书后面部分进行讨论。可视化只是其中一种方法。

When I learned about functions in computer programming, I imagined them working like a pencil sharpener. Dull pencils go in, and a casing concealing the machinery sharpens the pencil. Sharp pencils come out. This model doesn’t need to rest on a specific image, but just the general concept of how a pencil sharpener works.

当我学习计算机编程中的函数时，我把它想象成一个削铅笔器。钝铅笔放进去，外壳里的机械装置会削尖铅笔，削好的铅笔就出来了。这个模型不需要基于具体的图像，只需要理解削铅笔器的工作原理即可。

One construct lending tools to build models for another.

一个机构借用工具为另一个机构构建模型。

The takeaway point about models is that they act like seeds for constructs. Like a small group of pioneers with compact building materials heading to fresh ground to start a new settlement. A compressed set of key ideas that can be expanded.

模型的关键在于它们如同构筑的种子。就像一小群先驱者带着精简的建筑材料前往一片未知的土地，建立新的定居点。它们是一套可以扩展的关键理念的精炼集合。

30

31

Highways

高速公路

Constructs are built on roads linking buildings with one another. While having hundreds of intercity roads is useful, it doesn’t make use of the real power of your holistic brain. In order to do that, you need to add highways: linkages between isolated constructs.

建筑群建立在连接各个建筑物的道路之上。虽然拥有数百条城际道路很有用，但这并不能充分发挥你整体思维的真正潜力。为了做到这一点，你需要建造高速公路：连接各个孤立建筑群的桥梁。

A highway is a reference that links two completely different ideas. If you were reading a biology textbook and made comparisons from evolution to business courses you are taking, that would be a highway.

“高速公路”指的是连接两个截然不同的概念的参照点。例如，如果你正在阅读生物学教科书，并将进化论与你正在学习的商业课程进行比较，那么这就构成了一条“高速公路”。

The benefit of a highways isn’t an immediately obvious one. If you want to succeed in school, most instructors will emphasize having well defined constructs, not having a brain full of highways.

高速公路的好处并非显而易见。如果你想在学校取得成功，大多数老师都会强调要建立清晰的概念框架，而不是让大脑里充满各种高速公路。

However, highways help with creativity. Thinking “outside the box” might as well describe people who think outside of constructs. Highways allow them to do this by making connections between areas that they didn’t previously think were connected.

然而，高速公路有助于激发创造力。“跳出思维定式”或许可以用来形容那些不拘泥于既定框架的人。高速公路将原本看似无关的区域连接起来，使他们能够做到这一点。

Creativity can be seen as being able to utilize these highways to build new constructs in territories that were previously empty.

创造力可以被视为利用这些高速公路在以前空旷的地区建造新建筑的能力。

An example of when I’ve used a highway before was when I was reading The Prince, by Nicolo Machiavelli. This book outlines Machiavelli’s principles for governing 32

我之前使用过高速公路的一个例子是阅读尼科洛·马基雅维利的《君主论》时。这本书概述了马基雅维利的治国原则。

a state, ruling people and conquering other nations. Today it’s largely seen as either a work of a devious genius or a psychopath.

一个统治人民、征服其他国家的国家。如今，它被普遍认为要么是诡计多端的天才之作，要么是精神变态者的杰作。

When learning about the ideas Machiavelli presents in his book, I needed a basis to compare them to. As a result, I created my own highways between Machiavelli’s advice on statecraft and my personal experience with relationships, social settings and management. Although some of his ideas may have flaws, this approach allowed me to completely understand the ideas before deciding which I would accept or reject.

在学习马基雅维利著作中的思想时，我需要一个参照标准来进行比较。因此，我将马基雅维利的治国之道与我个人在人际关系、社交场合和管理方面的经验联系起来，构建了自己的理解框架。尽管他的一些观点可能存在缺陷，但这种方法使我能够在决定接受或拒绝哪些观点之前，充分理解这些观点。

Building highways offers you more flexibility as a learner. Normally, if you don’t understand the way an instructor teaches a subject, you’re completely lost. With highways, you can import your own understandings from different subjects.

构建知识高速公路能为学习者提供更大的灵活性。通常情况下，如果你不理解老师的授课方式，就会完全摸不着头脑。而有了知识高速公路，你可以将自己从不同学科中汲取的知识融会贯通。

33

Familiar Constructs

熟悉的结构

There are several constructs most people possess in a highly developed form. These familiar constructs are so ingrained, that they serve as an invaluable resource for models, highways and learning new subjects. There are probably many more you possess, but here are a few likely candidates:

大多数人都拥有一些高度发达的认知结构。这些熟悉的认知结构根深蒂固，是构建模型、构建思维路径和学习新知识的宝贵资源。你可能拥有更多类似的认知结构，但以下列举一些比较常见的：

Sensory Constructs

感官结构

These are probably your best developed sets of

这些可能是你开发得最好的几套……

understandings. You have hundreds of images, sounds and feelings linked together through experience. You might even want to consider sensations to be the root construct that all others are built on.

理解。你拥有数百种图像、声音和感觉，它们通过经验相互关联。你甚至可以将感觉视为所有其他概念构建的根本结构。

34

Relationship Constructs

关系结构

Stories, people and interactions define most of our

故事、人物和互动定义了我们大多数人的生活。

existence. Is it any wonder then that stories make new subjects easier to learn? Saying that halogen compounds have one less electron than noble gases is different than saying they’re neighbors on the periodic table.

存在。那么，故事能让新知识更容易学习也就不足为奇了。说卤素化合物比稀有气体少一个电子，和说它们在元素周期表上相邻，是截然不同的两回事。

Basic Math Constructs

基础数学结构

Depending on your math background, you may find

根据你的数学背景，你可能会发现

anything from arithmetic to advanced calculus to be

从算术到高等微积分，任何内容都可能涉及。

painfully obvious. These can be used as the basis for building further math constructs or you can use them to simplify linkages in other subjects.

显而易见。这些可以作为构建更复杂数学结构的基础，也可以用于简化其他学科之间的联系。

35

I’ll reference these and other familiar constructs when offering suggestions for implementing various techniques. Think of these as your capital cities which smaller settlements can be modeled after.

在提出各种技术实施方案的建议时，我会参考这些以及其他一些常见的概念。你可以把它们想象成你的首都城市，其他较小的聚落都可以模仿它们。

Constructs, Models and Highways, Oh My!

建筑、模型和公路，我的天哪！

All of this talk about constructs and models may seem abstract to start with. Don’t worry. The reason I bring them up is because they form the backbone of holistic learning.

一开始，所有这些关于概念和模型的讨论可能看起来比较抽象。别担心。我之所以提出这些概念，是因为它们构成了整体学习的基石。

Many books strive to teach different learning techniques. These are similar to the techniques I’ll describe. The difference with holistic learning is you have a background theory which explains why these techniques should work, and give you a better sense for modifying and creating your own.

许多书籍致力于教授不同的学习技巧，这些技巧与我将要描述的技巧类似。整体学习的不同之处在于，它提供了一套理论基础，解释了这些技巧为何有效，并能帮助你更好地调整和创建自己的学习方法。

By providing the background of how information is stored in your brain, hopefully it will lead you to adopt approaches that make sense within this strategy. You wouldn’t try to save computer files by telling the computer a story or typing them out twenty times. That doesn’t make sense given how we understand computers store information.

通过介绍大脑如何存储信息的背景知识，希望能够引导你采用符合这种策略的方法。你不会试图通过给电脑讲故事或把文件内容重复输入二十遍来保存电脑文件。考虑到我们对电脑信息存储方式的理解，这样做是行不通的。

Understand how your brain stores information and you can enhance the way you learn.

了解大脑如何存储信息，就能提高学习效率。

36

The Sequence of Holistic

整体序列

Learning

学习

Up until this point I’ve described what information looks like when it is stored in your head. But the real question is, how does it get there in the first place?

到目前为止，我一直在描述信息存储在大脑中的样子。但真正的问题是，信息最初是如何进入大脑的？

I’ve divided up almost all learning tasks into several unique steps. Often you won’t need to complete all the steps to understand enough to pass a test. The steps might not always follow in the same order. You may go back to the first step after completing the second before moving onto the third.

我已将几乎所有学习任务分解成几个独立的步骤。通常，你不需要完成所有步骤就能理解并通过考试。这些步骤的顺序也可能并非总是固定的。你可能在完成第二步后，需要返回第一步，然后再进行第三步。

What is important is that each of these steps represents key activities involved in learning. When you repeatedly miss a step in the process, or finish it poorly, the information won't be stored properly. Learning fails and the information doesn’t make it into your holistic web.

重要的是，这些步骤中的每一个都代表了学习过程中的关键活动。如果你反复错过某个步骤，或者完成得不够好，信息就无法被正确存储。学习就会失败，信息也无法融入你的整体认知网络。

37

By examining each step and seeing how it fits into our holistic learning theory, we can have a strategy for learning. With this strategy, you can use specific tactics to fix holes in your current technique. You can also develop new methods to replace inefficient ones you have for various steps along the holistic learning process.

通过分析每个步骤，并了解它们如何融入我们的整体学习理论，我们可以制定学习策略。有了这项策略，你就可以运用具体的技巧来弥补现有技术的不足。你还可以针对整体学习过程中的各个步骤，开发新的方法来取代效率低下的方法。

The sequence of holistic learning is:

整体学习的顺序是：

1) Acquire

1）获取

2) Understand

2）理解

3) Explore

3）探索

4) Debug

4）调试

5) Apply

5）申请

A final step which exists outside the sequence but applies to every step is Test.

序列之外还有一个步骤，但适用于每个步骤，那就是测试。

Testing is checking to see how well you are executing each of these steps. Without rigorous self-testing (by the time you reach the exam room, you’re too late) you may not realize a step was poorly executed.

测试是为了检验你对每个步骤的执行情况。如果没有严格的自我测试（等你到了考场就太晚了），你可能不会意识到某个步骤执行得不好。

38

Here are the six steps:

以下是六个步骤：

1) Acquire - The point at which information enters through your eyes and ears.

1）获取——信息通过你的眼睛和耳朵进入你的意识。

Reading, taking notes in a class or personal experiences are all part of the Acquire Phase.

阅读、课堂笔记或个人经历都属于获取阶段。

The goal here is to get accurate information in the most compressed form.

我们的目标是以最简洁的形式获取准确的信息。

2) Understand - Understanding means taking raw information and giving it a context. This would be the most basic interlinking you would need to perform in order to learn.

2）理解——理解是指将原始信息置于特定的语境中。这是学习过程中最基本的关联步骤。

3) Explore - The Explore Phase is really where holistic learning takes full force.

3）探索——探索阶段是整体学习真正发挥全部作用的阶段。

Here you form the models, highways and broader connections needed for well defined constructs.

在这里，你可以构建模型、道路和更广泛的连接，从而形成完善的结构。

4) Debug - The Debug Phase looks for errors in your models and highways. This phase prunes back your connections so invalid ones won’t remain, or will be constrained to the area they work.

4) 调试 - 调试阶段会检查模型和高速公路中的错误。此阶段会清理连接，使无效连接不再存在，或仅保留在其有效范围内的连接。

5) Apply - The Apply Phase takes debugging to the final level by making adjustments compared to how this information operates in reality. Having a set of understandings is useless if they aren’t tailored to the real world. Failure on this step could be an example of people who have book-smarts but can’t seem to use them outside the class.

5）应用——应用阶段将调试提升到最终阶段，通过根据实际情况调整信息来完善模型。如果理论知识不能应用于现实世界，那么它就毫无用处。这一步骤的失败可能就是一些书本知识丰富但无法在课堂外运用这些知识的例子。

39

6) Test - Continuously you should be testing your methods and learning throughout all six stages. This will help you quickly identify problems in the system you use for learning, and help you develop new techniques to combat weaknesses.

6）测试——在所有六个阶段中，你都应该持续测试你的方法和学习成果。这将帮助你快速发现学习系统中存在的问题，并帮助你开发新的技巧来克服弱点。

Quick Tip!

小贴士！

The different techniques in the second half of this book are suited towards different stages in the sequence. Speed reading can help in acquiring ideas, flow-based notetaking and metaphor can help in exploring ideas. Model debugging and project-based learning can help you debug and apply ideas.

本书后半部分介绍的各种技巧适用于学习过程中的不同阶段。快速阅读有助于获取思路，流程式笔记和比喻有助于探索思路。模型调试和项目式学习可以帮助你调试和应用想法。

40

41

The Acquire Phase

收购阶段

This phase represents the path information takes to enter your brain. Your ability to handle different formats of information and to eliminate clutter are essential here.

这一阶段代表信息进入大脑的路径。你处理不同格式信息和排除干扰信息的能力在此至关重要。

Here are a few things to consider when evaluating how well you perform in this phase:

以下是一些在评估你在此阶段表现时需要考虑的因素：

- How long does it take you to read a page of material with 90% comprehension?

- 你读完一页材料，理解度达到 90% 需要多长时间？

- How much of your lectures do you actual pay attention to?

- 你上课时到底有多少注意力在听讲？

In all cases, your ability to handle a medium of information forms the first filter which can enhance or destroy your learning efforts. Any information lost here is gone forever. No amount of holistic learning techniques can make up for a failure to acquire the important ideas.

在任何情况下，你处理信息媒介的能力都构成了第一道筛选屏障，它既能促进你的学习，也能阻碍你的学习。任何在此环节丢失的信息都将永远消失。再多的整体学习技巧也无法弥补未能掌握重要概念的缺陷。

When acquiring information, you have three major goals: 1) Simplicity

获取信息时，你有三个主要目标：1）简洁性

2) Volume

2）体积

3) Speed

3）速度

42

Acquiring for Simplicity

为简化而获取

Read the following words:

阅读下列单词：

“I am. I am. I am. I am. I am. I am.”

“我是。我是。我是。我是。我是。我是。我是。”

What is the point of reading all these words? There is a lot of redundancy as many words are repeated. You could have simply read: “I am. x6“ and that would have contained exactly the same information.

读这些字有什么意义？很多词重复，内容冗余。你完全可以只读“我是。x6”，这样就包含了完全相同的信息。

Reading requires that you consume the purest information possible. While most authors and lectures don’t fill space with dead air, they will often give you information you don’t need to form models and constructs. A professor that breaks down the meaning of a formula may be giving a lot of redundancy if you can determine how the formula is created on your own.

阅读要求你尽可能获取最纯粹的信息。虽然大多数作者和讲座不会用无意义的内容填充篇幅，但他们常常会提供一些你构建模型和概念时并不需要的信息。例如，如果你自己就能推导出某个公式的推导过程，那么教授对公式的详细解释可能就显得多余了。

Simplicity means you acquire the information with the lowest amount of redundancy. Supporting examples are important to the degree that they help you form models. When you don’t need them, don’t bother acquiring them.

简洁意味着以最少的冗余获取信息。佐证示例的重要性在于它们能否帮助你构建模型。如果不需要，就无需费心获取。

43

Acquiring for Volume

批量采购

As long as you account for simplicity, your should be trying to get the most information possible. Reading one sentence from this book offers far less understanding than reading every page. The more information you can process, the more you will understand. Someone who reads a 100 books a year will usually have more knowledge than someone who reads only 2 or 3.

只要你考虑到简洁性，就应该尽可能多地获取信息。读这本书里的一句话远不如读完每一页来得深入。你处理的信息越多，理解得就越透彻。一年读100本书的人通常比只读2、3本书的人知识更渊博。

Acquiring for Speed

加速获取

The final goal of acquiring information is speed. All things being equal, reading a book in thirty minutes is better than taking an hour. Speed tends to work against volume and simplicity. The faster you go, generally the less information you can absorb and the less discriminating you can be in determining what to acquire.

获取信息的最终目标是速度。在其他条件相同的情况下，30分钟读完一本书比花一个小时读完要好。速度往往不利于信息的获取量和简洁性。通常来说，速度越快，你能吸收的信息就越少，你在选择需要获取的信息时也就越缺乏选择性。

The Acquire Phase can be enhanced by adopting better reading and listening methods. Even at this early stage, most people have significant room for improvements.

通过采用更好的阅读和聆听方法，可以提升习得阶段的学习效果。即使在这个早期阶段，大多数人仍有很大的提升空间。

I’ll discuss some of these methods in Part II of this book.

我将在本书第二部分讨论其中的一些方法。

44

45

The Understand Phase

理解阶段

Input is nothing without comprehension. If you don’t understand the surface of what a book is trying to say, the chances of remembering it for an exam or applying it in real life are almost nonexistent. Most people intuitively feel the Understand Phase.

没有理解，输入就毫无意义。如果你不理解一本书想要表达的内容，那么你几乎不可能记住它以备考试或将其应用到现实生活中。大多数人都能凭直觉感受到理解阶段。

The information makes sense even if it still isn’t firmly rooted into your brain.

即使这些信息还没有完全印在你的脑海里，但它们本身是有道理的。

The holistic learning sequence could be seen as taking three layers, each expanding the degree of understanding. The Understand Phase forms the first layer, followed by Explore and finally Apply. Each provides more depth to the information you come across.

整体学习流程可以看作包含三个层次，每个层次都加深理解的程度。理解阶段是第一层，其次是探索阶段，最后是应用阶段。每个阶段都让你对所接触的信息有更深入的理解。

With the Understand Phase, you are getting at the surface of information. As an example, say you are learning a new mathematical formula. You know the basics of what the symbols in the formula stand for, and possible problems that could be solved using this formula. If you repeat the formula enough times, you might even remember it. Learning by rote is learning with only the Understand Phase.

在理解阶段，你只是触及信息的表面。例如，假设你正在学习一个新的数学公式。你了解公式中符号的基本含义，以及可以用这个公式解决的问题。如果你反复背诵公式，甚至可能记住它。死记硬背就只是停留在理解阶段的学习。

The Understand Phase, is where most people stop and smart people go beyond.

理解阶段，是大多数人止步的地方，而聪明的人则会超越它。

Simply reaching this phase shows that you have linked the information enough so you can understand the context. The formula isn’t just random squiggles and letters.

仅仅达到这个阶段就表明你已经将信息充分联系起来，能够理解其含义。这个公式并非只是随意的符号和字母。

46

Unfortunately, it isn’t much more. You might not be able to determine how the formula was derived, how it relates to other formulas or how it can be applied to problems outside what you’ve been taught.

遗憾的是，也就仅此而已。你可能无法确定这个公式是如何推导出来的，它与其他公式有何关联，或者它如何应用于你所学内容之外的问题。

Despite the limitations of stopping at this phase, it is the most critical. Unless you can acquire and understand the surface of information, you have no chance of building depth.

尽管止步于此阶段存在局限性，但这却是最关键的阶段。除非你能获取并理解信息的表面，否则你根本无法深入理解。

Quick Tip!

小贴士！

Not being able to understand something instantly, isn't a sign you aren't learning holistically. My suggestion, when you encounter a tricky subject is to break it into components. Narrow down specifically what you don't understand so you can use further reading to fill the gaps.

无法立即理解某些内容并不代表你没有全面学习。我的建议是，当你遇到棘手的问题时，将其分解成各个组成部分。具体找出你不理解的地方，然后通过进一步阅读来填补知识空白。

47

48

The Explore Phase

探索阶段

Exploration is really the start of holistic learning. With your basic understanding that covers the surface of information, you now try to link that information to other concepts. Here you would start using models to simplify and expand your constructs.

探索是整体学习的真正起点。在对信息有了初步了解之后，你现在尝试将这些信息与其他概念联系起来。这时，你会开始使用模型来简化和扩展你的认知结构。

You would also broaden your understanding of not only how the information is derived, but what it is related to.

你不仅可以拓宽对信息来源方式的理解，还可以拓宽对信息相关内容的理解。

A holistic learner would take the formula I mentioned in the last phase, and explore it. Where does it come from? What do the different components of the formula represent? What elements of the formula can be altered and how does that change results? What other formulas are similar to this in function or form?

一个具有整体学习能力的学习者会运用我在上一阶段提到的公式，并对其进行探索。这个公式从何而来？公式中的各个组成部分分别代表什么？公式中的哪些元素可以改变，改变后结果又会如何变化？还有哪些公式在功能或形式上与这个公式相似？

Answering these questions may take a bit of time if you aren’t used to them. But once you make these methods a habit, exploration will naturally take over.

如果你不习惯这些问题，回答它们可能需要一些时间。但一旦你养成这些方法的习惯，探索自然就会发生。

Understanding won’t be enough because curiosity will drive you to connect it to new material.

仅仅理解是不够的，因为好奇心会驱使你将所学知识与新的知识联系起来。

There are three major ways you can explore ideas: depth, lateral and vertical exploration.

探索想法主要有三种方式：深度探索、横向探索和纵向探索。

49

Depth Exploration

深度探索

Information comes from somewhere. Where does a formula come from? How was a discovery made? Why are things the way they are?

信息来源于某个地方。公式从何而来？一项发现是如何做出的？事物为何会是现在这个样子？

Depth exploration requires that you create links into information. Instead of just understanding a formula, you understand its proof. You understand why the proof was developed and by whom. Now, through depth exploration, your formula becomes supported underneath a foundation of other linked ideas.

深度探索要求你建立信息之间的联系。你不仅要理解公式本身，还要理解它的证明过程。你要明白这个证明过程的缘由和证明者。通过深度探索，你的公式便建立在其他相关概念的基础之上。

The disadvantage with depth exploration is that it usually requires additional research. Some classes will provide some depth, but rarely the amount necessary to explore an idea. Depth exploration is probably the best method to lock an idea in place, but also the most time consuming.

深度探索的缺点在于它通常需要额外的研究。有些课程会提供一些深度探讨，但很少能提供探索某个想法所需的全部内容。深度探索可能是最终确定想法的最佳方法，但也是最耗时的方法。

Lateral Exploration

侧向探查

Information doesn’t stand alone. What formulas are similar to this one in function or design? What other discoveries were made at the same time, by the same person or in the same field? What other facts surround this one?

信息并非孤立存在。有哪些公式在功能或设计上与此公式相似？同一时期、同一人或同一领域还有哪些其他发现？还有哪些事实与此相关？

50

Lateral exploration requires that you create links around information. Usually this means that you take models and link information between them. Relating one event that occurred in Ancient Greece with another event that took place in Ancient China.

横向探索要求你围绕信息建立联系。通常这意味着你要选取模型，并将它们之间的信息联系起来。例如，将古希腊发生的某个事件与古代中国发生的某个事件联系起来。

Lateral exploration requires less research than depth exploration, but more creativity. It requires that you see connections that might not be present initially.

横向探索需要的研究比深度探索少，但需要更多的创造力。它要求你看到最初可能并不存在的联系。

Your professors might not show you all the possible similarities and comparisons one formula has to another.

你的教授可能不会向你展示一个公式与另一个公式之间所有可能的相似之处和比较之处。

Vertical Exploration

垂直勘探

Information follows patterns, those patterns can be found in other information.

信息遵循一定的模式，而这些模式可以在其他信息中找到。

Can I compare this formula to a natural event, like water flowing or driving a car? How does this discovery relate to a completely different historical event? How is this idea similar to completely different ideas.

我能否将这个公式比作自然现象，比如水流或汽车行驶？这项发现与完全不同的历史事件有何关联？这个想法与完全不同的想法又有何相似之处？

Vertical exploration is the most difficult, but also the most creative way to learn.

垂直探索是最困难的，但也是最具创造性的学习方式。

But, if used properly, it can be done with greater speed than the background research required in depth exploration. Vertical exploration is the biggest subject of the techniques in this book as methods such as metaphor and visceralization work well within vertical exploration.

但是，如果运用得当，垂直探索的速度可以比深度探索所需的背景研究更快。本书所探讨的技巧中，垂直探索占据了最重要的位置，因为诸如隐喻和内省等方法在垂直探索中非常有效。

51

Vertical exploration involves building those highways between constructs. This benefits your creative thinking and can give you amazing powers to understand information.

# ↩

垂直探索指的是构建连接不同建筑的通道。这有助于培养你的创造性思维，并赋予你惊人的信息理解能力。

All of these three methods are equally valid. The techniques in this book can apply to any of the different types of exploration. The key is to practice and recognize what type of linking you are trying to create. Are you trying to build a foundation beneath an idea? Link an idea around similar ideas? Or create highways that bridge your idea and completely different ones?

这三种方法都同样有效。本书中的技巧可以应用于任何类型的探索。关键在于练习并认识到你想要建立的是哪种类型的联系。你是想为某个想法奠定基础？将一个想法与相似的想法联系起来？还是想创建连接你的想法和完全不同想法的桥梁？

Quick Tip!

小贴士！

Creating diagrams can help with vertical, lateral and depth exploration. Metaphor and visceralization both work best with vertical exploration. However, holistic learning doesn't need to be fancy, just by getting curious and asking questions you can explore an idea.

绘制图表有助于进行纵向、横向和深度探索。隐喻和直观化手法在纵向探索中效果最佳。然而，整体学习并不需要多么复杂，只需保持好奇心并提出问题，你就能探索一个想法。

52

53

The Debug Phase

调试阶段

Learning is not error free. The problem with interlinking, is that a wrong connection can create false understandings. This happens when you believe you understand an idea, but the relationship it is based on is faulty.

学习并非一帆风顺。关联性的问题在于，错误的关联会导致错误的理解。这种情况发生在你自认为理解了某个概念，但你理解它所依据的关联本身就是错误的。

Let’s say you create a link between how corporations improve with the process of evolution. This may be a useful metaphor, but it might lack accuracy. Natural selection takes place over thousands of generations with relatively low error rates when replicating. Corporations can change completely over just a few generations with incredibly high error rates. Unless you understand places the metaphor doesn’t apply, you might make reasoning errors.1

假设你将公司发展与进化过程联系起来。这或许是一个有用的比喻，但可能不够准确。自然选择需要数千代的时间才能完成，而且在复制过程中出错率相对较低。而公司却可以在短短几代之内发生翻天覆地的变化，而且出错率极高。除非你了解这个比喻不适用的情况，否则你可能会犯推理错误。¹

Debugging can be seen as pruning back the holistic web. Adding exceptions and breaking connection that don’t exist in reality. This isn’t a perfect process, but it is necessary to seek information that will clean up the desire to find patterns.

调试可以看作是对整个网络进行精简，添加一些实际上并不存在的异常并断开一些连接。这并非一个完美的过程，但对于寻求能够消除寻找模式的欲望的信息而言，却是必要的。

Debugging can take many forms, from reading books from authors that oppose your points of view (and can point out errors in your reasoning) to testing your information 1. Eliezer Yudkowsky, “No Evolutions for Corporations or Nanodevices”

调试可以采取多种形式，从阅读与你观点相左的作者的书籍（这些作者可以指出你推理中的错误）到测试你的信息。1. Eliezer Yudkowsky，“No Evolutions for Corporations or Nanodevices”（公司或纳米设备没有进化）

http://www.overcomingbias.com/2007/11/no-evolution-fo.html

http://www.overcomingbias.com/2007/11/no-evolution-fo.html

54

in the world and seeing where it doesn’t apply.

在世界上，看看它不适用于哪些情况。

I mentioned earlier in the book how I understood what a subspace was by using a model which combined a 3-D background and red grid. Unfortunately, this is only one form of a subspace. There are many others and the grid analogy might lead to incorrect conclusions. Debugging would help me fix this glitch.

我在本书前面提到过，我是如何通过一个结合了三维背景和红色网格的模型来理解子空间的。遗憾的是，这只是子空间的一种形式。子空间还有很多其他形式，而网格类比可能会导致错误的结论。调试可以帮助我修复这个错误。

Quick Tip!

小贴士！

The only way to debug is to practice. You can cut down on practicing time if you form a solid foundation in the first three steps. For more suggestions on debugging, read the section on Model Debugging.

调试的唯一方法就是练习。如果你在前三个步骤中打下了坚实的基础，就可以减少练习时间。有关调试的更多建议，请阅读“模型调试”部分。

55

56

The Apply Phase

应用阶段

Application is where learning becomes complete. Being able to apply information makes it more likely to match the real world. You would learn tax law better if you had to apply it to your own business than just hypothetical examples. You would understand statistics better if you designed your own experiments.

应用是学习的最终体现。能够运用知识，才能使其更贴近现实世界。比起仅仅学习假设案例，将税法应用于自身业务会更有助于你理解税法。设计自己的实验也能让你更好地理解统计学。

Little information will actually get to reach this phase. But the more you can carry to this final stage, the more you will completely understand. Application is part practice and part creativity as you take theories and force them onto the real world.

实际上，只有极少的信息能够真正到达这个阶段。但是，你能带到这个最终阶段的信息越多，你对理论的理解就越透彻。应用既包含实践，也包含创造力，你需要将理论应用于现实世界。

A certain amount of all information is subconscious. That subconscious portion might not be developed if you fail to apply. Someone who has read a library of business books may understand concepts, but someone who has run a business can feel them.

一部分信息是潜意识的。如果你不去实践，这部分潜意识信息就可能无法发展。读过大量商业书籍的人或许能理解一些概念，但只有真正经营过企业的人才能切身感受到它们。

Finding creative ways you can apply what you learn to your own life is the final step of holistic learning.

找到创造性的方法，将所学知识应用到自己的生活中，是全面学习的最后一步。

57

58

The Test Phase

测试阶段

Each one of these five phases needs to be accompanied by testing. As you go through the techniques in the latter half of this e-book, you will be trying out ways of learning that might dramatically differ from your current methods. Whenever you try new methods, information might get lost or absorbed differently. Testing allows you to track what your weaknesses are, so improvements can be made.

这五个阶段中的每一个都需要进行测试。在学习本书后半部分介绍的技巧时，你会尝试一些与你目前学习方法截然不同的方法。每当你尝试新方法时，信息的丢失或吸收方式都可能有所不同。测试可以帮助你追踪自身的不足之处，从而进行改进。

Testing should determine what level of understanding you have for any idea.

测试应该能够确定你对任何概念的理解程度。

Here’s the questions you need to ask yourself:

你需要问自己以下问题：

Acquire Test - Have I seen/listened to the idea before?

获取测试 - 我以前见过/听过这个想法吗？

Understand Test - Do I get (at a surface level) what this idea means?

理解测试 - 我是否（从表面上）理解了这个概念的含义？

Explore Test - Do I understand where this idea comes from, what it is related to and what outside ideas can be connected with it?

探索测试 - 我是否理解这个想法的来源、它与什么相关以及可以与哪些外部想法联系起来？

Debug Test - Have I removed inappropriate links between this idea and others?

调试测试 - 我是否已删除此想法与其他想法之间不恰当的链接？

Have I removed false conclusions based on connections that don’t actually exist?

我是否已删除基于并不存在的联系而得出的错误结论？

Apply Test - Have I used this idea in my practical life?

应用测试——我是否在实际生活中运用过这个理念？

59

Answering “no” to any of these points should give a clear idea of what level your understanding is with this particular idea. You might have heard the information, understood it at a basic level and connected it with other ideas – but failed to search through and delete false connections. Therefore your current level of understanding is just beyond exploration.

如果对以上任何一点回答“否”，就能清楚地了解你对这个特定概念的理解程度。你可能听说过相关信息，也基本理解了它，并将其与其他概念联系起来——但你却没有仔细甄别并剔除错误的关联。因此，你目前的理解水平还不足以进行深入探索。

Testing isn’t a complicated process, but it requires a lot of self-awareness. Read over the description of the five phases again as you go through the techniques. That way you can better understand where you sit with any new idea you encounter.

测试过程并不复杂，但需要很强的自我认知能力。在学习这些技巧的过程中，请再次阅读五个阶段的描述。这样，你就能更好地了解自己对任何新想法的理解程度。

60

Summary of Holistic

整体性总结

Learning Sequence

学习顺序

All of this talk about holistic learning theory may sound a bit overwhelming. Just how am I supposed to vertically explore, create models or build constructs? At this point you may want to flip to Part II of the book. That section covers the techniques which are built on this theory.

所有这些关于整体学习理论的讨论可能听起来有点让人不知所措。我究竟该如何进行纵向探索、创建模型或构建概念呢？此时，您不妨翻到本书的第二部分。该部分详细介绍了基于此理论的各种方法。

The sequence of holistic learning isn’t really a sequence at all. Instead it is a cycle that constantly jumps between steps. Understanding information goes back to Acquiring and then onto Exploration and Application before Debugging. Try to avoid seeing these steps as linear but as part of an ongoing cycle to create understandings.

整体学习的顺序并非真正意义上的顺序，而是一个不断循环往复的过程。理解信息需要先经历获取阶段，然后是探索和应用，最后才是调试阶段。尽量避免将这些步骤视为线性过程，而应将其视为一个持续循环的一部分，以逐步构建理解。

61

Pinpointing Weaknesses

找出弱点

in the Sequence

在序列中

What are your weak links in the chain of holistic

您在整体性链条中的薄弱环节是什么？

learning? Identifying weak points is a matter of regular testing. More broadly, you need to pinpoint where your chronic weaknesses are. Everyone has different strengths and weaknesses when it comes to learning. Perhaps you are great at acquiring and understanding but poor at exploring. Or perhaps you can connect ideas easily, but make too many false connections.

学习？找出弱点需要定期测试。更广泛地说，你需要精准定位你的长期弱点。每个人在学习方面都有不同的优势和劣势。也许你擅长获取和理解，但不太擅长探索。又或许你能轻松地将各种想法联系起来，但却常常建立太多错误的联系。

Finding your chronic weak points can tell you what techniques you need to master.

找到你的长期弱点可以告诉你需要掌握哪些技巧。

I can’t tell you what your weaknesses are. There are no concrete rules.

我无法告诉你你的弱点是什么。这方面没有硬性规定。

62

But here are a few guidelines you can use to see what you might need to work on: If Your Weakness is...

但以下几条指导原则可以帮助你了解自己可能需要在哪些方面努力：如果你的弱点是……

...Acquiring

……收购

Poor acquisition tends to manifest itself in one of two ways: 1) Reading or listening takes you a long time.

学习能力差往往表现为以下两种情况之一：1）阅读或聆听需要很长时间。

2) You need to re-read textbooks/notes to get all of the basic information.

2）你需要重新阅读教科书/笔记，以获取所有基本信息。

Some common problems that can result in poor acquiring are: 1) You have bad reading/study habits. If you’re constantly reading when distracted, or don’t follow reading techniques I describe in Part II of this book, you’re going to take much longer to read or require multiple reads of the same material.

导致学习效率低下的常见问题包括：1）阅读/学习习惯不良。如果你经常在分心的情况下阅读，或者没有遵循本书第二部分中描述的阅读技巧，那么你阅读同一份材料所需的时间将会大大延长，甚至需要反复阅读。

2) You have bad note taking habits. This can be through taking too many notes or taking too few. Too many notes prevents you from thinking while the professor talks.

2）你的笔记习惯不好。这可能是记笔记太多或记得太少。记笔记太多会让你在教授讲课时无法思考。

63

Too few/poor quality notes might prevent recapturing information not properly understood the first time.

笔记太少或质量太差可能会妨碍重新理解第一次没有正确理解的信息。

3) You don’t understand the basic terminology or the English language. If English isn’t your first language (or whatever language you’re studying in) you will make errors in interpretation. If you lack the basic terminology of your field, you may get confused.

3）你不了解基本术语或英语。如果英语不是你的母语（或者你正在学习的语言），你会在理解上出错。如果你缺乏本领域的基本术语，你可能会感到困惑。

The solution to poor acquisition is to improve your study, reading and note taking habits. I have suggestions in Part II for how to do this. Acquiring isn’t the most important phase of learning, so I wouldn’t worry if you aren’t perfect.

提高知识掌握能力的关键在于改善学习、阅读和笔记习惯。我在第二部分会给出一些建议。知识掌握并非学习过程中最重要的阶段，所以即使你做得不够完美也不用担心。

...Understanding

...理解

Poor understanding tends to be shown when:

理解能力不足通常表现为：

1) You’re reading but have no idea what the author is talking about.

1）你正在阅读，但完全不知道作者在说什么。

2) Your notes (which are perfectly legible) don’t make any sense to you.

2）你的笔记（字迹清晰可辨）对你来说毫无意义。

64

Getting to the surface understanding can’t be done through magic. My suggestion, if this is your stumbling block, is to seek as many well-written explanations as possible.

要真正理解问题的核心，靠魔法是行不通的。如果你正为此苦恼，我的建议是尽可能多地寻找条理清晰、解释详尽的资料。

Advanced techniques such as metaphor or visceralization can only work if the foundation of understanding is already there.

只有在理解的基础已经存在的情况下，隐喻或内脏化等高级技巧才能发挥作用。

Even if you feel you can’t understand your subjects, I’ve found that this is rarely the main problem. Usually most people can understand the basics of an idea. It is the cross application and linking required to remember ideas that most people stumble on.

即使你觉得自己无法理解所学内容，我发现这通常并非主要问题所在。大多数人通常都能理解一个概念的基本要点。真正让他们感到困惑的是，如何将不同概念相互关联、融会贯通，从而记住它们。

When you don’t understand, slow down and ask for different explanations. Often I’m struck by a new idea for awhile before I can fully understand it. The power I’ve made is being able to take the understanding, once formed, and rapidly grow that idea so that I can use it easily.

当你遇到不理解的事情时，放慢速度，寻求不同的解释。很多时候，我需要一段时间才能完全理解一个新想法。我所掌握的技能在于，一旦理解形成，就能迅速发展壮大这个想法，从而轻松运用它。

...Exploration

...勘探

Poor exploration is shown by inflexibility. It happens when you get the gist of an idea, but can’t relate it to other things you have learned. If you are asked to use the idea to solve a non-routine problem, you’re screwed.

探索能力差的表现是缺乏灵活性。这种情况发生在你理解了一个想法的大概意思，却无法将其与你已学过的其他知识联系起来的时候。如果让你用这个想法解决一个非常规问题，你就完蛋了。

65

People who can do math problems but can’t do word problems using the same techniques usually have a weakness in exploring. They understand how they’ve been taught to use the formula and the steps to solve the problem, but can’t apply it in a different setting.

那些能做数学题却无法用相同技巧解决应用题的人，通常缺乏探索能力。他们理解所学的公式和解题步骤，但却无法将其应用到不同的情境中。

Not being able to apply ideas to different problems is a weakness in the Explore Phase, not Apply Phase. I’ll make the distinction clearer by using an example: Suppose Johnny is in a basic statistics course. He understands the basics of the formulas and remembers the examples his professor gave when solving mathematical problems.

无法将想法应用于不同的问题是探索阶段的弱点，而不是应用阶段的弱点。我举个例子来更清楚地说明这一点：假设约翰尼正在学习基础统计学课程。他理解公式的基本原理，并且记得教授在解决数学问题时举的例子。

Now Johnny is given a problem on the test which requires him to use the formula in a slightly different way than he was taught. He can’t do it – the problem is in exploration.

现在，约翰尼在考试中遇到了一道题，这道题要求他用一种与之前学过的略有不同的方法来运用公式。他做不出来——问题出在探索上。

However, if Johnny breezed through the test, chances are his exploration is strong.

然而，如果约翰尼轻松通过了测试，那么他的探索能力很可能很强。

But, let’s say, he is later confronted with a problem with a statistics problem in his life.

但是，假设他后来在生活中遇到了一个统计学方面的问题。

Will he make use of the principles he learned during the course and apply them? Or will they not be able to make the jump from classroom to real-life? If he can’t – that’s a problem in application.

他能否运用课堂上学到的原理并加以实践？还是无法将课堂知识转化为实际应用？如果不能，那就是应用方面的问题。

66

...Debugging

...调试

Poor debugging is shown by inaccurate connections. I find this is less common in the classroom, and more common in the outside world. In classes, most people do too little exploration. As a result, there is little that needs debugging, if anything.

调试不力会导致连接不准确。我发现这种情况在课堂上不太常见，而在实际应用中则更为普遍。在课堂上，大多数人很少进行探索。因此，即使需要调试，也很少出现问题。

In the outside world, superstitions aren’t just the domain of religion and rituals.

在现实世界中，迷信并不只是宗教和仪式的专属领域。

People have all sorts of wacky associations they’ve made but failed to test. Believing cheering causes a sports team to win just because cheering matches up with winning is a good example.

人们常常会建立各种各样稀奇古怪的联系，但却从未经过验证。比如，有人认为欢呼能让运动队赢球，仅仅因为欢呼和胜利联系在一起，就是一个很好的例子。

A sign you don’t do enough debugging is if you don’t regularly find yourself to be wrong on a major belief or issue. If you always think you are correct, chances are you aren’t doing enough critical examination of the connections you make.

如果你很少发现自己在某个重要信念或问题上犯错，那就说明你调试得不够。如果你总是认为自己是对的，那么很可能你没有对你所建立的各种联系进行足够的批判性审视。

...Applying

……应用

As I mentioned with weaknesses in exploring, applying errors are caused when you can’t act on ideas in the real world. Having brilliant theories is useless if you can’t use them anywhere. Schools, in my opinion, fail to look at this critical aspect of learning.

正如我之前提到的探索能力不足，应用错误则源于无法将想法付诸实践。拥有再精妙的理论，如果无法应用于任何领域，也毫无用处。在我看来，学校往往忽视了学习中这一至关重要的方面。

67

People who have “book smarts” but lack common sense are usually people who fail at applying. Solving this phase is less technique and more practice. Get out there, run controlled experiments and give your ideas a test.

那些书本知识丰富但缺乏常识的人，通常在实践中会失败。解决这个问题与其说是技巧问题，不如说是实践问题。走出舒适区，开展对照实验，检验你的想法。

Identifying Your Weak Points

找出你的弱点

Shouldn’t you focus on your strengths and ignore your weaknesses? Normally I’d agree with you, but this is an area where each step is crucial and can’t be outsourced. If you’re running a business, being the best programmer in the world isn’t necessary if you can hire a programmer. As a learner, however, you can’t hire someone to explore or apply ideas. You have only one brain, so you need to focus on fixing weak points in the sequence.

难道不应该专注于发挥自身优势而忽略劣势吗？通常我会同意你的观点，但在这个领域，每一步都至关重要，而且无法外包。如果你经营一家公司，只要能雇佣程序员，就没必要成为世界上最好的程序员。然而，作为一名学习者，你无法雇佣别人来帮你探索或应用想法。你只有一个大脑，所以你需要专注于弥补学习过程中的薄弱环节。

Once you recognize weak points, you can practice techniques to strengthen them.

一旦发现自身的弱点，就可以练习一些技巧来加强它们。

Initially, adopting new techniques adds a bit of time. But as you master them, they become integrated into your natural strategy for learning.

起初，采用新技术会花费一些时间。但随着你逐渐掌握它们，它们就会融入你自然的学习策略中。

68

Information Structure

信息结构

The process of learning is similar for most subjects. Whether it’s chemistry, history or computer programming, you’ll still go through the stages of acquiring, understanding, exploring, debugging and finally applying.

大多数学科的学习过程都大同小异。无论是化学、历史还是计算机编程，你都会经历获取知识、理解概念、探索知识、调试知识以及最终应用知识这几个阶段。

The problem is that all information isn’t the same. You might need to remember a list of dates for a history class, and need to know how polymorphism works in a computer science class. The information in each case has a different structure.

问题在于，并非所有信息都相同。你可能需要记住历史课上的一系列日期，也可能需要了解计算机科学课上的多态性原理。这两种情况下的信息结构都不同。

Although the process for learning is similar, it is important to take into account the structure of information.

虽然学习过程类似，但必须考虑到信息的结构。

If you eat a hamburger or a bowl of alfalfa sprouts, the process is the same. You chew the food, it is broken down in your stomach, nutrients are absorbed in your intestines and it leaves the body as waste. However a hamburger and bowl of alfalfa sprouts have very different structures. As a result you must chew, digest and absorb them in different ways to get the nutrients and remove the waste.

无论是吃汉堡还是吃一碗苜蓿芽，过程都是一样的。你咀嚼食物，食物在胃里被分解，营养物质在肠道中被吸收，最后以废物的形式排出体外。然而，汉堡和苜蓿芽的结构截然不同。因此，你需要用不同的方式咀嚼、消化和吸收它们，才能获取营养并排出废物。

You can’t digest information with different structures the same way. Learning must 69

你无法用相同的方式消化结构不同的信息。学习必须…… 69

adjust for the difference between knowing the definition of a hundred terms versus being able to argue a thesis statement.

要考虑到了解一百个术语的定义与能够论证一个论点之间的差异。

Coming up with a solution for every type of information structure is impossible.

为每一种信息结构都找到解决方案是不可能的。

You’ll have to tweak the methods in the second half of this book towards whatever information structures you encounter. But I’ve come up with a few simple categories that can help you decide what structure your learning tasks fit in: 1. Arbitrary

你需要根据遇到的具体信息结构，对本书后半部分的方法进行调整。但我总结了一些简单的分类，可以帮助你判断学习任务属于哪种结构：1. 任意结构

2. Opinion

2. 意见

3. Process

3. 流程

4. Concrete

4. 混凝土

5. Abstract

5. 摘要

These five categories define the basic information structures I’ve noticed in most school and real-life settings. Some information sits in-between categories: physics can often move between concrete and abstract. Biology can go between arbitrary and concrete. In fact, most topics have elements of each structure.

这五大类信息结构是我在大多数学校和现实生活中观察到的基本信息结构。有些信息介于这些类别之间：物理学常常在具体和抽象之间转换，生物学则介于任意和具体之间。事实上，大多数主题都包含每种结构的元素。

70

71

Arbitrary Information

任意信息

Arbitrary information is a set of facts, dates, definitions or rules that have no logical grouping. This type of information is often encountered in schools and less frequently in the real world. I’ve heard from many new medical students complain about the amount of definitions they need to memorize in anatomy class.

任意信息是指一组缺乏逻辑关联的事实、日期、定义或规则。这类信息在学校里比较常见，但在现实世界中则较少见。我曾听很多医学新生抱怨解剖课上需要记忆的定义太多。

Methods to Use With Arbitrary Information

处理任意信息的方法

Your first goal with arbitrary information is to make it less arbitrary. If there is a logical pattern in the information, try to find that first. Otherwise the job of remembering and using the information becomes more difficult.

处理任意信息时，首要目标是使其不再那么随意。如果信息中存在逻辑模式，首先要找到它。否则，记忆和使用信息就会变得更加困难。

If that can’t be accomplished, these methods also work well: Linking

如果无法实现上述目标，以下方法也同样有效：链接

Pegging

钉子

Compression

压缩

72

Challenges with Arbitrary Information

任意信息带来的挑战

The one benefit of arbitrary information is that it is relatively easy to understand.

任意信息的一个好处是它相对容易理解。

Knowing how a heart pumps blood requires far more intelligence than simply remembering what the different parts of a heart are called.

了解心脏如何泵血需要的智力远比记住心脏各个部分的名称要高得多。

But this upside is also a curse. Since there is little understanding required, there is also little exploration that can be done. Therefore, this type of information is the most likely to be forgotten without sheer rote memorization. Linking, pegging and compression can help, but they can’t entirely compensate for the tricky nature of this structure.

但这种优势也带来了弊端。由于对理解的要求不高，因此也几乎没有探索的空间。所以，这类信息如果不死记硬背，最容易被遗忘。链接、关联和压缩或许有所帮助，但它们无法完全弥补这种结构本身的复杂性。

Quick Tip!

小贴士！

Arbitrary information is the hardest to learn holistically. If you need to remember a lot of arbitrary information for your classes, the Link, Peg and Information Compression methods can help make the process easier.

任意信息最难全面掌握。如果你需要记住大量课堂上涉及的任意信息，链接法、挂钩法和信息压缩法可以帮助你简化记忆过程。

73

74

Opinion Information

观点信息

Opinion information is information you need to argue. Arguing whether Theravada Buddhism is superior to Mahayana Buddhism would require learning opinion information. This type of information is common in essays and presentations in school.

观点信息是指用于论证的信息。例如，论证上座部佛教是否优于大乘佛教就需要学习观点信息。这类信息在学校的论文和演讲中很常见。

This type of information is also important when making decisions where there isn’t a consensus (what foods are healthy, what business opportunities are good, etc.).

在做出没有共识的决定时（例如哪些食物健康，哪些商业机会好等等），这类信息也很重要。

Challenges With Opinion Information

意见信息面临的挑战

With opinion information, your biggest problem is the acquiring phase. You need to examine a large volume of information and look for patterns, rather than memorize specific details. Speed reading techniques are a great asset in gathering information.

对于观点信息，你最大的挑战在于信息获取阶段。你需要审视大量信息并寻找规律，而不是死记硬背具体细节。快速阅读技巧是收集信息的一大利器。

Diagraming is also a useful method with opinion information. It can help you distill your key ideas after reading.

绘制图表也是整理观点信息的一种有效方法。它可以帮助你在阅读后提炼出关键思想。

75

76

Process Information

流程信息

Process information is information you need to act upon. Writing a computer program, building a house and designing a prototype are all based on process information. Practice is the most important element to learning any idea you need to act upon repeatedly, but creating the right background concepts is also crucial for saving time.

流程信息是指你需要采取行动的信息。编写计算机程序、建造房屋和设计原型都基于流程信息。练习是学习任何需要反复实践的概念的最重要因素，但建立正确的背景概念对于节省时间也至关重要。

Methods to Use With Process Information

与过程信息一起使用的方法

Most process information relies on having the right models. While a construct can be formed slowly with practice, having the right models can speed up learning. Here are some techniques to improve your models:

大多数流程信息都依赖于合适的模型。虽然概念可以通过练习慢慢形成，但拥有合适的模型可以加快学习速度。以下是一些改进模型的技巧：

Visceralization

内脏化

Metaphor

隐喻

Diagraming

图表绘制

Model Debugging

模型调试

77

Challenges With Process Information

流程信息方面的挑战

The biggest challenge with process information is that you need to actually put in the practice time. It doesn’t matter how well you understand the concepts, until you physically perform the actions, you won’t fully learn the subject material. Get the right background models and then practice the methods you’ve been taught.

流程信息最大的挑战在于你需要投入实际练习的时间。无论你对概念理解得多么透彻，只有亲身实践，才能真正掌握相关知识。找到合适的背景模型，然后练习你所学的方法。

The benefit of process information is that, if you do practice, it tends to stick with you much longer than almost any other form of information. Practice fuses the models with your construct.

过程信息的优势在于，如果你进行练习，它比几乎任何其他形式的信息都更容易被记住。练习能将模型与你的认知结构融合起来。

78

79

Concrete Information

具体信息

The next two categories of information, concrete and abstract, deal with the majority of information you learn in a school setting. Concrete information deals with ideas you can interact with tangibly. Most information sits on a spectrum between abstract and concrete, the difference can often be based more on the way it is presented than the content itself.

接下来要介绍的两类信息，具体信息和抽象信息，涵盖了你在学校环境中学习的大部分信息。具体信息指的是你可以实际操作的概念。大多数信息介于抽象和具体之间，二者的区别往往更多地体现在信息的呈现方式上，而非内容本身。

For example, biology can be a concrete subject because you have physical diagrams that represent the information. You don’t need to do much work visualizing these ideas because artists and nature have done the job for you. But it can also be an abstract subject when trying to imagine enzymes, neurons or chemical reactions.

例如，生物学可以是一门具体的学科，因为有图示来呈现信息。你不需要花费太多精力去想象这些概念，因为艺术家和大自然已经为你完成了这项工作。但当你试图想象酶、神经元或化学反应时，它也可以是一门抽象的学科。

Methods to Use With Concrete Information

与具体信息一起使用的方法

Most of the techniques listed in the second half of the book will work well with concrete information. Visceralization can be helpful if you want to put information into more than one of your senses. For example, you may see a diagram of a heart pumping blood, but could then translate this picture into a feeling or sound.

本书后半部分列出的大多数技巧都适用于具体信息。如果你想将信息调动到多种感官上，内脏化法会很有帮助。例如，你可能看到一张心脏泵血的示意图，但你可以将这幅图转化为一种感觉或声音。

80

81

Abstract Information

摘要信息

Abstract information is like concrete information, but it lacks the obvious connection with the senses. Mathematics, physics, psychology, computer science and chemistry are all fields that rely heavily on abstract information. Quantum physics or calculus all depend on abstract models that may not be easy to picture immediately.

抽象信息与具体信息类似，但它缺乏与感官的直接联系。数学、物理学、心理学、计算机科学和化学等领域都高度依赖抽象信息。量子物理学或微积分都依赖于抽象模型，而这些模型可能不容易立即被形象化。

Abstract information is the complete opposite of arbitrary information. Very difficult to understand but the pattern is highly logical. While arbitrary information may be incredibly shallow, abstract information can seem like diving to the bottom of an ocean.

抽象信息与任意信息截然相反。它虽然难以理解，但其模式却高度合乎逻辑。任意信息可能浅薄无比，而抽象信息则如同潜入深海一般，令人叹为观止。

Methods to Use With Abstract Information

与抽象信息一起使用的方法

When dealing with abstract information, you need to move it to a concrete level.

处理抽象信息时，需要将其转化为具体信息。

Holistic learners usually excel in classes with arbitrary information. This is because they can understand the subject well in advance of other students who can never seem to wrap their heads around the complex ideas.

全面型学习者通常在信息繁杂的课堂上表现出色。这是因为他们能够比其他学生更早地理解主题，而其他学生似乎永远也无法理解其中复杂的概念。

82

Visceralization and metaphor are essential to bring complex ideas down to a basic level. Model debugging plays prominent role because your initial attempts to model an idea may have unintended errors.

形象化和隐喻对于将复杂概念简化到基本层面至关重要。模型调试发挥着重要作用，因为你最初尝试对某个概念进行建模时可能会出现意想不到的错误。

Challenges With Abstract Information

抽象信息面临的挑战

The understanding and exploring phases here can be brutal. If you feel that you don’t understand a subject, slow the information stream down slightly and begin exploring the information you’ve been given. Since most of these courses tend to pile one idea on top of another, setting the right foundation is critical.

理解和探索阶段可能会非常艰难。如果你觉得自己对某个主题不理解，不妨放慢信息流的速度，开始深入探究已有的知识。由于大多数课程都倾向于将一个概念层层叠加，因此打好基础至关重要。

Quick Tip!

小贴士！

Abstract information is an area where holistic learning can excel over other methods. By converting information into a format that is easier to imagine, you are more likely to form links surrounding that idea. Visceralization and metaphor are both great ways to do this.

抽象信息是整体学习法优于其他方法的一个领域。通过将信息转化为更容易想象的形式，你更有可能围绕该概念建立联系。具象化和隐喻都是实现这一目标的绝佳方法。

83

How to Use the Five

如何使用五

Information Categories

信息类别

When you need to learn a new topic, decide what major category or categories your information fits within. Deciding which category you need to learn can help you determine what techniques to use when learning and what obstacles you might face in remembering.

当你需要学习一个新主题时，首先要确定该信息属于哪个或哪些主要类别。明确学习类别有助于你确定学习方法，以及记忆过程中可能遇到的障碍。

Weak and Strong Structures

弱结构和强结构

A bridge made out of straw isn’t a strong structure. A bridge with steel and careful engineering can be incredibly strong. Information structures can also be weak or 84

用稻草做的桥并不坚固。用钢材和精心设计的桥梁可以非常坚固。信息结构也可能很脆弱或脆弱。

strong. You should always try to use strong structures when possible.

强。你应该尽可能使用强结构。

An arbitrary structure is the weakest structure for information. It is the hardest to learn holistically, takes the longest to learn effectively and has little value outside its specific application. If possible, try to find patterns that make arbitrary information more logical. This will help in remembering.

任意结构是信息最薄弱的结构。它最难整体掌握，需要最长时间才能有效学习，而且在特定应用之外几乎没有价值。如果可能，尝试寻找能使任意信息更具逻辑性的模式。这将有助于记忆。

For example, if you have a list of definitions you need to memorize, go beyond the list. Even if the textbook offers no logical pattern, try to look for one. Maybe certain groups share a common Latin root word? Only if you can’t link together logically should you try using arbitrary linking techniques such as Pegging or Compression.

例如，如果你需要记忆一系列定义，不要局限于列表本身。即使教科书没有提供任何逻辑规律，也要尝试寻找其中的关联。也许某些词组共享一个共同的拉丁词根？只有当你无法通过逻辑推理将它们联系起来时，才应该尝试使用诸如词缀关联或词缀压缩之类的任意关联技巧。

Concrete and process structures are the strongest structures of information. Both of them create tangible experiences that help you link any new ideas through your senses.

具体结构和过程结构是信息最强有力的结构。它们都能创造切实的体验，帮助你通过感官将任何新想法联系起来。

Creating a computer program combines concrete and process information structures.

计算机程序的创建结合了具体信息结构和过程信息结构。

Because you can get immediate feedback through your senses about the effect of any changes, concepts quickly get wired into your brain.

因为可以通过感官立即获得关于任何变化效果的反馈，所以概念会很快铭刻在你的大脑中。

You can convert a weaker structure of information into a stronger form by practicing many of the methods later in the book.

你可以通过练习本书后面介绍的许多方法，将较弱的信息结构转化为较强的形式。

85

Why Your Classes are

为什么你的课程是

Boring

无聊的

Why do you find some topics fascinating and others boring? You probably are keenly aware of which subjects interest you and which don’t. But do you know why?

为什么你觉得有些话题引人入胜，而有些话题却枯燥乏味？你可能很清楚自己对哪些话题感兴趣，哪些不感兴趣。但你知道为什么吗？

There are many possible reasons why you might enjoy literature over physics or computer science over accounting. You might have a natural aptitude for one subject over another. You might be able to use one subject in your daily life. One subject may even have a more interesting teacher, who can connect the abstract ideas to something you're passionate about.

你或许会因为很多原因更喜欢文学而不是物理，或者更喜欢计算机科学而不是会计。你可能天生就对某个学科更有天赋。你可能能在日常生活中运用到某个学科的知识。甚至某个学科的老师可能更有趣，能够将抽象的概念与你感兴趣的事物联系起来。

The question is, are you in control over which subjects you like and dislike? Can you make a boring class more interesting? If you take control over how you learn, I’ve found you can electrify almost any subject.

问题是，你能掌控自己喜欢和不喜欢的科目吗？你能让枯燥的课堂变得更有趣吗？我发现，如果你能掌控自己的学习方式，几乎任何科目都能变得生动有趣。

Holistic learning and your interest in a class are tightly linked. The more 86

整体学习与你对课程的兴趣密切相关。86

interesting you find the class, the easier it is to learn holistically. Do you find it easy to relate your favorite subjects, but hard to relate to boring subjects? This relationship works both ways. You can make a boring class interesting by learning more holistically.

你觉得课程越有趣，就越容易进行整体学习。你是否觉得很容易将自己喜欢的科目与学习联系起来，但却很难将枯燥的科目联系起来？这种关系是双向的。你可以通过更全面的学习方法，让枯燥的课程变得有趣。

We all have things we need to learn that initially seem boring. Maybe it’s the statistics course you need to take in order to earn your degree in marketing. Maybe it’s the tax law you need to learn in order to run your business. The people who can brighten these dull topics will make studying easier while learning more.

我们都需要学习一些起初看起来很枯燥的东西。也许是为了获得市场营销学位而必须修读的统计学课程，也许是为了经营企业而必须学习的税法。那些能够把这些枯燥的知识讲得生动有趣的人，会让学习变得更容易，同时也能学到更多。

The next time you “have” to take a boring class, don’t be so quick to blame the class. The problem might just be that you haven’t been taught the subject in a way you can relate to. Using holistic learning methods you can connect to the ideas in a way that interests you.

下次当你“不得不”上一门枯燥的课时，别急着责怪课程本身。问题可能仅仅在于你没有以一种能引起共鸣的方式学习这门课。运用整体学习方法，你可以用自己感兴趣的方式来理解课程内容。

When you think of computer science, do you think of dull lines of text or a secret code of the universe? When you think of accounting, do you see income statements and balance sheets, or a map charting the beating heart of a business? When you learn history do you see dates and facts, or the epic story of millions of people?

提到计算机科学，你想到的是枯燥乏味的文本行，还是宇宙的秘密代码？提到会计，你想到的是损益表和资产负债表，还是描绘企业核心运作的蓝图？提到历史，你想到的是日期和事实，还是数百万人的史诗故事？

One of the best side-effects of holistic learning is that it forces you to look at subjects in a different light. Any set of ideas can be transformed from abstract principles into powerful images and stories that connect with what is most important to you.

整体学习法的一大益处在于，它能迫使你以全新的视角看待事物。任何概念都可以从抽象的原理转化为生动形象、引人入胜的故事，与你最重视的事物产生共鸣。

87

Goals for Learning

学习目标

Up until this point I’ve assumed your goal is to learn information completely enough to pass almost any test in a subject. But just passing tests and getting good grades isn’t enough. Why do you actually want to learn this material? What usefulness can it have in your life?

到目前为止，我一直认为你的目标是掌握足够的知识，以便通过几乎所有相关考试。但仅仅通过考试、取得好成绩是不够的。你学习这些知识的真正目的是什么？它对你的人生有什么用处？

Ironically, people who ask themselves questions like those are more likely to get better grades than the people who just want to pass with an A. Since they have a motivation to go beyond what is necessary to pass, they will understand the information more deeply than students who do not.

具有讽刺意味的是，那些会问自己这类问题的人，比那些只想拿A及格的人更有可能取得更好的成绩。因为他们有超越及格要求的动力，所以他们对知识的理解会比那些没有这种动力的学生更深刻。

When I was starting to learn computer programming, I was fascinated by it. I went far beyond the simple lessons they taught and tried to apply the information to programs I wanted to write. I’ve made several decently-sized computer games as a result of this interest for programming.

我刚开始学习计算机编程时，就被它深深吸引了。我不仅学习了老师教的那些简单的课程，还尝试将所学知识应用到我想编写的程序中。正是这份对编程的热爱，让我制作了几款规模不小的电脑游戏。

When I went through an accounting class, I immediately saw ways I could apply the principles to organize my own small business. Although these methods weren’t 88

当我学习会计课程时，我立刻意识到可以运用这些原则来管理我自己的小企业。虽然这些方法并非88

necessary for my small business, applying some of the concepts to my records helped me both in life and in the class.

对于我的小企业来说，这些概念是必不可少的，将它们应用到我的记录中，对我的生活和课堂学习都很有帮助。

When I went through a statistics class, I found the methods for determining significance and conducting tests to be valuable for my own experiments. Now, as I conduct business and personal experiments I use these mathematical principles for getting better information.

在学习统计学课程时，我发现其中关于确定显著性和进行检验的方法对我的实验非常有帮助。现在，我在进行商业和个人实验时，都会运用这些数学原理来获取更准确的信息。

When I went through a class teaching about vector spaces, I saw how the concepts of subspaces and vector spaces could be applied to my philosophy of life. Borrowing the concepts helped clarify ideas I had and gave me excellent metaphors for understanding.

当我学习向量空间课程时，我发现子空间和向量空间的概念可以应用到我的人生哲学中。借鉴这些概念帮助我理清思路，并为我提供了极好的比喻来加深理解。

Why so many examples? Because I want to point out that going beyond your subject doesn’t need to be an issue of passion. Finding ways to use a subject (even if it currently bores you to tears) can give it new meaning.

为什么要举这么多例子？因为我想指出，超越你原本的学科领域并不一定需要出于热爱。找到运用某个学科的方法（即使它现在让你感到无比厌倦）可以赋予它新的意义。

The ultimate step in holistic learning is to take the information you have learned and give it practical value. Almost any subject can have practical value if you choose to look for it. Giving a subject value in your daily life creates a far greater connection within your mental web than any technique I can possibly describe in Part II.

整体学习的最终步骤是将所学知识赋予实际价值。几乎任何学科，只要你用心寻找，都能拥有实际价值。将某个学科的知识融入日常生活，比我在第二部分中描述的任何技巧都能在你的思维网络中建立更牢固的联系。

Does your learning have a purpose? I don’t care much about grades. I strive to do well in my courses, but the difference between a B+ and A+ doesn’t really bother me.

你的学习有意义吗？我不太在意成绩。我努力在课程中取得好成绩，但B+和A+之间的差别对我来说并不重要。

89

What I do care about is having the asset of knowledge. Investing in learning can create tremendous rewards in your life if you actually use the concepts you’re spending so much time learning. Learning without a practical purpose is a waste of your time.

我真正看重的是知识本身的价值。投资学习，如果能将花费大量时间学习的知识真正运用到实践中，就能为你的人生带来巨大的回报。没有实际用途的学习就是在浪费时间。

Quick Tip!

小贴士！

Holistic learning can make your classes more valuable. By linking ideas together, almost any idea can become useful. Try linking some of your course material to other ideas that interest you. Every idea you learn can be used as a building block for self-improvement.

整体学习能让你的课程更有价值。通过将不同的想法联系起来，几乎任何想法都能变得有用。尝试将课程内容与你感兴趣的其他想法联系起来。你学到的每一个想法都可以作为自我提升的基石。

90

◦ Part II ◦

第二部分

Holistic Learning

整体学习

Techniques

技术

Holistic Learning Methods

整体学习方法

So far you’ve learned the holistic learning strategy. This is my strategy for learning new concepts and how I believe learning actually works best. It is based on linking ideas together, using models, building constructs and understanding different types of information. The second half of this book is devoted to specific techniques that work within the holistic learning framework.

到目前为止，你已经学习了整体学习策略。这是我学习新概念的策略，也是我认为最有效的学习方式。它基于将各种想法联系起来，运用模型，构建概念框架，并理解不同类型的信息。本书的后半部分将专门介绍在整体学习框架内行之有效的具体技巧。

A good way of viewing the information of this book would be like playing chess.

理解这本书信息的一个好方法就是像下棋一样。

In order to play chess you first need to know the rules and basic objective of the game.

要想下国际象棋，首先需要了解游戏规则和基本目标。

The first half of this book could be seen as a similar set of rules and objectives when learning.

本书的前半部分可以看作是学习时一套类似的规则和目标。

Once you understand the rules of chess, you then move onwards to specific strategies and plays to win the game. This is like the second half of the book which is devoted to different strategies I’ve found helpful within the rules of holistic learning.1

一旦你理解了国际象棋的规则，接下来就可以学习具体的策略和棋步来赢得比赛。这就像本书的后半部分，专门介绍我在整体学习原则下发现的各种有效策略。

1. Of course, holistic learning doesn’t offer rules as precise as chess. Rather, a set of guidelines that can help.

当然，整体学习并不像国际象棋那样提供精确的规则，而是提供一套可以提供帮助的指导原则。

92

Understanding the framework of holistic learning is the most important step in improving how you learn. Simply having techniques without the framework would make it impossible to adapt to different challenges, just as knowing chess plays without knowing the rules of the game.

理解整体学习框架是提升学习效果最关键的一步。仅仅掌握技巧而缺乏框架，就如同只懂棋却不懂规则一样，无法应对各种挑战。

All of these techniques won’t work for everyone or in every circumstance.

这些方法并非对每个人都有效，也并非在所有情况下都有效。

Therefore it is important to apply the holistic learning theory to isolate where your weaknesses are before deciding which techniques to use. These techniques come from a combination of my research into different learning methods and my own experiments.

因此，在决定采用哪些学习技巧之前，运用整体学习理论来找出自身的薄弱环节至关重要。这些技巧源于我对不同学习方法的研究以及我自身的实验。

Therefore, you might want to modify them to suit your particular learning style.

因此，你可能需要根据自己的学习风格对它们进行修改。
