Acquiring Ideas

获取想法

The first step in learning information is to acquire it. This means actually passing the information from a textbook through your eyes, optic nerve and brain. If you never see the information in the first place, or acquire it too slowly, that will put a stop to any efforts in learning.

学习信息的第一步是获取信息。这意味着要真正地将教科书中的信息通过你的眼睛、视神经和大脑传递出去。如果你一开始就没看到信息，或者获取信息的速度太慢，那么任何学习努力都将付诸东流。

With acquiring information I’ve found two methods helpful, speed reading and flow-based notetaking.

在获取信息的过程中，我发现有两种方法很有帮助：快速阅读和流程式笔记。

95

96

Speed Reading

速读

If you can read faster, you can acquire more information. That’s just common sense. But speed reading is more than just speed. Simply trying to read faster usually results in lost comprehension. But by practicing with different reading techniques and changing how you read, you can read faster with better understanding.

阅读速度越快，获取的信息就越多。这显而易见。但速读不仅仅是速度的问题。单纯追求速度往往会导致理解力下降。但通过练习不同的阅读技巧，改变阅读方式，你就能读得更快，理解得更透彻。

Speed reading could easily be divided up into enough techniques to fill another entire book (and indeed it has: Breakthrough Rapid Reading is one of my favorites).

快速阅读可以很容易地细分为足够多的技巧，足以写成另一本书（事实上也确实有这样的书：《突破性快速阅读》是我最喜欢的书之一）。

But I’m going to focus on three main sub-techniques you might want to try: 1) Using a pointer.

但我将重点介绍你可能想尝试的三种主要子技术：1）使用指针。

2) Practice reading.

2）练习阅读。

3) Active reading.

3）主动阅读。

Using a Pointer

使用指针

Your eye doesn’t actually stay in one place on the page as you read. Instead, it constantly makes tiny movements that slow your reading speed. Using a pointer can 97

阅读时，你的眼睛实际上并不会一直停留在书页上的同一个位置。相反，它会不断地进行细微的移动，这会降低你的阅读速度。使用指示棒可以提高阅读速度。

improve your reading rate simply by

只需以下方法即可提高阅读速度

focusing your eye onto one part of the

将目光集中在某个部分上

page–the part you want to read.

页码——你想阅读的部分。

A pointer has the added benefit of

指针还有一个额外的好处：

allowing you to control your speed by

让你能够控制你的速度

changing the speed you move the

改变你的移动速度

pointer. Speed reading involves more

指针。快速阅读涉及更多

than just reading fast, as sometimes you will want to slow down to carefully examine one section, and skim over another that is less important.

与其快速阅读，不如放慢速度仔细检查某一部分，而略读其他不太重要的部分。

To start using a pointer, grab a book and place your index finger right below the line you want to read. Move it across the line as you read before going to the next line.

要开始使用指示棒，拿起一本书，把食指放在你想读的那一行下方。阅读时，食指沿着这一行移动，然后再移到下一行。

Although some speed reading experts advocate using a pointer everywhere, I tend to only use it for books. Online articles and short sections of print don’t usually benefit from the extra control a pointer offers.

虽然有些速读专家提倡在所有场合都使用指针，但我通常只在阅读书籍时才用。在线文章和短篇印刷文本通常不需要指针提供的额外控制。

Using a pointer will feel uncomfortable for the first two weeks. Until you get into the habit of reading with a pointer it will probably seem slow and awkward. However, once you adapt to using your finger to scroll through the page, it will make sense. The extra control and focus it provides when reading is invaluable to boost your reading rate.

头两周使用指针阅读可能会感觉不太舒服。在养成习惯之前，你可能会觉得阅读速度慢、操作笨拙。但是，一旦你适应了用手指滚动页面，一切就都明白了。阅读时，指针带来的额外控制力和专注力对于提高阅读速度至关重要。

98

Practice Reading

练习阅读

Another aspect of speed reading is practice reading. Practice reading isn’t the same as reading in the same way jogging on the spot isn’t running. When you practice read, you expect to absorb almost none of the material you are reading. The only purpose of practice reading is to train yourself to comprehend at a faster rate.

速读的另一个方面是练习阅读。练习阅读与阅读不同，就像原地慢跑和跑步不一样。练习阅读时，你几乎不指望能吸收任何内容。练习阅读的唯一目的就是训练自己更快地理解文本。

1) You can practice read by getting a book you haven’t read before. Mark a point in the book and set a timer for three minutes. Then read through the book (with your pointer) slightly faster than you can understand all of the material. When the timer goes off, mark the line you finished on.

1）你可以找一本以前没读过的书来练习阅读。在书中标记一个点，然后设定三分钟的计时器。接着，用手指标记，以略快于你理解所有内容的速度阅读这本书。计时器响起后，标记你读完的那一行。

2) Count the number of lines you read and multiply that by the average words per line on the first paragraph and divide by three. This should give you your approximate words per minute (assuming you read for three minutes).

2）数一数你读了多少行，乘以第一段每行的平均字数，再除以三。这样就能算出你每分钟的阅读字数（假设你读了三分钟）。

3) This exercise can test your flexibility with improving your speed of reading.

3）这项练习可以测试你的灵活性，提高你的阅读速度。

Another exercise is directed towards improving your comprehension. Similar to the above exercise, read for three minutes using your pointer. When you are completed, start a paper writing down every major or important idea you read in the 99

另一项练习旨在提高你的理解能力。与上述练习类似，用你的指示棒阅读三分钟。完成后，在一张纸上写下你在99分钟内读到的每一个主要或重要的想法。

last three minutes (without looking back at the book).

最后三分钟（不回头看书）。

Write as many ideas as you can think of that come directly from the book. Next, go through the book again and make a second list of important ideas. Take the number of ideas you correctly wrote down after the three minute session and subtract the ones you remembered incorrectly. Then divide this number by the total meaningful ideas you gathered in your more detailed search.

尽可能多地写下你从书中直接想到的想法。接下来，再次通读全书，列出第二份重要想法清单。用你三分钟后正确记录的想法数量减去你记错的想法数量。然后，将这个数字除以你在更深入的搜索中收集到的有意义的想法总数。

This number represents your comprehension ability at that reading speed for that type of book. By practice reading you can aim to improve your comprehension at various words per minute, giving you greater speed and flexibility with reading.

这个数字代表你以该阅读速度阅读该类型书籍的理解能力。通过练习阅读，你可以尝试提高不同阅读速度下的理解能力，从而提升阅读速度和灵活性。

100

Active Reading

主动阅读

Although I’m grouping active reading under the category of speed reading, it could be described as the opposite of speed reading. Active reading slows down your reading rate while greatly increasing your comprehension ability. Active reading goes beyond simply highlighting your textbook and writing small notes in the margins, but fully integrating ideas as they hit you.

虽然我将主动阅读归类为速读，但它也可以被描述为速读的反面。主动阅读会放慢你的阅读速度，同时大幅提升你的理解能力。主动阅读不仅仅是划重点和在页边空白处写笔记，而是要将脑海中浮现的想法完全吸收并融会贯通。

To start active reading, begin with your book and a notepad. On the notepad write the heading for the chapter and any subheadings for the section you are reading. After finishing reading a subsection (using your pointer!), turn to your notepad and make a few notes.

要开始主动阅读，首先准备好书和笔记本。在笔记本上写下章节标题以及你正在阅读的部分的任何小标题。读完一个小节（用食指！）后，翻到笔记本上记下一些笔记。

During your active reading you should note down:

在积极阅读的过程中，你应该记下以下内容：

1) What the major points are from the section.

1）本节的主要内容是什么？

2) How I can remember the major points from the section.

2）如何记住本节的要点。

3) How I can extend or apply the major points from this section.

3）我如何扩展或应用本节中的要点。

The first question simply gets you to acquire the information fully. The second 101

第一个问题只是为了让你充分掌握信息。第二个问题是为了让你了解基本情况。

question forces you to link, visualize or metaphor the information. The third question gets you to move beyond this and apply the information in a different context. These three questions force you to move each major point through the understanding, explore and finally application phase of holistic learning.

第一个问题迫使你将信息联系起来，进行形象化或比喻。第三个问题则引导你更进一步，将信息应用到不同的情境中。这三个问题促使你逐步理解、探索，最终应用，从而完成整体学习。

For example, let’s say I just finished reading a chapter in psychology about classical conditioning. The major points might be:

例如，假设我刚读完心理学中关于经典条件反射的一章。其要点可能是：

- Discovered by Ivan Pavlov

由伊万·巴甫洛夫发现

- Connects a stimulus with a response

将刺激与反应联系起来

I might remember this by:

我可能会通过以下方式记住这一点：

- Picturing Pavlov’s dogs which drooled at the sound of a bell.

想象一下巴甫洛夫的狗听到铃声就流口水的情景。

I might extend this by:

我可能会进一步阐述：

- Remembering how I feel compelled to answer the phone if I hear a similar ringtone on a television program.

- 我记得，如果我在电视节目中听到类似的铃声，我就忍不住想接电话。

102

Clearly if you did this entire active reading process on every idea in your textbook, you might become overwhelmed. Once you become familiar with it, I strive to use active reading only on sections I have trouble understanding or remembering.

显然，如果你对教科书中的每个概念都进行这种主动阅读，你可能会感到不知所措。一旦你熟悉了这种方法，我就会尽量只在那些我难以理解或记住的部分使用主动阅读。

Mastering Speed Reading

掌握速读技巧

Speed reading, like holistic learning, is a skill. That means reading this book has no benefit to you unless you practice. Throughout this book there will be dozens of opportunities to practice and build new skills. My suggestion is to pick only one or two of these Mind Challenges at a time and practice them for a few weeks before taking on another.

快速阅读和整体学习一样，都是一门技能。这意味着，如果你不练习，读这本书对你没有任何益处。本书中提供了数十个练习和培养新技能的机会。我的建议是，每次只选择一到两项思维挑战，练习几周后再去挑战下一项。

小贴士！

Don't forget to make use of the Speed Reading bonus material.

别忘了利用速读附加材料。

The printout can make it easier to track your practice reading trials.

打印出来的结果可以更方便地追踪你的练习阅读试验情况。

103

Mind Challenge!

脑力挑战！

The goal of this Mind Challenge is to make you comfortable with speed reading techniques and increase your reading speed and comprehension. After you’ve completed this mind challenge, pick another in the book and attempt it.

这项思维挑战的目标是让你熟练掌握速读技巧，提高阅读速度和理解力。完成这项挑战后，请选择书中的另一项挑战进行尝试。

1) Buy one or two books that are similar to the type of material you want to be able to speed read. These will be your books for practice reading.

1）购买一两本与你想练习速读的材料类型相似的书籍。这些将作为你的练习阅读用书。

2) Commit for at least 3 weeks to practice either speed or comprehension exercises (as outlined in Practice Reading) for fifteen minutes a day on your practice books.

2) 至少坚持 3 周，每天在练习册上练习 15 分钟的速度或理解力练习（如《练习阅读》中所述）。

3) Also commit to using your finger as a pointer for the next two weeks on all written material on paper.

3）此外，在接下来的两周内，在所有纸质书面材料上，都要用手指作为指示物。

4) Practice active reading with at least one of your textbooks once a week.

4）每周至少用一本教科书进行一次主动阅读。

104

105

Flow-Based Notetaking

基于流程的笔记法

I’m not a fan of taking detailed and intricate notes. I’m a believer in the “learn it once” principle, which means you should be listening and processing the information as your instructor is teaching–not just transcribing it on a piece of paper to learn later.

我不喜欢做详细繁琐的笔记。我信奉“一次学会”的原则，这意味着你应该在老师讲课的时候认真听讲并消化信息，而不是仅仅把内容抄写在纸上以便以后学习。

One technique I use during classes where there is a lot of information is flow-based notetaking. The goal with flow-based notetaking is providing a surface for connecting and linking ideas as they are reaching you. The linear, bullet-point style of notes that most people use is replaced with a much more fluid (although messier) format.

在信息量大的课堂上，我会使用一种名为“流程式笔记”的技巧。这种笔记方法的目的是提供一个平台，让你能够将脑海中涌现的想法连接起来。它摒弃了大多数人使用的线性、要点式的笔记方式，转而采用一种更加流畅（尽管可能略显凌乱）的格式。

With flow-based note-taking you start by only writing out the major ideas. This means using a few words at most instead of entire sentences. This can reduce readability later, but it enhances learning during the lecture. Facts, dates, details and descriptions are reduced to just a few words, not lengthy paragraphs.

流程式笔记法首先只记录要点。这意味着最多只用几个词，而不是完整的句子。这可能会降低后续的可读性，但能提升课堂学习效果。事实、日期、细节和描述都精简到几个词，而不是冗长的段落。

Once you get an idea written down, your next step is drawing a few arrows to connect it to other ideas. Instead of an ordered hierarchy of ideas, you want to represent the ideas as being interrelated components. This process more closely mirrors the actual holistic learning strategy, where ideas are linked into a web.

一旦你把一个想法写下来，下一步就是画几个箭头把它和其他想法连接起来。你不需要把想法排列成有序的层级结构，而是要把它们表示成相互关联的组成部分。这个过程更贴近实际的整体学习策略，在这种策略中，各种想法像一张网一样相互连接。

106

I tend to use flow-based notetaking as a method for using other techniques as well.

我倾向于使用流程式笔记法作为结合其他技巧的方法。

Metaphor, diagraming and information compression are methods that can be used in conjunction with flow-based notetaking to enhance your understanding. This way you can write out major ideas and connect them to small pictures, diagrams or references to other subjects.

比喻、图表和信息压缩等方法可以与流程式笔记法结合使用，以加深理解。这样，你可以写下主要观点，并将它们与小图片、图表或与其他主题的参考资料联系起来。

Remember that notes are only an intermediate step towards understanding.

请记住，笔记只是理解过程中的一个中间步骤。

Having a beautiful set

拥有一套漂亮的套装

of perfectly written

完美写作

notes is useless if you

如果你这样做，笔记就毫无用处了。

don’t understand the

不明白

subject you are trying

您正在尝试的主题

to learn. Flow-based

学习。基于流程

notetaking, therefore

因此，记笔记

is messier approach to

是一种更混乱的方法

taking notes, but one I

做笔记，但我

believe is more

相信更多

effective at helping to

能够有效地帮助

understand the

理解

material.

材料。

107

108

Hybrid Flow-Based Notetaking

混合式流程笔记法

Flow-based notetaking involves a trade-off between recording and exploration.

基于流程的笔记方法需要在记录和探索之间做出权衡。

With regular, linear notetaking, you can create an almost perfect record of what was said in a class. This method is useful if you need to review that information multiple times in order to learn it properly.

通过规律的、线性的笔记方法，你可以几乎完美地记录课堂上所讲的内容。如果你需要多次复习才能彻底掌握这些信息，这种方法非常有用。

With flow-based notetaking you are sacrificing some later readability, for current understanding. By reducing the content of your notes and adding links or diagrams, the material can be learned more holistically. However, if the class has a high information density or you plan to review notes thoroughly later, there are hybrid strategies you can pursue.

使用流程式笔记法，虽然能更好地理解当前内容，但会牺牲一些日后的可读性。通过精简笔记内容并添加链接或图表，可以更全面地学习知识。然而，如果课程信息量较大，或者你计划之后仔细复习笔记，也可以采用一些混合式的笔记策略。

Flow-Based Afternotes

基于流程的后记

The first hybrid strategy for flow-based notetaking is to take regular notes first and then recopy them into a flow-based format. If you are having trouble keeping up with the pace in a class, this strategy can give you more time to properly digest the information. Although it takes longer than a purely flow-based or linear notetaking style, it gives both readability and understanding.

第一种混合式流程笔记策略是先做常规笔记，然后再将其誊写成流程式笔记格式。如果您在课堂上跟不上节奏，这种策略可以为您提供更多时间来充分理解信息。虽然它比纯粹的流程式或线性笔记方式耗时更长，但它既保证了笔记的可读性，又便于理解。

109

I suggest starting with flow-based afternotes for the first month of trying this new notetaking style. This will ensure that you have a copy of your clearly organized notes in case you need to study them later.

我建议在尝试这种新的笔记方式的第一个月，先从基于流程的笔记开始。这样可以确保你拥有一份条理清晰的笔记副本，以备日后复习之需。

Flow-Based Commenting

基于流程的评论

Some classes have an extremely high information density. When you are writing frantically just to get everything on paper, flow-based notetaking is almost impossible.

有些课程的信息密度极高。当你拼命地想要把所有内容都记下来时，基于流程的笔记方法几乎是不可能的。

Flow-based notetaking assumes that you can record all the critical information in a class in less time than it takes to teach. Most good teachers will give plenty explanation room and examples. During that time you can create the connections, metaphors and diagrams you need to learn holistically.

基于流程的笔记方法假设你可以在课堂上用比授课时间更短的时间内记录下所有关键信息。大多数优秀的老师都会提供充足的讲解空间和例子。在这段时间里，你可以建立联系、运用比喻和图表，从而进行整体学习。

However, in cases when information density goes faster than you can record, flow-based commenting is an alternative strategy. Basically it involves writing down the key information and inserting links into your notes when there is a break. If a professor puts up a few dozen formulas you need to record, you could write all these down first.

然而，当信息传播速度超过你的记录能力时，基于流程的注释就成了另一种策略。它的基本思路是，先记下关键信息，并在信息间隙插入链接。例如，如果教授列出了几十个需要记录的公式，你可以先把它们全部写下来。

Following that, you could add more connections when the professor starts giving examples of how the formulas are used.

接下来，当教授开始举例说明公式的使用方法时，你可以添加更多联系。

110

Recognizing Critical Information

识别关键信息

The key ability with flow-based notetaking is to know what is important. What is the core information taught here? If you write down everything said in a lecture with equal emphasis, then you’ll spend your entire class transcribing instead of thinking.

基于流程的笔记法的关键在于把握重点。这里教授的核心信息是什么？如果你把讲座中提到的所有内容都一一记录下来，并且赋予它们相同的权重，那么你就会把整节课的时间都花在抄写上，而不是思考。

Instinctively writing down every word written on an overhead transparency or Powerpoint slide is useless if you don’t actually think about what you are writing.

如果你不认真思考自己写的内容，那么凭直觉把投影胶片或 PowerPoint 幻灯片上的每一个字都记下来是没用的。

With flow-based notetaking I cut down the amount of information I transcribe and emphasize on connecting and sorting that information in a way I understand.

通过流程式笔记，我减少了记录的信息量，并着重以我能理解的方式将这些信息联系起来并进行分类。

Quick Tip!

小贴士！

Get comfortable writing your ideas in a flow-based format, before trying to do it during class. Flow-based notetaking works best when you have already mastered the Diagraming and Metaphor techniques in the next section.

在课堂上尝试之前，先熟悉一下如何用流程图的形式记录你的想法。如果你已经掌握了下一节中介绍的图表和比喻技巧，流程图式的笔记方法会更加有效。

111

Mind Challenge!

脑力挑战！

The purpose of this mind challenge is to get practice with flow-based notetaking, before deciding whether to use it instead of your current method for taking notes.

这项思维挑战的目的是让你练习基于流程的笔记方法，然后再决定是否用它代替你目前记笔记的方法。

1) Buy a separate note-book and write “Flow-Based Notetaking Practice” at the top.

1）买一本单独的笔记本，并在顶部写上“基于流程的笔记练习”。

2) Commit for two weeks that once per day, you will take your existing notes (written during a class) and transcribe them in a flow-based style. That means taking ideas and writing them down, drawing connections between different ideas.

2）坚持两周，每天一次，将你课堂上做的笔记整理成流程式转录。这意味着要把想法写下来，并建立不同想法之间的联系。

3) As additional practice, you may want to implement some of the other techniques into your flow-based notetaking style.

3）作为额外的练习，你可能希望将其他一些技巧融入到你的流程笔记风格中。

112

Linking Ideas

连接想法

After you acquire information, the next step is to understand and explore those ideas. Understanding only the surface of information, often isn’t enough to make it stick. Going beyond that can take a bit of extra time. But hopefully, as some of these methods become habits, you can use them automatically when you need to.

获取信息之后，下一步是理解和探索这些想法。仅仅了解信息的表面往往不足以真正记住它。深入理解可能需要额外的时间。但希望随着这些方法逐渐成为习惯，你可以在需要时自动运用它们。

These techniques aren’t necessary for every piece of information you learn. Many of the ideas I tackle in a class, I don’t go through the entire formal process of finding metaphors, visceralizing or creating a diagram. Attempting to do so would mean all my time was wasted studying.

并非所有学习信息都需要这些技巧。我在课堂上讲解的许多概念，并不会经过寻找比喻、形象化表达或绘制图表等完整的正式流程。如果那样做，就等于浪费了我所有的学习时间。

Instead, I use these methods selectively on information that falls into two categories:

相反，我只对以下两类信息有选择地使用这些方法：

1) Difficult information

1）难以理解的信息

2) Critical information

2）关键信息

113

Difficult information could be a list of dates, or a series of ten steps which don’t logically follow each other. Difficult information may be abstract, arbitrary, or simply be from a subject that you don’t have many models to draw from. In these cases, applying linking methods can ensure those ideas aren’t forgotten.

难以理解的信息可能是一串日期，也可能是十个逻辑上不连贯的步骤。这些信息可能抽象、随意，或者来自你缺乏参考范例的领域。在这种情况下，运用关联方法可以确保这些信息不会被遗忘。

Critical information is like the foundation of a building. It forms the base from which you construct many other ideas from. A beginner learning about matrices would find that determinants and row reduction are both extremely crucial topics. Failing to understand these ideas (even slightly) could ruin any possibility of learning hundreds of other ideas from which they are based.

关键信息就像建筑物的地基，是构建其他诸多概念的基础。对于矩阵初学者来说，行列式和行简化都是极其重要的概念。如果对这些概念理解有误（哪怕只是略懂皮毛），就可能错失学习其他数百个相关概念的机会。

Information that isn’t particularly crucial or difficult, doesn’t warrant special techniques. Since much of the learning process is subconscious, you will probably form enough associations and models for it to stick without the intervention of a special technique.

如果信息并非特别重要或困难，则无需特殊技巧。由于大部分学习过程都是潜意识的，你很可能会形成足够的联想和模型，无需特殊技巧的介入就能记住这些信息。

Using Linking Methods to Form Models

使用链接方法构建模型

Earlier in the book I pointed out how models formed the basis of constructs.

# ↩

本书前面部分我指出了模型是如何构成概念基础的。

Simplified images and concepts that can be used to describe new information. These 114

可用于描述新信息的简化图像和概念。这114

linking methods are the primary ways to create models in holistic learning. Most of the time I create a model, I would use either metaphor, visceralization or diagrams.

在整体学习中，关联方法是构建模型的主要途径。大多数情况下，我会运用隐喻、形象化描述或图表来构建模型。

Practice, Practice, Practice!

练习，练习，再练习！

Like all the methods in this book, these techniques require practice to use effectively. If you aren’t used to using them it can take 2-3 times as long to apply them.

与本书中的所有方法一样，这些技巧也需要练习才能有效运用。如果您不习惯使用它们，可能需要花费两到三倍的时间才能掌握。

Furthermore, when you are beginning with these techniques, I suggest making use of a pen and paper. I don’t write out metaphors and diagrams if I can imagine them clearly, but if you aren’t used to these techniques, paper is the best way to practice.

此外，当你开始学习这些技巧时，我建议使用纸笔。如果我能清晰地想象出比喻和图表，我就不会把它们写下来，但如果你还不习惯这些技巧，纸笔是最好的练习工具。

115

116

Metaphor

隐喻

Metaphors are a literary tool that describe an object by relating it to something that it isn’t actually associated with. Saying a woman has an hourglass figure, doesn’t mean that she is made of glass and sand falls from the top of her body to a lower half. Instead, it is a metaphor comparing the curves of her figure to the curves of an hourglass.

比喻是一种文学手法，它通过将一个事物与它实际上并不相关的事物联系起来来描述它。说一个女人身材呈沙漏形，并不意味着她是由玻璃制成的，沙子会从她的上半身流到下半身。相反，这是一种比喻，将她身材的曲线比作沙漏的曲线。

Similes are another tool in literature which are almost identical to metaphors.

明喻是文学中的另一种修辞手法，它与隐喻几乎相同。

Similes involve comparing two unrelated things with “like” or “as”. The man was built like an ox. My grandfather is wise as an owl. The wind felt like frozen knives piercing my skin. All of these are similes.

明喻是用“像”或“如同”来比较两个不相关的事物。例如：那人身材魁梧，像头牛。我爷爷智慧过人，像只猫头鹰。寒风刺骨，像冰冷的刀子扎进我的皮肤。这些都是明喻。

Metaphors work in stories by stealing common experiences and attaching them to uncommon ones. If a story said that the character John “had a bulldog face” then you could easily visualize him. Here the metaphor serves its purpose by linking the character John, who you have no mental basis to draw a description from, and relates it to a bulldog, which you have probably seen before.

故事中的隐喻通过借用常见的经验并将其与不常见的经验联系起来而发挥作用。如果故事中说人物约翰“长着一张斗牛犬的脸”，那么你很容易就能想象出他的形象。这里，隐喻通过将你没有任何经验可以描述的约翰与你可能见过的斗牛犬联系起来，从而达到了它的目的。

The purpose of metaphors in holistic learning is similar. You want to create a bridge between an unfamiliar idea and a familiar one. While metaphors in literature are often used to provide visual descriptions, metaphors in holistic learning are more often used to connect similar processes, events or ordering of information.

整体学习中隐喻的作用与之类似。它旨在搭建一座桥梁，连接陌生的概念和熟悉的概念。文学作品中的隐喻常用于提供视觉描述，而整体学习中的隐喻则更多地用于连接相似的过程、事件或信息顺序。

117

For example, let’s say you were in a psychology lecture learning about classical conditioning. Classical conditioning is the process of associating a stimulus and a response and was made famous by Pavlov’s dogs. Pavlov noticed that by conditioning the dogs to associate a ringing bell with the arrival of food, the dogs would salivate when he rang a bell. After several times, the dogs would salivated when hearing a bell, even if he didn't bring food.

例如，假设你正在上心理学课，学习经典条件反射。经典条件反射是指将刺激与反应联系起来的过程，巴甫洛夫的狗使之闻名遐迩。巴甫洛夫注意到，通过训练狗将铃声与食物的到来联系起来，当他摇铃时，狗就会分泌唾液。几次之后，即使他没有带来食物，狗听到铃声也会分泌唾液。

How could you use metaphor to learn this? The first step in metaphor is to look for something in your experience that models this process. As I grew up with Canadian winters, the first metaphor I imagined was

如何运用比喻来学习这个概念呢？运用比喻的第一步是在你的经验中寻找能够模拟这个过程的事物。由于我是在加拿大漫长的冬季中长大的，我首先想到的比喻是……

walking through snow.

在雪地里行走。

When you first walk through snow, every

当你第一次踏上雪地时，每

possible path is equal because they are all

所有可能的路径都相同，因为它们都是

densely filled with powder. But after several

里面装满了粉末。但经过几次之后……

walks through the snow, the first path you

雪地漫步，你走的第一条路

chose will become easier to walk through.

选择将变得更容易。

This is because the compacting of snow under

这是因为积雪在地下被压实。

your feet creates a trail. Soon it is far easier to walk through one path than any other.

你的双脚踩出了一条路。很快，你会发现走其中一条路比走其他路要容易得多。

118

I can link this concept of walking through snow to classical conditioning by seeing the associations in the dogs brain. Initially, the bell could cause the dog to salivate or not (representing the expanse of snow with no trails). But after conditioning the bell with the arrival of food, the path from bell to food inevitably creates a trail through the snow. Eventually the dog will drool at the sound of the bell because that path has been so strongly conditioned.

我可以将狗狗在雪地里行走的概念与经典条件反射联系起来，通过观察狗狗大脑中的联想。最初，铃声可能让狗狗流口水，也可能不流口水（代表着一片没有路径的雪地）。但是，在将铃声与食物的到来建立条件反射后，从铃铛到食物的路径必然会在雪地里形成一条路径。最终，狗狗听到铃声就会流口水，因为这条路径已经被强化了。

Like most metaphors this one isn’t perfect, but it can be a useful example. Coming up with a metaphor is a matter of following three simple steps: 1) Identify the information you want to better understand or remember. In our case it was classical conditioning.

和大多数比喻一样，这个比喻并不完美，但它可以作为一个有用的例子。想出一个比喻只需遵循三个简单的步骤：1）确定你想更好地理解或记住的信息。在我们的例子中，它是经典条件反射。

2) Find something in your experience that matches part of the idea you want to understand. Perfect matches are often impossible, so compromise with a couple imperfect metaphors instead of a complete match. In our case we used walking through snow as an example.

2）在你的经历中找到与你想理解的概念部分相符的事物。完全匹配往往是不可能的，所以与其追求完全一致，不如用几个不太完美的比喻来代替。在我们的例子中，我们用在雪地里行走作为例子。

3) Repeat this process and check for circumstances where the metaphor doesn’t apply. With this example, walking through snow is a linear process, whereas brain neural connections have many different impulses running at the same time.

3）重复上述步骤，检查是否存在比喻不适用的情况。例如，在雪地里行走是一个线性过程，而大脑神经连接则涉及许多不同的冲动同时进行。

119

Sometimes a metaphor doesn’t easily drop into your lap and requires more creative effort. Our snow-walking example fit snugly within the idea of classical conditioning.

有时候，一个恰当的比喻并不容易找到，需要更多的创造性思考。我们举的雪地行走的例子就非常符合经典条件反射的概念。

But, often metaphors require more effort in constructing.

但是，比喻的构建往往需要花费更多精力。

Let’s say you were taking basic calculus and needed to understand derivative. A derivative is the result of differentiating a function and has many useful properties in mathematics.

假设你正在学习基础微积分，需要理解导数的概念。导数是对一个函数求导的结果，它在数学中有很多有用的性质。

A derivative will measure the slope at any part of the parent function. So if you have a function that rises in a straight line upwards, the derivative will be flat as the slope is the same throughout the parent function. In a curved line, the derivative will have a shape that models how the slope changes at every position on the parent function.

导数衡量的是原函数在任意一点的斜率。因此，如果一个函数沿直线向上递增，那么它的导数将是水平的，因为原函数的斜率在整个曲线上保持不变。对于曲线，导数的形状会反映出原函数上每个点的斜率是如何变化的。

The problem with this explanation of a derivative is that it might be hard to remember what a derivative represents. Creating a metaphor can help because it will connect the principles of differentiation to a common experience.

这种对导数的解释的问题在于，人们可能很难记住导数代表什么。创造一个比喻会有所帮助，因为它能将微分原理与常见的经验联系起来。

A metaphor you might come up with is driving a car. On the dashboard you have the odometer and speedometer. The odometer measures how far your vehicle has traveled and the speedometer measures how fast you are going. If you graphed your odometer and speedometer over time, the speedometer should be the derivative of the odometer. The slope of your position graph would be the speed graph.

你可以用开车来做比喻。仪表盘上有里程表和速度表。里程表记录车辆行驶的距离，速度表记录行驶速度。如果将里程表和速度表的读数随时间变化绘制成图表，速度表的读数应该是里程表读数的导数。速度图的斜率就是位置图的斜率。

120

Tips for Improving Your

提升你的技巧

Metaphors

隐喻

The problem with both of the examples in the last section is that they are based on previous metaphors I’ve already constructed. When you are given an idea, you might have few starting points in creating a metaphor. How can you improve the speed and quality of the metaphors you make?

上一节中的两个例子的问题在于，它们都基于我之前已经构建过的比喻。当你得到一个想法时，你可能很难找到构建比喻的切入点。那么，如何才能提高构建比喻的速度和质量呢？

1) Start by asking for a metaphor.

1）首先要求对方举一个比喻。

Unless you ask yourself what a good metaphor would be to describe an idea, you probably won’t find one. Keep the concept of metaphors in mind the next time you encounter an idea you have difficulty relating to.

除非你主动思考用什么比喻来恰当地描述某个想法，否则你可能找不到合适的比喻。下次遇到难以理解的想法时，不妨想想比喻这个概念。

121

2) Pick the first thing that comes to mind.

2）选择你脑海中浮现的第一个想法。

Finding metaphors is a process of creative experimentation. This means you’ll probably have to go through several incorrect metaphors before finding one that seems to model your topic. I can usually go through 4-6 incorrect metaphors in a minute or two before finding one that seems to work.

寻找比喻是一个充满创造性实验的过程。这意味着你可能需要尝试好几个不恰当的比喻，才能找到一个似乎能恰当地描述你主题的。我通常一两分钟内就能尝试四到六个不恰当的比喻，然后才能找到一个合适的。

My suggestion is to not inhibit the creative process by claiming you can’t find a good metaphor. Instead, just grab the first thing that comes to mind. Look for where it fits and where it doesn’t fit. If it doesn’t fit, discard part of it and try again.

我的建议是，不要因为找不到合适的比喻而阻碍创作过程。相反，想到什么就说什么。看看它是否合适，不合适。如果不合适，就舍弃一部分，重新尝试。

3) Refine and test your metaphors.

3）完善并检验你的比喻。

Often you’ll find a metaphor that works as a description for some parts of your idea, but not all. My suggestion then is to collect multiple metaphors that each explore the idea from a different angle. Not only does this reduce the chance of making an error in understanding, but it gives you a greater amount of links to a single idea, which improves the quality of your construct.

你常常会发现某个比喻可以描述你想法的某些部分，但并非全部。因此，我的建议是收集多个比喻，每个比喻都从不同的角度探讨你的想法。这不仅能降低理解错误的可能性，还能让你围绕同一个想法建立更多联系，从而提升你构建的框架的质量。

122

Mind Challenge!

脑力挑战！

The purpose of this Mind Challenge is to improve your ability with using metaphors to understand and remember abstract ideas: 1) Commit for at least two weeks to go over a subject you are studying once each day. After you read your textbook or notes, write out at least 3-5 major ideas.

这项思维挑战的目的是提高你运用比喻来理解和记忆抽象概念的能力：1）坚持至少两周，每天复习一遍你正在学习的科目。阅读完课本或笔记后，写下至少3-5个主要观点。

2) With each idea, write out a possible metaphor that could be used to explain it.

2）针对每个想法，写出一个可以用来解释它的比喻。

3) If the metaphor isn’t complete, try looking for one or two more metaphors that could also associate to the same idea.

3）如果比喻不完整，试着再找一两个可以与同一概念相关的比喻。

4) Use the 10-Year Old Rule. Could you explain this metaphor to a ten year old child? If your metaphor is just as confusing as the original example, repeat it to yourself and rewrite it until you get something that is simple and easy to understand.

4）运用“十岁小孩法则”。你能向一个十岁小孩解释这个比喻吗？如果你的比喻和最初的例子一样令人费解，那就反复琢磨，直到你写出一个简单易懂的版本。

5) Repeat this process with the other 2-4 ideas in your textbook until you are satisfied that you understand them.

5）对课本中的其他 2-4 个概念重复此过程，直到你确信自己理解它们为止。

123

124

Visceralization (Visceral + Visualization) You’ve probably heard of visualization. This is the process of creating a mental image. Visceralization is my word to describe imagining not only a mental picture, but sounds, sensations and emotions. Often a mental image will work, but connecting an idea to several senses and even emotional states can create a stronger link than a picture.

内脏化（内脏 + 可视化）你可能听说过可视化。这是在脑海中构建图像的过程。内脏化是我用来描述不仅想象画面，还想象声音、感觉和情绪的词汇。通常，一幅画面就能奏效，但将一个想法与多种感官甚至情绪状态联系起来，比单纯的图像更能建立起牢固的联系。

To visceralize an idea, the best way to start is simply with forming a mental picture.

要将一个想法形象化，最好的方法就是从在脑海中形成一幅画面开始。

This works best when the idea is already fairly easy to imagine. Imagining the process of light entering your eyes, traveling through rods and cones in your retina, through your optic nerve and into your brain is a process easier to visualize than, let’s say, different philosophies of ethics.

当想法本身就比较容易想象时，这种方法效果最佳。想象一下光线进入你的眼睛，穿过视网膜上的视杆细胞和视锥细胞，经过视神经最终进入大脑的过程，这比想象不同的伦理哲学要容易得多。

Visceralization works best with concrete information. I’ve found abstract information to be better suited for metaphors, although there is considerable gray area between the two.

生动形象的表达方式最适合具体信息。我发现抽象信息更适合用比喻来表达，尽管两者之间存在相当大的灰色地带。

After you have formed a mental picture, begin adding other sensations into the image. If you are trying to visualize the perception of light, imagine feeling the light enter your eyes. You might want to visualize a specific sound as it hits your retina and surges down the optic nerve.

在脑海中形成画面之后，开始在画面中添加其他感觉。如果你想想象光线的感知，就想象光线进入你的眼睛。你也可以想象某种特定的声音击中视网膜，沿着视神经向下传播。

When I started to learn about matrices, I had to learn how to calculate a 125

当我开始学习矩阵时，我必须学习如何计算125。

determinant. A determinant is found by multiplying the top left and bottom right numbers and subtracting from that the product of the top right and bottom left numbers. This abstract process would have been difficult to remember if I hadn’t visceralized it first.

行列式。行列式的计算方法是：将左上角和右下角的数字相乘，然后减去右上角和左下角的数字的乘积。如果我没有先将其形象化，这个抽象的过程会很难记住。

Visceralizing this process of calculating a determinant involved first imagining a 2x2 grid containing four numbers. I then imagined my right hand swiping through the top left and bottom right numbers. As I did this I imagined a blue streak and the feeling of added weight being formed in my hand. Then I imagined my left hand swiping through the top right and bottom left numbers. From that I imagined a red streak and weight being reduced in my right hand.

为了更直观地理解计算行列式的过程，我首先想象一个包含四个数字的 2x2 方格。然后，我想象我的右手划过左上角和右下角的数字。在这个过程中，我想象出一道蓝色的痕迹，同时感觉右手的重量增加了。接着，我想象我的左手划过右上角和左下角的数字。这时，我想象出一道红色的痕迹，同时感觉右手的重量减轻了。

By connecting specific senses, sounds and

通过连接特定的感官、声音和

kinesthetic actions to the original idea, it was

动觉行为与最初的想法，是

easy to remember for future questions.

便于记忆，方便以后提问。

Some learning experts claim that there are

一些学习专家声称存在

three main types of learning styles present in

三种主要的学习风格类型

people: visual, auditory and kinesthetic.

人类：视觉型、听觉型和动觉型。

Visual learners (I presume I’m a highly visual

视觉型学习者（我猜我自己就是一个视觉型学习者）

learner) require information to be presented in

学习者）需要以以下方式呈现信息

pictures to understand them. Auditory

通过图片来理解它们。听觉

126

listeners need to hear information in terms of sounds and instructions to understand.

听众需要通过声音和指令来获取信息才能理解。

Kinesthetic learners need to feel physically involved by touching and manipulating in order to understand.

动觉型学习者需要通过触摸和操作来感受身体上的参与，才能理解。

While I don’t think labeling yourself as one learner or another is entirely constructive, it is useful to see that different people learn differently. Visceralization is an attempt to take information that

虽然我不认为给自己贴上某种学习者的标签完全有益，但认识到不同的人学习方式不同是有益的。内省式学习是一种尝试，它试图将信息转化为……

isn’t in your preferred format and

格式不符合您的偏好，而且

translate it into a style that you can

将其翻译成一种你可以……的风格

easily understand and relate with.

容易理解和认同。

An added step to

增加一个步骤

visceralization is giving ideas

内脏化正在激发灵感

emotional impact. It is well-

情感上的影响。这很好。

known by psychologists that

心理学家们都知道，

memory is influenced by being in

记忆会受到所处环境的影响

different emotional states.

不同的情绪状态。

Connecting ideas to emotional

将想法与情感联系起来

impacts (even small ones) can make

影响（即使是微小的影响）也能造成

them more memorable than if they

它们比它们更令人难忘

are completely dry.

完全干燥。

127

How to Visceralize

如何进行内脏化

1) Identify the concept you want to visceralize. This could be a process in biology, a function in computer programming or mathematical concept in calculus.

1）确定你想形象化的概念。这可以是生物学中的某个过程、计算机编程中的某个函数，或者微积分中的某个数学概念。

2) Start by picking a mental image to base the idea from. If you aren’t used to visceralization, I suggest making a crude drawing of the idea on paper so it will be easier to hold for the duration of this exercise.

2）首先，选择一个画面作为构思的基础。如果你不习惯将画面具象化，我建议你在纸上粗略地画出这个想法，这样更容易在整个练习过程中保持这种感觉。

3) Does the process move through time, or is it a static image? Taking a determinant has several steps, so it flows through time. If your concept does flow through time, try to visualize it moving as if you were watching a movie.

3）这个过程是随时间变化的，还是一个静态图像？确定一个决定因素需要多个步骤，因此它是一个随时间变化的过程。如果你的概念确实随时间变化，试着把它想象成一部电影，看着它动态移动。

4) Now add another sensation to your image. Try picking it up, acting upon it or feeling it as a sensation within your body. Link the sensation to the movement or feel of the mental image.

4）现在，在你的意象中添加另一种感觉。试着捕捉它、对它采取行动，或者把它当作身体内的一种感觉来感受。将这种感觉与心理意象的运动或感觉联系起来。

5) Add other sensations or emotional impacts to the image.

5）为图像添加其他感觉或情感影响。

6) Refine and repeat the image until you can bring it up in just a few seconds of thinking of it.

6）反复练习，直到你能在想到它后的几秒钟内把它想出来。

128

Like metaphor, visceralization is a process of creative experimentation. You may not be able to come up with a great picture at first, so just pick something to get you started. You can always refine and discard parts of the picture that don’t work until you get an image that is memorable and vivid.

与隐喻类似，具象化也是一个创造性的实验过程。你可能一开始无法想出一个完美的画面，所以先随便选一个作为起点。你可以不断修改完善，剔除不合适的部分，直到最终得到一个令人难忘、生动形象的图像。

I strongly suggest making the use of paper and pen when practicing this technique.

我强烈建议在练习这项技巧时使用纸笔。

Using paper can help you get practice with forming memorable images.

使用纸张可以帮助你练习形成令人印象深刻的图像。

Metaphorisceralization

隐喻化

Alright, so perhaps blending three words together (metaphor, visceral and visualization) is a bit much. But metaphors can be combined with visceralization for abstract but important ideas you want to better understand and remember. The process is exactly the same as visceralization, except you use a metaphor to find a concrete description of your abstract idea first.

好吧，或许把三个词（比喻、直观感受和视觉化）混在一起有点复杂。但是，比喻可以和直观感受结合起来，帮助你更好地理解和记忆那些抽象但重要的概念。这个过程和直观感受完全相同，只是你首先要用比喻来具体描述你的抽象概念。

With our calculus example from the last section, this could mean you visceralize driving your car while watching the speedometer and odometer moving. Sometimes adding a visceralization to metaphor is overkill, but it can be helpful for tricky concepts that are hard to describe and imagine.

以上一节的微积分例子为例，这意味着你可以想象自己开车时，看着速度表和里程表上的数字变化，从而产生一种切身的感受。有时，在比喻中加入切身感受可能有点过头，但对于难以描述和想象的复杂概念，这种方法却很有帮助。

129

Mind Challenge!

脑力挑战！

The purpose of this mind challenge is to give you better flexibility and skill with your ability to form mental pictures and link in different sensations.

这项思维挑战的目的是提高你形成心理图像和将不同感觉联系起来的能力，从而增强你的灵活性和技巧。

1) Get a few blank sheets of paper and a pencil for drawing.

1）准备几张白纸和一支铅笔用来画画。

2) Pull open your textbook and pick a few key concepts or ideas. If you are just starting with visceralization, pick ideas that are easy for you to form mental images.

2）打开课本，挑选几个关键概念或想法。如果你刚开始接触内省法，那就选择那些容易在你脑海中形成图像的想法。

Completely abstract ideas or incredibly complex ones might be too hard to start with.

完全抽象或极其复杂的概念可能太难入门。

3) Form a mental image, add sensations and emotions to your idea as the steps are for visceralization on the previous pages.

3）形成心理图像，将感觉和情感添加到你的想法中，就像前面几页中关于内脏化的步骤一样。

4) Quickly sketch a picture of the idea based on your mental image. (30-60 seconds max.)5) Repeat this with several other ideas each day for a two weeks.

4）根据你脑海中的画面，快速勾勒出这个想法的草图。（最多30-60秒。）5）连续两周，每天用几个不同的想法重复这个过程。

130

131

Diagraming

图表绘制

The final technique I have for exploring ideas is diagraming. Diagraming is a simpler form of visceralization. Creating diagrams takes more time than visualizing an image, but it is easier to do and can be used on fairly abstract ideas that would be hard to imagine otherwise. Diagraming can also be combined easily with flow-based notetaking and active reading while you are learning.

我探索想法的最后一种技巧是绘制图表。绘制图表是一种更简单的具象化方式。虽然绘制图表比想象图像需要更多时间，但它更容易操作，并且可以用于处理那些难以用其他方式想象的抽象概念。在学习过程中，绘制图表还可以轻松地与流程笔记和主动阅读相结合。

A diagram is a picture that compresses several ideas together in an easy source. The most common types of diagrams are charts. A scatterplot can compress hundreds of individual data points into a single graph. Flow-based diagrams can chart a complex series of interactions and steps onto one image that is easy to see.

图表是一种将多个概念浓缩成易于理解的图像。最常见的图表类型是散点图。散点图可以将数百个独立的数据点压缩到一张图中。流程图可以将一系列复杂的交互和步骤绘制在一张清晰易懂的图像上。

Often books will come with premade diagrams to simplify the information they contain. Where they lack diagrams, constructing your own can be useful to chart the flow of ideas, picture different concepts or link different concepts together.

书籍通常会附带预先制作好的图表，以简化其中包含的信息。如果书籍没有图表，自己绘制图表也很有用，可以帮助梳理思路、形象化不同的概念或将不同的概念联系起来。

There are three main types of diagrams I’ll cover here: flow, concept and image diagrams. Using some combination of these three types can help you understand almost any concept. The only disadvantage of diagraming is that it takes longer than metaphor or visceralization. However, with practice I’ve been able to speed up this process as well, so that I can quickly create a crude diagram in less than a minute.

本文将介绍三种主要的图表类型：流程图、概念图和图像图。结合使用这三种图表类型几乎可以帮助你理解任何概念。绘制图表的唯一缺点是比比喻或形象化描述耗时更长。但是，通过练习，我已经能够加快这个过程，现在我可以在不到一分钟的时间内快速绘制出一个粗略的图表。

132

Flow-Based Diagrams

基于流程的图表

A flow based diagram is useful for:

流程图适用于：

- Charting a sequence of steps. (How to do long division, the process of creating a cash-flow statement, etc.)

- 绘制步骤顺序图。（例如，如何进行长除法、如何编制现金流量表等。）

- Charting historical events, creating branches linking events together not only through causation but through the time period they rest.

- 绘制历史事件图，创建分支将事件联系起来，不仅通过因果关系，而且通过它们所处的时间段。

- Mapping out a system. (e.g. How a function works in a computer program) The basis of a flow-based diagram is that you start with a single element, and draw connecting arrows to different ideas as they relate to that element. I could have created a diagram for the steps I undertook to write this book. Starting with the initial idea, I could have drawn lines showing subsequent steps, branching off where there is more options.

- 绘制系统流程图。（例如，计算机程序中某个函数的工作原理）流程图的基本原理是从一个元素开始，然后用箭头连接与该元素相关的不同概念。我本可以绘制一个流程图来展示我撰写本书的步骤。从最初的想法开始，我可以画线表示后续步骤，并在出现更多选项时进行分支。

The importance in a diagram must be for your understanding, not creating a pretty picture. It is easy to get caught up in making a tidy and beautiful picture and waste hours on a diagram which could have been built in just a few minutes. Simplify and be messy if you need to.

图表的重点在于帮助理解，而不是追求美观。人们很容易沉迷于绘制整齐漂亮的图表，从而浪费数小时，而这些图表原本只需几分钟就能完成。如果需要，可以简化图表，即使略显粗糙也没关系。

133

Concept-Based Diagrams

基于概念的图表

A concept based diagram links together ideas and is closely related to flow-based notetaking. Here the associations aren’t necessarily different steps in a sequence or an order of dates, but relationships between ideas. Create arrows connecting different ideas, but include 1-3 word snippets on each arrow to note how the two ideas are related.

概念图将各种想法联系起来，与流程图式笔记密切相关。这里的关联不一定是顺序中的不同步骤或日期顺序，而是想法之间的关系。用箭头连接不同的想法，并在每个箭头上添加 1-3 个词语片段，以说明这两个想法之间的联系。

If I wanted to create a diagram of different financial accounting principles, I might start by writing down the four different statements: balance sheet, income, retained earnings and cash flow. From that I could then connect ideas together to form a web of information.

如果我想绘制一张展现不同财务会计原则的图表，我可能会先列出四份不同的报表：资产负债表、利润表、留存收益表和现金流量表。然后，我可以将各个概念联系起来，形成一张信息网络。

If I wanted to map out the characters in a novel, I could start with the protagonist in the center and map out different characters and relationships that character had.

如果我想绘制一部小说中的人物关系图，我可以从主角开始，把主角放在中心位置，然后绘制出不同的人物以及主角与这些人物之间的关系。

Mapping of this kind can help organize your thinking on a large quantity of information.

这种思维导图可以帮助你整理大量信息的思路。

Start with the most important ideas and branch off into details and minor ideas.

先从最重要的想法入手，然后逐步展开细节和次要想法。

134

Image Diagrams

图像图表

Not technically a diagram, but image diagrams are important for diagraming so I’ll include these here. An image diagram is any rough sketch or doodle used to represent an idea or the association of ideas. Here you can create a small image either by itself or within larger diagrams to make them more memorable.

严格来说，图像图并非图表，但它对于图表绘制至关重要，因此我在此也列出。图像图是指任何用于表示想法或想法关联的草图或涂鸦。您可以在这里创建单独的小图像，也可以将其嵌入更大的图表中，以增强记忆效果。

I frequently make small images in my notes or diagrams as a reference for important ideas and to make them more clear inside my head. Drawing detailed images can be a waste of time if it takes too long, but a simple 10-20 second doodle can be valuable if it helps connect the ideas properly.

我经常在笔记或图表中画一些小图，作为重要概念的参考，并帮助我更清晰地理解它们。如果绘制过于精细的图像耗时过长，那可能是一种浪费时间，但一个简单的10-20秒的涂鸦，如果能帮助我更好地将各个想法联系起来，就很有价值。

Combining Diagrams with Metaphor and Visceralization Diagrams can be mixed with the usage of metaphor and visceralization to improve your understanding of ideas. After you have found a metaphor or mental image to describe an idea, create a quick sketch, connecting different concepts together on paper.

将图表与隐喻和形象化相结合 图表可以与隐喻和形象化相结合，以加深对概念的理解。找到一个合适的隐喻或心理意象来描述某个概念后，快速绘制草图，将不同的概念在纸上连接起来。

With our calculus example from the previous section on metaphors, I could have drawn an image of a racecar and linked the odometer to a position graph and the 135

结合上一节关于隐喻的微积分例子，我可以画一辆赛车的图像，并将里程表与位置图和135号赛车联系起来。

speedometer to a speed graph. I could have associated the two of those graphs with a symbol for differentiation making the relationship between all elements clear.

将速度表与速度图联系起来。我本可以用一个表示差异的符号将这两个图表关联起来，从而清晰地展现所有元素之间的关系。

Adding a diagram to a metaphor or visceralized image may be unnecessary for many situations, but it can be helpful for remembering a complex idea.

在许多情况下，为比喻或形象化的描述添加图表可能是不必要的，但它有助于记住复杂的概念。

136

137

Mind Challenge!

脑力挑战！

The purpose of this challenge is to enhance your skill at making diagrams and increase your diagraming speed. Since diagraming is the slowest of the three linking techniques mentioned in this section, improving speed is important if you want it to become a useful technique for your daily studying without it becoming a burden on your time.

这项挑战旨在提升你绘制图表的技巧和速度。由于图表绘制是本节提到的三种链接技巧中最慢的一种，因此，如果你想让它成为日常学习中一项实用的技巧，而不至于占用你太多时间，那么提高速度就至关重要。

1) Get a sheet of paper and find an idea or set of concepts that could be made into a diagram.

1）拿一张纸，想出一个想法或一组概念，并将其制作成图表。

2) Start a timer for no more than 2-5 minutes and begin creating a diagram using one or a combination of the different diagram types.

2) 开始计时，时间不超过 2-5 分钟，然后开始使用一种或多种不同的图表类型来创建图表。

3) When the timer beeps, stop what you are doing and make a note of the amount 138

3) 当计时器发出哔哔声时，停止你正在做的事情，并记下数字 138。

of information you’ve managed to store, the clarity of that information and how many different relationships or connections you were able to make.

你所存储的信息量、信息的清晰度以及你能够建立的不同关系或联系的数量。

4) Repeat this exercise once a day for two weeks until you’re comfortable making quick diagrams of several different ideas.

4）每天重复此练习一次，持续两周，直到你能轻松地快速绘制几个不同想法的图表。

Quick Tip!

小贴士！

Once you've mastered diagraming, try combining it with flow-based notetaking in classes or active reading for your textbooks.

一旦你掌握了图表绘制技巧，就可以尝试将其与课堂上的流程图笔记或教科书的主动阅读结合起来。

139

Handling the Arbitrary

处理任意性

Arbitrary information can present a challenge when trying to learn holistically.

任意信息会给全面学习带来挑战。

Just how do you form links, metaphors or visceralizations with things such as:

你究竟如何与以下事物建立联系、比喻或情感共鸣：

- A list of dates.

- 日期列表。

- The scientific names of different parts of your anatomy.

- 你身体各个部位的学名。

- A series of steps.

一系列步骤。

- Rules and laws that have no clear basis, but still need to be followed.

- 没有明确依据，但仍然需要遵守的规则和法律。

- Scientific formulas that take hours to derive manually.

- 需要花费数小时手动推导的科学公式。

Normally these are situations that require memorization. Holistic learning strives to avoid rote memorization whenever possible. Instead, using metaphor, visceralization and diagraming to create models and eventually constructs is a better and faster way to use your brain. Unfortunately there are some cases where these tools won’t work.

通常情况下，这些情况需要记忆。整体学习力求尽可能避免死记硬背。相反，运用比喻、形象化和图表来创建模型并最终构建概念，是一种更有效、更快捷的思维方式。遗憾的是，在某些情况下，这些方法并不适用。

140

Information that is arbitrary, or too large and complex to understand fully requires different techniques. If you find that using the linking methods won’t help you understand the material, or it simply takes too long for the amount of information you need to learn, arbitrary methods can come in handy.

如果信息过于随意，或者过于庞大复杂而难以完全理解，则需要采用不同的方法。如果您发现使用关联方法无法帮助您理解材料，或者学习所需信息量过大而耗时，那么任意方法就派上用场了。

These arbitrary methods hover the line between rote memorization and holistic learning. The link, peg and information compression methods may be seen as just another set of memorization techniques. However, they have been designed so that memorization can be done quickly and work the way the brain is set up to learn. If rote memorization is a blunt club and holistic learning is a scalpel, these techniques would fall somewhere around the range of a steak knife.

这些方法介于死记硬背和整体学习之间，看似随意，实则不然。链接法、挂钩法和信息压缩法或许可以被视为另一种记忆技巧。然而，它们的设计旨在快速记忆，并符合大脑的学习方式。如果把死记硬背比作钝器，把整体学习比作手术刀，那么这些技巧的精准度就如同牛排刀一般。

Even more so than the linking techniques, the arbitrary techniques require practice. There are two reasons more practice is required with these methods: 1) You should use them infrequently. I use the link and peg techniques sparingly, since the linking methods described in the last chapter produce a deeper understanding.

相比连接技巧，任意技巧更需要练习。这些方法需要更多练习的原因有两个：1）应该少用。我很少使用连接和钉合技巧，因为上一章介绍的连接方法能带来更深入的理解。

Because they aren’t being used constantly, practice is important to keep these tools sharp.2) They are more complex than linking methods. Link, peg and information 141

由于这些工具并非经常使用，因此练习对于保持其熟练度至关重要。2）它们比链接方法更复杂。链接、挂钩和信息 141

compression are less intuitive than the linking methods because they use a bit of mental trickery to get the job done. Because they are less intuitive, they require more practice to pull off successfully.

压缩方法不如链接方法直观，因为它需要一些思维技巧才能完成任务。正因为如此，它们需要更多的练习才能熟练掌握。

Quick Tip!

小贴士！

Arbitrary information has a weaker structure. Always try to shift information into a layer that is easier to learn:

任意信息的结构较弱。应尽量将信息转移到更容易学习的层次：

Weak – Learning through repetition.

薄弱环节——通过重复学习。

Better – Learning with linking, pegging or information compression.

更好的学习方式——通过链接、关联或信息压缩。

Best – Learning with metaphor, visceralization or diagrams.

最佳学习方法——运用比喻、形象化或图表。

142

143

The Link Method

链接方法

I didn’t create the link method, as it is a memory trick that has been around for years. The link method is called that because it serves the purpose of linking a series of ideas together, like a chain. As long as you can access one link on the chain, you should be able to easily travel to any other link on the chain.

我并非链接法的发明者，这是一种流传多年的记忆技巧。之所以称之为链接法，是因为它的作用是将一系列概念像链条一样连接起来。只要你能访问链条上的一个环节，就能轻松地跳转到任何其他环节。

The link method works best for storing a sequence of arbitrary information. Steps in a process, sets of names or formulas written out in sequence all can be tackled using the link method. As you get practice with the link method you can chain together a series of several dozen ideas with only a few minutes of focus.

链接法最适合存储一系列任意信息。流程步骤、名称集或按顺序排列的公式都可以用链接法处理。随着你对链接法的熟练运用，只需几分钟的专注，你就能将几十个想法串联起来。

Quick Tip!

小贴士！

Despite the name (I didn't invent the technique) the Link Method has less to do with holistic learning and sits closer towards rote-memorization. It can be a useful method, but I would stick with metaphor, visceralization and diagraming where possible.

尽管名为“链接法”（我并非此法的发明者），但它与整体学习关系不大，更接近于死记硬背。它或许有用，但我建议尽可能坚持使用比喻、形象化和图表等方法。

144

Steps to Use the Link

使用链接的步骤

Method

方法

Step One: Create Your Sequence

第一步：创建你的序列

Start by writing out on paper a sequence of information you want to store. Break apart the information into units you can immediately understand. It is important that the information be displayed in a linear list because that is the only way the link method can hold data.

首先，在纸上写下你想存储的信息序列。将信息分解成你能立即理解的单元。信息必须以线性列表的形式呈现，因为这是链接方法能够存储数据的唯一方式。

A simple example might be linking together a grocery list: 1) Bananas

一个简单的例子是将购物清单连接起来：1）香蕉

2) Milk

2）牛奶

145

3) Baked Beans

3）烤豆

4) Butter

4）黄油

5) Jam

5）果酱

While I’m sure few classes would get you to remember a grocery list, the principle remains the same.

虽然我确信很少有课程能让你记住购物清单，但原理仍然是一样的。

Turning a formula into a sequence requires that you convert it into a form you might enter into a calculator. Therefore a formula such as V = 1+x/b could be written as V = 1 PLUS X DIVIDE B. V, =, 1, PLUS, X, DIVIDE and B would be your elements in the series. Complex formulas may take time to break down if you aren’t used to this approach, but it can still be helpful if you are worried you might forget.

将公式转化为数列需要将其转换成计算器可以输入的形式。因此，像 V = 1+x/b 这样的公式可以写成 V = 1 PLUS X DIVIDE B。其中，V、=、1、PLUS、X、DIVIDE 和 B 就是数列中的元素。如果您不习惯这种方法，可能需要一些时间才能理解复杂的公式，但如果您担心自己会忘记，这种方法仍然很有帮助。

Step Two: Symbolize Each Object in the List

第二步：将列表中的每个对象符号化

When dealing with an abstract list, you need to create an easily recognizable symbol for each item in the list. In a management course, I needed to remember Henry Fayol’s ten principles of management. I used the link technique and created a symbol for each element. Division of labor became a knife and remuneration of 146

处理抽象列表时，你需要为列表中的每个项目创建一个易于识别的符号。在一次管理课程中，我需要记住亨利·法约尔的十大管理原则。我运用了链接技巧，为每个要素创建了一个符号。劳动分工变成了一把刀，而报酬则变成了146。

personnel became a carrot on a stick.

人员成了诱饵。

It is important that the symbol

符号很重要

immediately helps you conjure the original

立即帮助你唤起最初的记忆。

concept. Picking symbols that don’t give any

概念。选择不带任何含义的符号

significance to the original idea aren’t useful,

对最初想法的意义并不重要，

because the link method can only store visual

因为链接方法只能存储视觉信息。

symbols, not abstract ideas. Unless you feel

符号，而非抽象概念。除非你觉得

confident you can convert your symbol back

您有信心将您的符号转换回来

to the original idea, you can’t use the link method.

对于最初的想法，你不能使用链接方法。

With formulas, you can memorize elements of the formula by creating an object that starts with the same letter as the algebraic symbol and coming up with a shorthand for different mathematical symbols. The variable a in a formula could be symbolized by an apple and raising a term to the power of two could be visualized as a colored square.

利用公式，你可以通过创建一个以代数符号首字母开头的对象，以及为不同的数学符号创建简写来记忆公式中的元素。例如，公式中的变量 a 可以用一个苹果来表示，而将一项的二次方可以形象地表示为一个彩色方块。

Write out your symbols next to each item in your sequence. As you get better with linking, you might not need to write all these steps. When you start with the method, write them out so they become habits.

在序列中的每个项目旁边写出你的符号。随着你连接能力的提高，你可能不需要写出所有步骤。刚开始使用这种方法时，把它们写下来，以便养成习惯。

147

Step Three: Create Your Links

第三步：创建链接

This step is the basis of the link method. What you want to do is create vivid and exaggerated mental images that associate two symbols in the sequence. This means you will need to create a mental image linking 1 and 2, 2 and 3, 3 and 4, etc.

这一步骤是关联法的基础。你需要做的是创建生动且夸张的心理图像，将序列中的两个符号联系起来。这意味着你需要创建一个心理图像，将 1 和 2、2 和 3、3 和 4 等联系起来。

With our grocery list we would have to first create a mental image that links bananas to milk. For this I might imagine a giant banana that has cow spots on it. I could also imagine a farmer milking a banana’s udders instead of a cow.

有了购物清单，我们首先需要在脑海中构建一个将香蕉和牛奶联系起来的画面。为此，我可能会想象一根巨大的香蕉，上面长着奶牛的斑点。我还可以想象一个农民正在挤香蕉的奶，而不是挤奶牛的奶。

These ridiculous mental images are important for

这些荒谬的心理图像对于……很重要

creating the link. If the link isn’t wildly exaggerated and vivid, it will be difficult to recall. Simply picturing an ordinary jug of milk next to a banana wouldn’t be sufficient to create a strong link. But a cow-spotted banana or a banana being milked are both crazy enough to stick in memory.

建立联系。如果这种联系不够夸张生动，就很难记住。仅仅想象一罐普通的牛奶放在一根香蕉旁边，不足以建立牢固的联系。但是，一根长着奶牛斑点的香蕉，或者正在挤奶的香蕉，这两种画面都足够奇特，能够让人印象深刻。

After you create link between two items, make a link between the next two items. So for our grocery list that means you would need a link between milk and baked beans.

在两个项目之间建立链接后，再将接下来的两个项目建立链接。例如，在我们的购物清单中，牛奶和烤豆之间就需要建立链接。

Again, a cow-spotted bean or a giant bean wrestling a carton 148

又来了，一颗牛斑豆或一颗巨型豆子与一个纸箱搏斗 148

of milk might be vivid enough to create a link.

牛奶的形象或许足够生动，足以建立联系。

Try continuing with our grocery list to create your own links between beans and butter and butter with jam.

请尝试按照我们的购物清单，将豆子和黄油、黄油和果酱等食材组合起来。

After you are done created a list, go through all of your links to see that one easily follows into the next. If you can’t find the next link after viewing one, you probably didn’t associate a vivid enough picture to the resulting details.

创建列表后，请检查所有链接，确保链接之间衔接流畅。如果查看一个链接后找不到下一个链接，可能是因为你没有将足够清晰的画面与结果联系起来。

Quick Tip!

小贴士！

One attribute the Link method shares with holistic learning methods is the need for imagination. Don't be shy, trying to pick only

Link教学法与整体学习法的一个共同特点是需要想象力。不要害羞，尽量只挑选自己感兴趣的内容。

“reasonable” connections between ideas. Linking works best when the mental pictures are exaggerated and bizarre. Holistic learning works best with many, varied connections.

概念之间“合理”的联系。当脑海中的画面夸张而怪诞时，联系效果最佳。整体学习最有利于建立多种多样的联系。

149

Challenges With the Link

链接方面的挑战

Method

方法

Although the link method can be more time consuming than other techniques, it is reliable and your speed will improve with practice. There are a few other challenges that can arise with using the link technique you will need to be careful of when creating a list:

虽然链接法比其他方法更耗时，但它可靠，而且随着练习，速度会提高。使用链接法创建列表时，还需要注意一些其他挑战：

Repetition of Symbols

符号的重复

Lets say you want to remember the following formula sequence: r, =, σ, (, Z, x, *, Z, y, ), Divide, (, n, Minus, 1, ) 150

假设你想记住以下公式序列：r, =, σ, (, Z, x, *, Z, y, ), Divide, (, n, Minus, 1, ) 150

Overall this formula is a good candidate for the link technique. Unfortunately there is the repetition of the “(“ twice and the “)” twice. This means that you may inadvertently jump from the first “(“ to the n, instead of the first Z.

总的来说，这个公式很适合使用链接技术。但遗憾的是，公式中重复出现了两次“（”和两次“）”。这意味着你可能会无意中从第一个“（”跳到n，而不是第一个Z。

When symbols are repeating and you are worried about confusing the order, I suggest labeling each with a color, so that all elements in the sequence are unique. This way your link between “σ” and “(“ might use a blue bracket and the Division with “(“

当符号重复出现，而您又担心顺序混乱时，我建议给每个符号都贴上颜色标签，这样序列中的所有元素都是唯一的。例如，连接“σ”和“(”的括号可以用蓝色表示，而除法符号可以用“(”表示。

might use a red bracket.

可能会用到红色括号。

Broken Links

失效链接

One failing of the link technique is that if one link in the sequence is broken, you can’t retrieve any of the following links. This is why I suggest keeping the sequences short to about 5-15 links maximum. Beyond that it is better to chunk the entire sequence into a series of smaller links.

链接技术的一个缺陷是，如果序列中的一个链接断开，就无法恢复后续的任何链接。因此，我建议将序列长度控制在 5-15 个链接以内。超过这个长度，最好将整个序列拆分成一系列较短的链接。

This way you might have a formula broken into three parts. Those three major sections would form a linked list of three and each major section would begin a new linked list containing 7 or 8 elements. This mental re-stitching can take extra time, however, so using it for every possible formula might not be advisable.

这样一来，公式可能被拆分成三个部分。这三个主要部分会构成一个包含三个元素的链表，而每个主要部分又会创建一个包含七八个元素的新链表。然而，这种重新组织公式的方法会耗费额外的时间，因此不建议对每个可能的公式都使用这种方法。

151

Indecipherable Symbols

无法解读的符号

As I mentioned earlier, the symbols need to have a clear description that is immediately obvious. If your symbols lack clarity, the linked list will fail. Some people who master the linking system begin to create there own shorthand, using symbols to represent common ideas, phrases or even syllables of words.

正如我之前提到的，符号必须有清晰明了的描述。如果符号不够清晰，链表就会失效。一些精通链表系统的人会开始创建自己的速记符号，用符号来表示常用概念、短语甚至单词的音节。

Lost Triggers

丢失的触发器

In some lists, you may want to add one additional link, a link between the first item and a trigger. With our grocery store example, how can you remember your linked list if you can’t think of the first object on that list? In this case you might want to associate the first object on the list with a trigger, say your bags you take the grocery store, or the storefront itself. On seeing the trigger you should be reminded of your first link and all the links following it.

在某些列表中，您可能需要添加一个额外的链接，即第一个项目与一个触发器之间的链接。以我们之前的超市购物示例为例，如果您记不住列表中的第一个对象，又该如何记住整个链表呢？在这种情况下，您可以将列表中的第一个对象与一个触发器关联起来，例如您去超市购物时携带的购物袋，或者超市门面本身。看到这个触发器后，您就能想起第一个链接以及它后面的所有链接。

The same method can be done with information for tests. Linking the fist item with an idea, say a formula with what it calculates or a list of principles with the theory they represent can be helpful in completing the linking process.

同样的方法也适用于考试信息。将第一项信息与某个概念联系起来，例如将公式与其计算结果联系起来，或者将原则列表与其所代表的理论联系起来，有助于完成关联过程。

152

Mind Challenge!

脑力挑战！

Learning the link method will probably take more time to master than the methods of the previous section. Try committing for an entire month to practice using various lists from your textbook or notes.

掌握链接方法可能比掌握上一节中的方法需要更多时间。建议你花整整一个月的时间，利用课本或笔记中的各种列表进行练习。

1) Pick a formula, list, group or any set of ideas that can be expressed in an ordered sequence.

1）选择一个公式、列表、分组或任何可以用有序顺序表达的想法集合。

2) Go through the above steps for creating a linked sequence, breaking it into a list, creating symbols and forming the proper links. Review your linked list to ensure all the ideas are vivid, repetition of symbols is minimal and the symbols are easily decipherable.

2) 按照上述步骤创建链表，将其拆分成列表，创建符号并建立正确的链接。检查你的链表，确保所有概念清晰明了，符号重复最少，且符号易于理解。

153

3) After your first week of the mind challenge, pick a random list from the previous week or weeks and attempt to go through it until you can reform the original formula, group or list.

3) 在完成第一周的思维挑战后，从前一周或前几周中随机选择一个列表，并尝试逐一分析，直到你能重新构建出原来的公式、分组或列表。

4) After the second week you may want to time yourself to improve your speed at using this method.

4）第二周后，你可能需要计时来提高使用这种方法的速度。

I am not a perfect master of the link method as I prefer the holistic linking methods of metaphor, visceralization and diagraming to these techniques where possible. Since other books have been written about the link technique, I recommend doing a Google or Amazon search to find more information if you want to go beyond the basics of linking.

我并非链接法的完美大师，因为我更倾向于使用整体性的链接方法，例如隐喻、具象化和图表绘制。由于已有其他书籍介绍过链接法，如果您想深入了解链接法的基础知识，我建议您在谷歌或亚马逊上搜索相关信息。

154

155

The Peg Method

钉板法

The peg method is similar to the link method, except it expands upon the basic idea. With the peg system, you store information attached to numbers, so you can recall any of the ideas without needing them to be in a specific sequence. The peg system can also be useful for linking together a series of numbers as in dates.

挂钩记忆法与链接记忆法类似，但它扩展了基本思路。使用挂钩记忆法，您可以将信息与数字关联起来，这样就可以随时回忆起任何信息，而无需遵循特定的顺序。挂钩记忆法也适用于将一系列数字（例如日期）关联起来。

With the peg system you aren’t linking a series of ideas with each other but with a specific numbered slot. I only use the peg system to record no more than a dozen items, however advanced versions of the peg system can store hundreds of items independent of any specific sequence. I’ll discuss these methods briefly, but I’ve found being able to store up to 12 items by pegging to be sufficient for learning most ideas.

使用挂钩系统，你不是将一系列想法彼此关联起来，而是将它们与特定的编号插槽关联起来。我只用挂钩系统记录不超过十几个项目，但高级版本的挂钩系统可以存储数百个项目，而且无需遵循任何特定顺序。我会简要讨论这些方法，但我发现，对于大多数概念的学习来说，用挂钩系统存储最多 12 个项目已经足够了。

The peg system is based off of creating symbols for the basic numbers. My implementation of the peg system uses rhyming words to easily store the numbers 0-12.

这个数字挂钩系统基于为基本数字创建符号。我实现的这个系统使用押韵的词语来轻松存储0到12的数字。

These can then be used as empty slots for storing concepts or steps in a process.

这些空间可以用作存储概念或流程步骤的空位。

0 - Hero

0 - 英雄

1 - Gun

1 - 枪

2 - Shoe

2 - 鞋子

3 - Tree

3 - 树

156

4 - Door

4 - 门

5 - Hive

5 - 蜂巢

6 - Sticks

6 - 棍子

7 - Heaven

7 - 天堂

8 - Plate

8 - 盘子

9 - Wine

9 - 葡萄酒

10 - Pen

10 - 笔

11 - Ribbon (I know, not quite a rhyme with eleven)

11 - 丝带（我知道，这和十一并不押韵）

12 - Oven (similar sounding to dozen)

12 - 烤箱（发音与“打”相似）

Once you get the numbers 0-12, you can

一旦你得到了0到12这几个数字，你就可以……

then associate any symbols that you need to

然后关联你需要的任何符号

peg to one of these thirteen slots. Forming a

将销钉插入这十三个插槽之一。形成一个

picture of a large bottle of wine fighting a

一张大酒瓶与……搏斗的图片

knife might cause me to associate the 9th slot

刀可能会让我联想到第九个槽位

with a knife (my symbol for Henry Fayol’s

用刀（我用来指代亨利·法约尔的符号）

principle of division of labor).

分工原则）。

With this sense you operate exactly as

有了这种感觉，你的操作就完全一样了。

you did with the link system, except you

你对链接系统做了些什么，除了你

157

associate each item not with the one before and after it in the sequence, but with a specific position on the numbers 0-12. This way if one link becomes broken, every other link can still be recalled easily. The only effort required is remembering your 0-12 rhyming symbols.

将每个项目与数字 0-12 上的特定位置关联起来，而不是与它在序列中的前后项目关联。这样，即使一个环节断开，其他环节仍然可以轻松回忆起来。你只需要记住 0-12 的押韵符号即可。

Using the Peg Method to Store Dates

使用挂钩法存储日期

I haven’t taken too many subjects that required

我没选修过太多需要这些科目的课程。

excessive date memorization, but from my brief

过度记忆日期，但从我的简短经历来看

experience, I’ve found the peg system to work well in storing numbers. Let’s say you wanted to link

根据我的经验，我发现用挂钩系统来存储数字效果很好。假设你想链接

Columbus’s discover of America to the date 1492.

从哥伦布发现美洲到1492年。

The first step would be to create your trigger that

第一步是创建触发器。

could store the event for the date in question. In our case this might be an image of a ship crashing onto a crudely drawn picture of North America.

可以存储指定日期发生的事件。在我们的例子中，这可能是一张船只撞击到一幅粗略绘制的北美洲地图的图片。

The next step would be to link the number 1, 4, 9

下一步是将数字 1、4 和 9 联系起来。

and then 2, to the date in question. So for us this would 158

然后是 2，也就是相关的日期。所以对我们来说，这将是 158。

mean first linking a picture of a gun to the trigger image. Perhaps an oversized pistol holding up poor ol’ Christopher as he crashes into North America? Next you would need to link gun and door, door with wine and finally wine with shoe. Then as you play back the sequence of links you could get the numbers 1, 4, 9 and 2 or 1492!

意思是先把枪的图片和扳机的图片关联起来。比如说，一把超大的手枪正指着可怜的克里斯托弗，而他正坠落到北美大陆？接下来，你需要把枪和门关联起来，门和酒关联起来，最后酒和鞋子关联起来。然后，当你回放这些关联序列时，你就能得到数字 1、4、9 和 2，或者 1492！

Advanced Pegging

高级钉子

An advanced form of using the peg technique involves associating a phonetic sound to each digit 0-9, rather than a rhyming image. You can then use the phonetic sound to form a series of words to store dozens, if not hundreds of numbers in a sequence instead of just a couple. I won’t go into this form of pegging, simply because I’ve found it to be unnecessary for more than party tricks.

更高级的记忆技巧是将数字0-9与一个发音联系起来，而不是与一个押韵的图像联系起来。这样，你就可以用这些发音组成一系列单词，从而按顺序存储几十个甚至几百个数字，而不仅仅是几个。我不会深入探讨这种记忆技巧，因为我发现它除了用来表演一些小把戏之外，并没有其他用途。

However, if you want to impress your friends with your ability to remember a string of hundreds of numbers, you might want to do a search looking for more information on this advanced form of the peg technique.

但是，如果你想用记住数百个数字的能力给朋友们留下深刻印象，你可能需要搜索一下有关这种高级数字记忆技巧的更多信息。
