Mind Challenge!

脑力挑战！

The peg method is built off of the link method, so do not start this Mind Challenge until you’ve completed the previous one for the link method. Here the goal is to familiarize yourself with the peg method and begin using it to store pegged lists of information and series of numeric information such as dates.

挂钩法建立在链接法的基础上，因此在完成链接法的挑战之前，请不要开始这个思维挑战。本挑战的目标是熟悉挂钩法，并开始使用它来存储信息列表和数字序列，例如日期。

1) Pick a list, group or date suitable for using the link method. Make sure it has no more than 13 items if you are trying to store a pegged list.

1）选择一个适合使用链接方法的列表、分组或日期。如果要存储关联列表，请确保其项目不超过 13 个。

2) Follow the steps for pegging until you can bring up any number in the list from 0-13 without needing to refer to the original source or other nodes on the list.

2) 按照步骤进行定位，直到您可以调出列表中 0-13 之间的任何数字，而无需参考原始来源或列表中的其他节点。

3) Repeat this exercise once a day for two weeks, after the first week spend some time trying to reform past dates or lists without referring to the source.

3）连续两周每天重复此练习一次，第一周结束后，花些时间尝试在不参考来源的情况下重新整理过去的日期或列表。

160

161

Information Compression

信息压缩

Information compression is another common method for storing large quantities of arbitrary information. The goal with information compression is to reduce the size of information so that it can be associated together in a logical way. I’ll explore three main ways of doing this: mnemonics, picture linking and notes reduction.

信息压缩是另一种存储大量任意信息的常用方法。信息压缩的目标是减少信息量，以便能够以逻辑方式将它们关联起来。我将探讨三种主要方法：记忆术、图像链接和笔记简化。

Mnemonics

记忆术

Mnemonics are devices that store several ideas together by using a phrase or word that can organize the

记忆术是一种利用短语或词语将多个概念组织在一起的记忆方法。

information. In first aid, one mnemonic for treating a bleeding injury is RED. Rest the injured area, Elevate the injured area and apply Direct pressure. Similar mnemonics have been used for centuries to store information.

信息。在急救中，处理出血伤口的一个记忆口诀是“RED”。即：休息（Rest the wound area）、抬高（Elevate the wound area）和施加直接压力（Applicance Direct Pressure）。类似的记忆口诀已经使用了几个世纪，用于记忆信息。

Using a mnemonic is as simple as collecting several ideas you want to compress together and picking a word or phrase you could use to organize them. Acronyms such as RED, NASA or USA are useful for storing several words or ideas under a single word.

使用记忆术很简单，只需收集几个想要归纳的想法，然后选择一个词或短语来组织它们即可。像 RED、NASA 或 USA 这样的首字母缩写词，可以将多个单词或想法用一个词来表示。

162

The best mnemonics have an easily identifiable word

最好的记忆术都包含一个易于识别的词语。

to store the ideas.

用来储存想法。

Picture Linking

图片链接

Picture linking can be seen as a cross between the link method and diagraming or visceralization. Here the goal is to link several ideas together by representing them in a single image, theme or concept. In my management class, I linked together the five forces model by creating a little doodle of the “five horsemen of the business apocalypse”. Each visually connected the ideas with the different parts of the original theory.

图片链接法可以看作是链接法和图表法或具象化方法的结合。其目标是通过单一图像、主题或概念将多个想法联系起来。在我的管理课上，我通过绘制“商业末日五骑士”的涂鸦，将五力模型串联起来。每幅涂鸦都以视觉化的方式将各个想法与原理论的不同部分联系起来。

Another way to use picture linking is to create one picture that combines several ideas together. Once you create a symbol to represent each idea, you put them all in the same vivid mental image.

另一种运用图像联想的方法是，将几个想法融合在一起，创造出一幅图像。先为每个想法创建一个符号，然后将它们全部整合到同一个生动的心理图像中。

I find picture linking works best if it is done on paper, creating small visual drawings to connect several ideas together at once. If done quickly, it can be faster than the link or peg method.

我发现，用纸笔绘制图片进行联想效果最好，通过绘制小型视觉图，一次性将几个想法联系起来。如果速度快，这种方法比链接或挂钩法更快。

163

Notes Compression

音符压缩

Notes compression is a useful way to get a grasp of a lot of material. By itself, it isn’t an entirely useful technique. But it can serve as the starting point for using other information compression techniques, linking,

笔记压缩是掌握大量资料的有效方法。它本身并不是一个完全有效的技术，但它可以作为使用其他信息压缩技术、链接等的起点。

pegging or holistic learning methods. The idea behind notes compression is taking a huge quantity of

循序渐进的学习方法或整体学习方法。笔记压缩背后的理念是提取大量信息。

information you need to learn, and reducing it to just a few pages of notes. Note compression allows for two things:

将你需要学习的信息精简到几页笔记中。笔记压缩可以带来两方面的好处：

1) It allows you to organize large amounts of information. Normally, it is difficult to take the hundreds of facts, concepts and ideas over the duration of a course and sort it fully. But if that information is represented on just two or three pages, it becomes easier to organize the ideas at the highest level.

1）它能帮助你整理大量信息。通常情况下，要把课程中数百个事实、概念和想法进行全面梳理是很困难的。但如果这些信息只用两三页纸就能呈现，那么从宏观层面组织思路就容易多了。

2) It allows for easier connections than would be previously possible. Looking at the entire structure of your subject can allow you to draw connections and link information that would be difficult to do from a zoomed-in perspective.

2）它使得建立联系比以往更容易。从整体结构来审视研究对象，可以帮助你发现并关联信息，而这些信息在局部视角下很难做到。

164

Steps to Compress Your Notes

压缩笔记的步骤

1) Give yourself several blank sheets of white paper. Take all the notes for the particular course or sub-unit you want to compress. This exercise can take an hour or two, so make sure you have the time.

1）准备几张空白的白纸。记下你想精简的特定课程或单元的所有笔记。这项练习可能需要一到两个小时，所以请确保你有足够的时间。

2) Starting with the smallest writing you can use, write down a major idea from your notes. Use as few words as possible.

2）从你能使用的最小字号开始，写下笔记中的一个主要观点。尽量用最少的文字。

3) Next to that idea, write a related idea, formula, concept or definition. Write the idea in small lettering and use few words as a description to save space.

3）在该想法旁边，写下一个相关的想法、公式、概念或定义。用小字书写，并用简短的词语进行描述，以节省空间。

4) Continue this process of writing ideas in a loose format, until you have written down, in reduced form, every major idea from your notes. You should end up with a 1-3 sheets of paper with densely written information.

4）继续以这种松散的格式记录想法，直到你用精简的形式写下笔记中的每一个主要想法。最终你应该得到1-3张纸，上面密密麻麻地写满了信息。

5) As an additional step, you may want to rewrite this page for better organization if your first attempt is difficult to sort through, or connections between the material are hard to see.

5）作为额外的步骤，如果您的第一次尝试难以理解，或者材料之间的联系难以看出，您可能需要重写此页面以更好地组织内容。

On the next page I have one half of a notes compression I did in a past course on statistics. This can help point out weaknesses and logically group ideas. Of course, you can compress notes from a fraction of a course or an entire topic, the scale is up to you.

下一页是我之前统计学课程笔记的精简版，只占一半。这有助于发现知识漏洞，并对概念进行逻辑归纳。当然，你可以精简课程的一部分内容，也可以精简整个主题的笔记，具体比例取决于你。

165

166

Mind Challenge!

脑力挑战！

This mind challenge should get you used to using information compression methods.

这项思维挑战应该能让你习惯使用信息压缩方法。

1) Once per day, go through your textbook or notes and pick out a group of facts you would like to compress. Then create either a mnemonic or picture linking to group the ideas under one theme.

1）每天浏览一次课本或笔记，挑选出一组你想精简的信息。然后，创建一个记忆口诀或图片，将这些信息归纳到一个主题下。

2) After doing this for two weeks, create a notes compression for the last two weeks of material, incorporating the various picture linking or mnemonics you used earlier.

2）两周后，对最后两周的学习材料进行笔记压缩，并结合你之前使用的各种图片链接或记忆技巧。

3) Test yourself to see if you can remember the entire group of ideas after using one of these methods to compress several ideas together. Keep doing this process for four weeks (2 notes compressions) or until you feel comfortable with using these methods quickly and easily.

3) 测试一下自己，看看在使用上述方法之一将几个想法压缩在一起后，是否还能记住所有想法。持续进行此过程四周（每次压缩两个笔记），或者直到您感觉能够快速轻松地使用这些方法为止。

167

Extending Ideas

拓展思路

Just passing the test isn’t enough. Having an A or A+ in your subjects isn’t important if you can’t use any of the information you’ve learned. The final stage in holistic learning is application. This is where you’ve not only understood and explored ideas, but you have tested, debugged and applied this knowledge.

仅仅通过考试是不够的。如果你无法运用所学知识，即使科目成绩是A或A+也毫无意义。全面学习的最后阶段是应用。在这个阶段，你不仅要理解和探索各种概念，还要检验、改进并应用这些知识。

Fully taking an idea from the acquiring to application stage isn’t always necessary to get a good grade. But the further you can take an idea along the learning process, the more useful and memorable it becomes. None of these extension ideas are original, but they are easily forgotten. By extending ideas beyond what you need to get a grade, hopefully you can learn something worthwhile.

要取得好成绩，并非一定要将一个想法从获取阶段完全应用到实际应用阶段。但是，你越能深入地探索一个想法，它就越有用，也越容易被记住。这些拓展思路并非原创，但它们很容易被遗忘。通过拓展思路，超越获得高分所需的范围，你或许能学到一些真正有价值的东西。

168

169

Practical Usage

实际应用

The best way to extend ideas you learn in courses is to apply the material in your practical life. This is rarely a problem with self-education or career-focused education.

将课堂上学到的知识运用到实际生活中，是拓展学习成果的最佳途径。这对于自学或以职业为导向的教育来说，通常不成问题。

However, if you need to take many abstract courses to work towards a degree, some of the information may seem unnecessary or at least not applicable for years into the future. By making the ideas practical, they are more likely to stick.

然而，如果你需要修读许多抽象课程才能获得学位，那么其中一些信息可能看起来不必要，或者至少在未来几年内都不适用。通过将这些概念付诸实践，它们更容易被记住。

Practical usage isn’t a step-by-step technique. It is a creative process of looking for unusual ways you can apply the ideas you are ingesting. Although you might not be sure how you can use your history or calculus class in daily life, I’m sure you could find some uses if you spent ten minutes doing a brainstorm.

实际应用并非按部就班的技巧，而是一个创造性的过程，需要你寻找运用所学知识的新颖方法。虽然你可能不确定如何在日常生活中运用历史或微积分知识，但我相信，如果你花十分钟进行头脑风暴，一定能找到一些用途。

Instead of giving steps, I’d like to share some ways I’ve been able to use different ideas in courses I’ve studied. Some of these are highly practical solutions, others are strictly internal solutions by applying abstract course material to my own life.

与其给出具体步骤，我更想分享一些我在学习课程中运用不同理念的方法。其中一些是极具实用性的解决方案，另一些则是纯粹的内在解决方案，即将抽象的课程内容应用到我的生活中。

1) Statistics - I used statistics courses to help decide the name of this book and the price to sell it at. Using Google AdWords, I ran an experiment testing a variety of names and prices. Statistics helped me pinpoint the significance of the sample size I found to see which should make it to the final product.

1）统计学——我运用统计学课程的知识来确定这本书的书名和定价。我利用谷歌广告（Google AdWords）进行了一项实验，测试了各种不同的书名和价格组合。统计学帮助我确定了样本量的显著性，从而最终确定了哪种组合最适合最终产品。

170

2) Computer Science - Aside from the obvious uses of programming, I’ve found computer science as a useful way of looking at problems. Debugging, algorithms, writing out procedures and organization are all useful skills that can be applied elsewhere.

2）计算机科学——除了编程的显而易见的用途之外，我发现计算机科学也是一种看待问题的有效方法。调试、算法、编写程序和组织结构都是可以应用到其他领域的实用技能。

3) Accounting - Taking accounting courses helped me sort out my personal finances and income statements. Applying the basic accounting principles to my finances made them easier to read and understand.

3）会计——学习会计课程帮助我理清了个人财务状况和损益表。将基本的会计原则应用到我的财务报表中，使它们更容易阅读和理解。

4) Economics - Economics helped me reevaluate how I look at money in society.

4）经济学——经济学帮助我重新评估了我对社会中金钱的看法。

By viewing it as a medium for exchanging value, I changed much of my philosophy for how money, the economy and world issues function.

通过将金钱视为交换价值的媒介，我改变了我对金钱、经济和世界问题运作方式的许多看法。

5) History - History can be a tool for understanding the present. Learning about ancient Asian history helped me when trying to look at issues facing modern China, India and Japan. History provides me with a context for understanding world issues.

5）历史——历史是理解当下的工具。学习古代亚洲历史帮助我理解现代中国、印度和日本面临的问题。历史为我理解世界问题提供了背景。

These are just a few examples, but I strive to make use of anything I can learn in subjects. If a course has absolutely no merit in daily life, what is the point of taking it?

以上仅举几例，但我力求将所学知识运用到实践中。如果一门课程对日常生活毫无用处，那学习它的意义何在呢？

171

Mind Challenge!

脑力挑战！

Once a week for the next two months, pick one of your major courses. Spend at least 5-10 minutes creating a list of ways you can use this information in your daily life.

接下来的两个月，每周抽出一天时间，选择你的一门主修课程。至少花5-10分钟时间，列出你可以在日常生活中运用这些知识的方法。

Make sure the list has at least 20 ideas and don’t censor yourself in letting them flow.

确保清单上至少有 20 个想法，并且不要限制自己，让想法自由流淌。

After you’re done this weekly exercise, pick one of those ideas and implement it.

完成本周练习后，选择其中一个想法并付诸实践。

172

173

Model Debugging

模型调试

Model debugging is a fancy name for a simple concept: practice. Practicing questions and testing yourself is the only way you can get rid of errors in the holistic learning process. You can’t debug a computer program easily without actually running it and looking for errors. Similarly, you can’t debug your brain without testing it against questions and homework from your studies.

模型调试其实就是一个简单的概念：练习。练习题目并进行自我测试是消除整体学习过程中错误的唯一途径。你不可能在不实际运行并查找错误的情况下调试计算机程序。同样，你也不可能在不通过练习题和作业来检验自己的学习成果的情况下调试自己的大脑。

If you do the holistic learning process well, spending hours each day debugging shouldn’t be necessary. Just like a skilled programmer can write more code with fewer errors, having the right skills in place from the beginning should reduce the time you spend practicing. Still, perfection is impossible, so taking the time to practice and debug your understanding is always a good idea.

如果你能有效地进行整体学习，就不需要每天花费数小时进行调试。就像熟练的程序员能编写出更多错误更少的代码一样，从一开始就掌握正确的技能也能减少你练习的时间。当然，完美是不可能的，所以花时间练习和调试你的理解始终是有益的。

Since you probably already know how to set up and do practice questions and homework, I won’t repeat the obvious. But here are a few tips for improving the model-debugging process:

既然你可能已经知道如何设置和完成练习题和作业，我就不再赘述了。但这里有一些改进模型调试过程的技巧：

# ↩

1) Separate Typos From Concept Errors

1）区分拼写错误和概念错误

I’m sure most computer programmers are used to occasionally failing to compile 174

我相信大多数程序员都习惯了偶尔编译失败的情况。

because they mistyped a key word. Worse is spending twenty minutes tracking down a bug because you used the wrong variable in an innocent mistake. But if you don’t understand how a fundamental concept or algorithm should work, this is a far more serious problem.

因为他们输错了一个关键词。更糟糕的是，你可能因为无意中用错了变量，花了二十分钟去追踪一个bug。但如果你不理解一个基本概念或算法的运作方式，那问题就严重得多。

The same applies to your own model debugging. When you get questions wrong, you need to separate simple errors that can easily be fixed, from those that represent a failure to understand key ideas. In the case of simple errors, just repeat a new question and learn from it. In the case of concept errors, go back to your models, metaphors and visceralizations to see if you made mistakes in the reasoning process.

这同样适用于你自己的模型调试。当你做错题时，你需要区分容易修正的简单错误和那些反映出你对关键概念理解不足的错误。对于简单错误，只需重复做一道新题并从中学习即可。对于概念错误，则需要回顾你的模型、比喻和直观理解，看看你的推理过程是否出现了偏差。

2) The Shotgun Approach

2）广撒网式方法

Spending hours repeating the same type of questions is no different from rote memorization. I prefer to spend my time debugging on a shotgun approach, which tackles a few questions of each type, but doesn’t become repetitive. I feel if you must spend hours repeating a question, then do it. But a better solution is to use the holistic learning methods earlier, so remembering how to solve certain problems become easier.

花几个小时重复做同一种类型的问题，和死记硬背没什么区别。我更喜欢用“广撒网”的方式调试问题，每种类型的问题都做几个，这样就不会显得重复。我觉得如果你非要花几个小时重复做某个问题，那就去做吧。但更好的办法是尽早运用整体学习方法，这样就能更容易地记住如何解决某些问题。

175

3) Spread Practice Times Out

3）拉开练习时间

Split your practice sessions into daily intervals, rather than pre-test crash sessions.

将练习时间分成每天的固定时段，而不是考前集中练习。

A quick refresh each day will be more likely to stick than a huge download into your brain the night before.

每天快速复习一下比前一天晚上一次性把大量知识灌输到大脑里更容易记住。

Quick Tip!

小贴士！

Practicing questions repeatedly is a slow way to learn. Model debugging is necessary, but if you need to do the same types of questions repeatedly, chances are you need more work on the exploring or understanding phases. If you feel you don't quite understand a topic, try going back and exploring the ideas.

反复练习题目是一种缓慢的学习方法。模型调试固然必要，但如果你需要反复练习同类型的题目，很可能说明你需要在探索或理解阶段投入更多精力。如果你觉得自己对某个主题理解不够透彻，不妨回过头来仔细研究一下相关的概念。

176

Mind Challenge!

脑力挑战！

If you are already doing regular practice sessions for questions in your classes, continue with what you are doing. Try to implement some of these ideas for improving how you practice, but otherwise keep testing yourself. If you aren’t doing regular practice sessions, or you are doing crash sessions before a test, try spreading your learning out over the entire term. Spend a few minutes each day instead of hours before the test.

如果你已经有针对课堂题目的定期练习习惯，那就继续保持。尝试运用一些改进练习方法的建议，但除此之外，还要继续进行自我测试。如果你没有定期练习，或者只是在考试前临时抱佛脚，那就尝试将学习时间分散到整个学期。每天花几分钟练习，而不是考前几个小时。

177

178

Project Based Learning

基于项目的学习

Project-based learning is my favorite technique for self-education. While going to this level of depth is probably unnecessary for most formal schooling, it can be useful when you don’t have an instructor or a final exam.

项目式学习是我最喜欢的自学方法。虽然对于大多数正规教育来说，深入到这种程度可能没有必要，但当你没有老师或期末考试时，它会非常有用。

Project-based learning simply means constructing a 1-3 month project that will force you to learn. In order to complete the project, you must know more than you do.

项目式学习简单来说就是设计一个为期1-3个月的项目，旨在促使你学习新知识。为了完成这个项目，你必须掌握比现在更多的知识。

Taking on a project will drive you to learn as you go, pushing any new ideas right through every step of the holistic learning process.

承担一个项目会让你在过程中不断学习，并将任何新想法贯穿于整体学习过程的每一步。

Taking on a 1-3 month project can be a little daunting, but if you are interested in really knowing a subject, I believe it is the best way to learn quickly. As with the last two methods for extending ideas, this one doesn’t have a step-by-step formula. But here are some examples you might want to follow for learning different subjects: 1) Computer Programming - Design a project that will take you 1-3 months of work to complete. This could be a small application, a website or game.

承担一个为期 1-3 个月的项目可能会让人有些畏惧，但如果你真的想深入了解某个主题，我认为这是快速学习的最佳途径。与前两种拓展思路的方法一样，这种方法也没有固定的步骤。不过，以下是一些你可以参考的学习不同主题的例子：1）计算机编程——设计一个需要 1-3 个月才能完成的项目。它可以是一个小型应用程序、一个网站或一个游戏。

2) History - Write a short e-book about the historical subject you want to study.

2）历史——写一本关于你想研究的历史主题的简短电子书。

Write one that will get you to do research as well as create your own thesis.

写一篇能让你进行研究并形成自己论文的文章。

179

3) Financial Accounting - Pick several companies and do a complete analysis of their financial statements before deciding who you would invest money in.

3）财务会计——选择几家公司，对其财务报表进行全面分析，然后再决定投资哪家公司。

Before you start designing a project to encourage your self-education, here are some tips I’ve found useful when running my own projects: 1) Keep it Small. A project should push your abilities forward, but massive, year-long adventures can start to drag after several months. If learning is your goal, keep the projects within a few months.

在你开始设计一个旨在促进自学的项目之前，以下是我在开展项目时总结的一些实用技巧：1）保持项目规模小。项目应该能够提升你的能力，但规模庞大、耗时一年的项目在几个月后可能会变得拖沓。如果你的目标是学习，那么最好将项目控制在几个月以内。

2) Write it Down. Commit to your project on paper, otherwise it won’t last. I don’t recommend committing to projects if you seriously doubt your motivation is strong enough to last. However, written documents can help you stay focused if you feel frustrated or bored by the next immediate activity.

2）写下来。把你的项目计划写下来，否则它不会持久。如果你严重怀疑自己的动力是否足够强大，我不建议你贸然投入项目。但是，如果你对眼前的任务感到沮丧或厌倦，书面文件可以帮助你保持专注。

3) Create an Objective Outcome. Just working on a project isn’t always enough.

3）设定目标结果。仅仅埋头做项目并不总是足够的。

I’ve found my learning efforts work best if there is a clear goal at the end of the project.

我发现，如果项目结束时有一个明确的目标，我的学习效果就会最好。

If the project serves a function beyond just learning, you can boost your motivation towards continuing it.

如果项目除了学习之外还有其他功能，就能提高你继续下去的动力。

180

Mind Challenge!

脑力挑战！

Design a project that you expect to take one month to accomplish. Examples could include:

设计一个预计需要一个月才能完成的项目。例如：

-E-book

电子书

-Program

-程序

-Invention

-发明

-Website

-网站

-Design

-设计

-Blog

-博客

The project should be simple, but have a sharp learning curve. Write out your deadline for completion and schedule a bit of time each day to work on this project.

项目应该简单易上手，但学习曲线要陡峭。设定完成截止日期，并每天安排一些时间来完成这个项目。

After you’ve finished the project do a review of the project-based learning method and decide what other projects you might like to tackle.

项目完成后，回顾一下项目式学习方法，并决定你可能还想尝试哪些其他项目。

181

Review of Holistic

整体性回顾

Learning Techniques

学习技巧

Theory and technique are equal parts to the holistic learning strategy. With just the theory, it is difficult to put holistic learning into practice. With just the techniques, any methods you use will be haphazard and random at best.

理论与技巧对于整体学习策略而言同等重要。仅凭理论难以将整体学习付诸实践；而仅凭技巧，你所使用的任何方法充其量也只能是杂乱无章、毫无章法的。

These techniques just represent a small minority of the total ways you can learn. I encourage you to find other methods and incorporate them into your approach. Use what works best for you and discard everything else until you find a pattern that works.

这些技巧只是众多学习方法中的一小部分。我鼓励你寻找其他方法，并将它们融入到你的学习方法中。选择最适合你的方法，并不断尝试其他方法，直到找到有效的模式。

Practice is essential for making use of these holistic learning methods. That is why I have created a Mind Challenge for each of the different methods. The purpose of these challenges is to focus you on practicing one technique long enough for it to become a habit. Just reading about these ideas isn’t enough if you can’t use them automatically in your studies.

练习对于运用这些整体学习方法至关重要。因此，我为每种方法都设计了一项思维挑战。这些挑战旨在帮助你专注于练习某一项技巧，并使其养成习惯。如果你无法在学习中自然而然地运用这些方法，仅仅阅读相关理论是不够的。

182

Completing all of the challenges would take close to two years and might not be feasible for the immediate future. I suggest that you pick only one challenge to work on in the next month or two. Base your decision on which method you would to turn into a habit. If your obstacles are in understanding concepts, you might want to practice metaphor. If you can’t handle the volume of dates and definitions, linking or pegging might be a better method to master.

完成所有挑战需要近两年时间，短期内可能不太现实。我建议你选择一项挑战，在接下来的一两个月内集中精力攻克。选择哪项挑战取决于你想养成哪种习惯。如果你的障碍在于理解概念，不妨尝试运用比喻。如果你难以处理大量的日期和定义，那么链接或关联或许是更适合掌握的方法。

The holistic learning theory should help you pinpoint where you might want to improve. From that point, you can determine which techniques would improve on that weak point. By finally moving that technique from a tool, which requires effort to use, to a habit which happens automatically, you can improve the way you learn information.

整体学习理论可以帮助你精准定位需要改进的地方。从那里出发，你可以确定哪些技巧可以弥补这一弱点。最终，通过将这些技巧从需要付出努力才能使用的工具转变为一种自动发生的习惯，你就能改进学习信息的方式。

Included with this e-book are several documents for practicing some of the techniques mentioned in the book. You can use these documents to help you get started with your practicing sessions.

这本电子书附带了一些练习书中提到的技巧的文档。你可以利用这些文档来帮助你开始练习。

183

第三部分

Beyond Holistic

超越整体性

Learning

学习

185

The Productive Student

高效学生

Throughout this book I’ve emphasized “Learn More”. Holistic learning expands your ability to handle difficult subjects, raising the upper limit for how well you can understand your classes. Learning holistically will help improve your grades and understanding, but it probably won’t shave off huge amounts of studying time. The new methods can take a few weeks to master, so the time-saving benefits are long-term.

本书中我一直强调“多学习”。整体学习法能拓展你应对复杂学科的能力，提高你对课程理解的上限。整体学习有助于提升你的成绩和理解力，但可能不会大幅节省学习时间。掌握新的学习方法需要几周时间，因此节省时间的益处是长期的。

Now I’d like to focus on the other half of this books title, “Study Less”. Becoming a productive student or self-learner is the art of cutting down the amount of time you spend in the books. During school, I have time to run this business, write as much as 7000 words each week, exercise and run a Toastmasters club on top of full-time classes.

现在我想重点谈谈这本书标题的另一半——“少学习”。成为一名高效的学生或自学者，关键在于减少花在书本上的时间。在校期间，除了全日制课程之外，我还有时间经营自己的事业，每周写作多达7000字，锻炼身体，并运营一个Toastmasters演讲俱乐部。

Despite this schedule, I still have time to spend time with friends and enjoy weekends.

尽管日程安排很紧，但我仍然有时间与朋友们相聚，享受周末时光。

Here are the key ideas for becoming more productive as a student: 1) Energy Management

以下是提高学生学习效率的关键要点：1）能量管理

4) Batch

4）批次

2) Don't “Study”

2）不要“学习”

5) Get Organized

5）做好准备

3) End Procrastination

3）停止拖延

186

Productivity Tip #1

提高效率小技巧#1

Manage Your Energy

管理你的能量

I’ve seen the victims of poor energy management. These are the students completely burnt out from excess projects, requiring injections of caffeine just to function. Balancing courses and life isn’t easy, especially if you have a full schedule.

我见过一些因精力管理不善而受害的学生。他们因为过多的项目而筋疲力尽，需要靠咖啡因才能勉强维持运转。平衡课程和生活并不容易，尤其是在日程安排非常紧凑的情况下。

Your body has fuel cells, both physically and mentally. You can’t run on empty forever. If you try to cheat your body into giving a few extra hours today, it can mean a dozen lost hours next week. If you’ve been struggling to cope with burnout, stress and exhaustion, you haven’t been managing your energy.

你的身体拥有能量储备，包括生理和心理能量。你不可能永远处于能量耗尽的状态。如果你今天试图欺骗身体多工作几个小时，下周可能就意味着损失十几个小时。如果你一直饱受倦怠、压力和疲惫的困扰，那就说明你没有有效地管理自己的能量。

Better energy management has two steps:

更好的能源管理包括两个步骤：

1) Increase your energy capacity.

1）提高你的能量容量。

2) Switch your schedule from a linear format to a circular format.

2）将你的日程安排从线性格式改为循环格式。

187

Increasing Your Energy

提升你的能量

Energy isn’t just a genetic gift. There are many things you can do to boost the amount of force you can give towards your work. Here are a few things to consider: 1) Do you exercise 3-5 times per week? If the answer is no, you’re undercutting your potential energy levels. Unless you’re unable to exercise for medical reasons, there is no excuse for not getting your 40 minutes a day. A small investment in exercise can have a huge impact on your ability to concentrate and work quickly.

精力并非完全取决于基因。你可以通过多种方式提升工作效率。以下几点值得考虑：1）你每周锻炼3-5次吗？如果答案是否定的，那么你的精力水平就受到了限制。除非你因健康原因无法锻炼，否则没有理由不每天锻炼40分钟。哪怕只是在锻炼上投入一点时间，也能极大地提升你的专注力和工作效率。

2) Do you get 7-8 hours of sleep each night? Some people work best on 4-5 hours of sleep. But I’m willing to bet neither of us can do that. Pulling an all-nighter is a dangerous move when you need to keep your mind sharp.

2）你每晚能睡7-8个小时吗？有些人睡4-5个小时就能保持最佳状态。但我敢打赌，我们俩都做不到。熬夜对保持头脑清醒来说非常危险。

3) What do you eat? Do you eat a diet high in meat, fat and sugar? Switch to a diet that emphasizes whole grains and unprocessed foods. This will keep your blood sugar levels even throughout the day, avoiding the highs and lows.

3）你平时吃什么？你的饮食中肉类、脂肪和糖分含量很高吗？不妨改吃以全谷物和未加工食品为主的食物。这样可以保持你全天血糖水平稳定，避免血糖忽高忽低。

4) How many glasses of water do you drink each day? You are over two-thirds water. Dehydrating yourself is a quick way to zap your energy.

4）你每天喝多少杯水？你体内超过三分之二都是水。脱水会迅速消耗你的精力。

188

5) What meals do you eat each day? If your answer is lunch, dinner and sometimes breakfast, you’re energy levels will suffer. Ideally, you should eat 4-5 smaller meals throughout the day to ensure a more constant supply of nutrients. Eating a bit right before bed can also help with morning grogginess by avoiding low-blood sugar when you wake up.

5）你每天吃哪些餐？如果你每天只吃午餐、晚餐，偶尔吃早餐，你的精力就会受到影响。理想情况下，你应该一天吃4-5顿少食多餐，以确保营养摄入更加稳定。睡前吃点东西也有助于避免醒来时血糖过低，从而缓解早晨的昏昏沉沉。

Circular Scheduling

循环调度

A linear schedule has work spread evenly over the entire time period. A circular schedule focuses on doing a lot of work earlier with ample rest time afterwards.

线性日程安排将工作均匀地分配到整个时间段内。循环日程安排则侧重于前期完成大量工作，之后留出充足的休息时间。

Keeping a circular schedule helps your body keep up a rhythm of high productivity instead of a death march. Here are few ways to make your schedule more circular: 1) Set a day off each week. I take one day off every week where I don’t do any schoolwork. Compressing seven days of work into six might seem difficult at first, but taking a day off prevents burnout.

保持循环作息有助于身体维持高效的节奏，而不是陷入疲惫不堪的状态。以下是一些让你的作息更循环的方法：1）每周安排一天休息。我每周都会休息一天，不做任何学习上的事情。把七天的工作压缩到六天可能一开始会觉得很难，但休息一天可以防止过度劳累。

2) Evenings off. Compress all your work into the morning. Instead of taking breaks throughout the day, get your work done early so you can have a few hours off each night.

2）晚上休息。把所有工作都集中在早上完成。不要在白天断断续续地休息，而是早点完成工作，这样你每天晚上就能有几个小时的休息时间。

189

3) 90 minute timeboxes. Set aside 90 minutes towards a project or studying. After the ninety minutes is complete, you stop working. Timeboxing can help you keep your studying time focused.

3）90分钟时间盒。设定90分钟的时间段用于项目或学习。90分钟结束后，就停止工作。时间盒可以帮助你保持学习时间的专注。

Quick Tip!

小贴士！

One of the best books on the subject of energy management is

关于能源管理主题的最佳书籍之一是

The Power of Full Engagement . Although I've briefly touched on the subject, this book can give far more depth. The book divides up energy into four categories and gives more advice for how to maximize your energy and work within cycles. A must-read for anyone serious about enhancing their productivity.

全身心投入的力量。虽然我之前只是略微提及过这个主题，但这本书能提供更深入的见解。书中将能量分为四类，并就如何最大限度地利用能量以及如何在周期内高效工作提出了更多建议。对于任何认真想要提高工作效率的人来说，这本书都是必读之作。

190

Productivity Tip #2

提高效率小技巧之二

Don’t “Study”

不要“学习”

I never study. I’ll read my textbooks. I’ll review notes. I’ll finish assignments and do practice questions. But I never “study”. A big waste of your time is to spend time

我从不“学习”。我会读课本，复习笔记，完成作业，做练习题。但我从不“学习”。把时间浪费在学习上是最大的浪费。

“studying” without specifically defining what you want to accomplish. At the end of the year, grades, not how many hours you “studied” are going to matter most.

只是“学习”，却不明确定义你想达成的目标。到了年底，最重要的不是你“学习”了多少小时，而是你的成绩。

Cal Newport, author of How to Win at College, claims he hates the word studying:

《如何在大学取得成功》一书的作者卡尔·纽波特声称他讨厌“学习”这个词：

“It’s ambiguous, and for most students it’s entangled in all sorts of emotional baggage. They feel guilty if they haven’t suffered enough in the library. Student life, for them, becomes a constant struggle — always trying to “study” more, yet always falling a bit short. It’s a lot like dieting. But with less involvement from Kirstie Alley.”1

“这很模糊，对大多数学生来说，它牵扯着各种各样的情感包袱。如果他们在图书馆里不够努力，就会感到内疚。对他们来说，学生生活变成了一场持续的斗争——总是试图“学习”更多，却总是差那么一点点。这很像节食。只不过没有柯丝蒂·艾利（Kirstie Alley）的参与。”¹

1. Cal Newport: “Studying with Kirstie Alley, Decoding the Quarter System, and Coping with Early Classes”, http://calnewport.com/blog/?p=258

1. 卡尔·纽波特：“与柯斯蒂·艾利一起学习、解读学季制以及如何应对早课”，http://calnewport.com/blog/?p=258

191

Instead of studying, define the activities you need to perform in order to learn the material. For myself these are the activities I need to do in order to get an A or A+ in most classes:

与其死记硬背，不如明确你需要做哪些活动才能真正掌握学习内容。就我个人而言，为了在大多数课程中拿到A或A+，我需要做以下这些活动：

1) Read the chapters covered

1）阅读已涵盖的章节

2) Complete assignments and take notes in class

2）完成作业并做好课堂笔记

3) Use some of the holistic learning methods to tackle trouble spots.

3）运用一些整体学习方法来解决难点。

4) Optionally take a set of flow-based notes for the material covered before tests.

4） （可选）在考试前，对所学内容进行流程笔记。

That’s it. My list has been narrowed down by doing as much learning in-class as possible, so your list might have more items. The point isn’t that I have a short list, but that I have made a list in the first place. Unless you itemize what you need to do in order to learn, you’ll waste endless hours “studying” instead of optimizing your time to actually learn.

就是这样。我的清单是通过尽可能多地在课堂上学习而精简的，所以你的清单可能包含更多项目。重点不在于我的清单短，而在于我首先列出了清单。除非你把学习需要做的事情逐一列出，否则你会浪费无数时间“学习”，而不是真正有效地利用时间去学习。

192

Productivity Tip #3

提高效率小技巧#3

Nuke Procrastination

核拖延症

If an assignment is due next Wednesday are you the type of person who starts working on it:

如果作业下周三就要交了，你是那种会马上开始做的人吗？

(A) As soon as it is assigned.

（A）一旦分配。

(B) All in one session, some time between today and the due date.

（B）一次性完成，在今天到截止日期之间的某个时间。

(C) Tuesday night.

（C）周二晚上。

(D) Wednesday morning, ten minutes before class!

（D）星期三早上，上课前十分钟！

Unfortunately, most students I know would have to pick either C or D. Which is the best answer? It may surprise you that I don’t believe answering A is ideal either. As I’ll explain, beating procrastination doesn’t mean just completing work earlier.

不幸的是，我认识的大多数学生都只能选择C或D。那么，哪个才是最佳答案呢？或许你会惊讶，我认为A也不是理想的选择。正如我将要解释的，克服拖延症并不意味着仅仅意味着提前完成作业。

193

The correct answer (in most cases) would actually be B. Completing an assignment in one go saves time by batching. In addition, if you complete the assignment using the Weekly/Daily Goals method, you can save yourself the stress and guilt of deciding when to do assignments.

正确答案（大多数情况下）应该是 B。一次性完成作业可以节省时间，因为它可以集中处理任务。此外，如果您使用每周/每日目标法来完成作业，就可以避免决定何时完成作业的压力和内疚感。

Weekly/Daily Goals System

每周/每日目标系统

The W/D Goals method is one of the best ways I know of to combat procrastination. The idea is simple:

W/D目标法是我所知的对抗拖延症的最佳方法之一。它的理念很简单：

1) At the end of each week, compile a list of all the assignments, homework, reading and studying activities you want to do in the following week.

1）每周结束时，列出你下周要完成的所有作业、家庭作业、阅读和学习活动。

Unless something unexpected arises during the week, you are obligated to finish this list–but no more than this list. This splits off the endless amount of assignments and work you could be doing into a manageable chunk of one week. If you have a particularly busy week, you might hold-off on long-term assignments. If you have a lighter week, you might get ahead on reading for tests far before the date.

除非本周出现意外情况，否则你必须完成这份清单上的任务——但不能超过清单上的内容。这样可以将你原本可能堆积如山的作业和工作拆分成一周内可以完成的部分。如果你这周特别忙，可以暂时搁置一些长期任务。如果这周比较轻松，你可以提前预习考试内容。

194

2) At the end of each day, check your weekly to-do and create a daily goals list.

2）每天结束时，检查你的每周待办事项，并制定每日目标清单。

The next step is to break down your weekly work over each day. That’s six days of work (assuming you’re taking a rest day). You’re obligated to finish this list each day, but no more than this list.

下一步是将你一周的工作分解到每一天。这相当于六天的工作量（假设你休息一天）。你必须每天完成这份清单上的任务，但不能超出清单。

What does the W/D Goals system accomplish?

W/D目标系统实现了什么目标？

1) It saves you the stress of deciding whether to work more or less on a day. You just check your list to see whether you’re done.

1）它省去了你决定当天工作量多少的压力。你只需查看清单，看看是否完成了工作即可。

2) It keeps you from procrastinating on big projects. By relying on your weekly and daily goals lists, instead of due dates, you are the one in control over your schedule.

2）它可以防止你拖延大型项目。通过依靠每周和每日目标清单，而不是截止日期，你可以掌控自己的日程安排。

3) It helps you balance workloads. By looking ahead at your schedule you can adapt your weekly and daily goals to smooth over your work. Instead of pulling all-nighters before a test, and wasting hours of your time three weeks before, you can split up the work.

3) 它能帮助你平衡工作量。通过提前查看日程安排，你可以调整每周和每日目标，从而更有效地完成工作。与其在考试前熬夜，或者提前三周就浪费大量时间，不如将工作分摊到各个阶段。

195

Here is a sample of the weekly/daily

以下是每周/每日的示例

goals lists I maintain:

我维护的目标清单：

I use TadaList, which is an online to-do list program for storing my

我使用 TadaList，这是一个在线待办事项清单程序，用来存储我的待办事项。

lists. Checking my Daily Goals

清单。查看我的每日目标

regularly and my Weekly Goals

定期以及我的每周目标

each night, helps me stay on track.

每晚都帮助我保持专注。

196

Productivity Tip #4

提高效率小技巧#4

Batching

批量处理

Batching involves taking a group of similar, small sections of work and doing them at one time. Batching helps cut down studying time because you can focus completely instead of switching between tasks.

批量学习是指将一组相似的、小的任务集中起来一次性完成。批量学习有助于减少学习时间，因为你可以完全专注于一项任务，而无需在不同任务之间切换。

Between both schoolwork and writing, I use batching in many places. I might do all my required reading for each week at one time, or I might write 3-4 articles in a row.

无论是学业还是写作，我都会在很多方面采用批量处理的方式。比如，我可能会一次性完成每周的所有阅读任务，或者连续写三四篇文章。

Here are some tips to add batching to your productivity system: 1) Size matters. Batching works best when collecting small sections of work together. You can’t “batch” your entire course for the day before a final exam.

以下是一些将批量处理融入你的效率系统的技巧：1）规模很重要。批量处理最适合将小块工作集中起来完成。你不可能把整门课程的内容都“批量”到期末考试前一天完成。

Batching will have a negative impact if you take it beyond 3-5 hour sessions of work.

如果每次工作时间超过 3-5 小时，批量处理会产生负面影响。

197

2) One-Off Assignments. If an assignment takes me less than 8 hours of work, I usually try to accomplish it in one sitting. Splitting up a 3 hour essay over 15 sessions can add hours of wasted time as you slowly build up momentum in your writing.

2）一次性作业。如果一项作业耗时不到 8 小时，我通常会尽量一次性完成。把一篇 3 小时的论文分成 15 次完成，会浪费大量时间，因为你需要慢慢积累写作节奏。

3) Build Your Concentration Threshold. Your concentration threshold is the amount of time you can focus on a task before your productivity takes a nosedive. By taking on larger batches of tasks, you can slowly expand your threshold. Having a high threshold is helpful because it means you can batch large sections of work.

3）提高你的专注阈值。专注阈值是指你在工作效率骤降之前能够集中精力完成一项任务的时间。通过一次性处理更多任务，你可以逐步提高你的专注阈值。拥有较高的专注阈值很有帮助，因为这意味着你可以集中处理大块的工作。

Productivity Tip #5

提高效率小技巧#5

Be Organized

保持条理

Being organized will not get you A’s. I’ve known A+ students who have horrible organization skills and C students with flawless systems. Being organized can help with your productivity and learning, but don’t assume that all your problems have disorganization at their root.

做事有条理并不一定会让你得A。我认识一些成绩A+的学生，他们的组织能力很差；也认识一些成绩C的学生，他们的组织系统却完美无缺。做事有条理确实能提高你的效率和学习效果，但不要以为你所有的问题都是由缺乏条理造成的。

If you haven’t already, here are the key steps necessary for staying organized: 1) Everything has a home. Tasks, assignments and due dates all get stored in a proper location. Mess is the result of the homeless. Devise a place to put everything, and it will be a lot easier to stay ordered.

如果你还没做到，以下是保持井然有序的关键步骤：1）每样东西都有它固定的位置。任务、作业和截止日期都应该存放在合适的地方。杂乱无章是无家可归的结果。为每样东西都找到合适的存放位置，保持整洁就会容易得多。

199

2) Carry a notepad with you at all times. Keep something to write on at all times of the day. This is invaluable for writing down tasks, due dates or ideas.

2）随时携带记事本。一天中任何时候都不要忘记带上纸笔。这对于记录任务、截止日期或想法都非常有帮助。

3) Maintain a calendar and a to-do list. Use to-do lists to store tasks and projects.

3）维护日历和待办事项清单。使用待办事项清单来存储任务和项目。

Use your calendar to store events and due dates.

使用日历记录事件和截止日期。

Even though being organized isn't a cure-all solution, it can definitely help.

虽然保持条理并非万能的解决办法，但它肯定会有所帮助。

Organization skills can make it far easier to be productive, while eliminating stress.

良好的组织能力可以大大提高工作效率，同时消除压力。

Quick Tip!

小贴士！

If you're struggling with poor organizing habits, I recommend readi ng Zen To Done , b y Leo Babauta. This book focuses on the hardest part of getting organized—turning those skills into habits.

如果你正苦于糟糕的整理习惯，我推荐你读一下利奥·巴布塔的《禅意整理》（Zen To Done）。这本书着重讲解整理中最难的部分——如何将这些技巧转化为习惯。

Babauta creates a simple framework for staying organized and getting work done.

Babauta 创建了一个简单的框架，帮助人们保持条理并完成工作。

200

201

Educate Yourself

自我提升

Holistic learning doesn’t just apply to the classroom, but in your personal life. In fact, I’ve found that actively engaging in self-education improves you ability to learn in a formal setting. Picking subjects that interest you and pursuing them in your spare time can be incredibly rewarding.

全面学习不仅适用于课堂，也适用于你的个人生活。事实上，我发现积极参与自主学习能够提升你在正规学习环境中的学习能力。选择你感兴趣的科目，并在空闲时间深入学习，会带来意想不到的收获。

However, self-education comes with its own unique challenges. Without the structure of school, it is harder to maintain a focus, find resources and test your understanding. Despite the expense and inefficiencies of taking classes, they can offer you guided instruction along with a letter grade to tell you your performance.

然而，自学也面临着其独特的挑战。没有学校的体系支撑，就更难保持专注、找到学习资源以及检验自己的理解程度。尽管上课费用高昂且效率不高，但学校可以提供指导，并以等级评定来反映你的学习表现。

I’ve been actively engaged in self-education for as long as I can remember. I’ve taught myself skills like computer programming, web-design and writing. I’ve also learned subjects from world religions to evolutionary psychology without ever having taking a formal course. I’d like to present some of the ideas I’ve found useful in self-education that you might want to apply to your own life.

我从小就积极进行自学。我自学了计算机编程、网页设计和写作等技能。我还自学了从世界宗教到进化心理学等各种知识，从未参加过任何正规课程。我想分享一些我在自学过程中发现的实用方法，或许对你有所帮助。

Most of the self-education I’ve done has been project-based, but there are other considerations to help improve your ability to teach yourself. Getting the right habits, overcoming the frustration barrier and setting learning goals are also helpful.

我的大部分自学都是基于项目的，但还有其他一些因素可以帮助你提高自学能力。养成良好的学习习惯、克服挫折感以及设定学习目标也都很有帮助。

202

Structuring Learning

结构化学习

Habits

习惯

A formal school structure makes forming the right habits easy. Show up to classes.

正规的学校制度有助于养成良好的习惯。按时上课。

Read your textbook. Take the tests. Take notes in class. All of these behaviors are not only given by the instructor, but are reinforced by the hundreds of people who surround you in classes.

认真阅读课本，参加考试，课堂上做好笔记。这些行为不仅由老师指导，也受到课堂上数百名同学的督促和强化。

Self-education is harder to form the right habits because no role-models are easily available. The structure of what you want to learn isn’t handed to you on the first day.

自学更难养成正确的习惯，因为没有现成的榜样可供借鉴。你想学习的内容框架不会在第一天就摆在你面前。

This flexibility can become a weakness if you don’t have the right learning habits.

如果没有正确的学习习惯，这种灵活性可能会变成一种弱点。

Here are some habits to consider as keys to improving your learning ability: 1) Daily Reading

以下几个习惯有助于提高学习能力：1）每日阅读

Reading every day is one of the best ways to improve your understanding. I strive 203

每天阅读是提高理解力的最佳方法之一。我努力做到每天阅读 203

to read at least a book each week and 50-70 books each year. Books can’t teach you everything, but they form a solid foundation of ideas you can build any learning efforts from. By reading a large volume, you can structure your education more effectively, getting a wide variety of viewpoints on a subject instead of just one.

每周至少读一本书，每年读50-70本书。书籍虽然不能教会你一切，但它们能为你构建坚实的思想基础，让你在此基础上开展各种学习活动。通过大量阅读，你可以更有效地构建自己的学习体系，获得关于某一主题的多种观点，而不仅仅是单一视角。

2) Daily Practice

2）日常练习

By working on your projects and practicing your skills every day, you can enhance any understandings given to you through reading books. Practicing helps provide a structure for your learning, since it is the first time you will have a benchmark of your abilities.

通过每天完成项目和练习技能，你可以巩固从书本中获得的知识。练习有助于构建学习框架，因为这是你第一次能够衡量自身能力的基准。

3) Daily Goal Setting

3）每日目标设定

Reading and practice aren’t enough if they aren’t directed. If your efforts are aimed at every subject imaginable, you won’t get into any useful depth into a subject. But by setting learning goals and breaking it into daily increments, your learning can be more useful to you by learning subjects fully instead of just in pieces.

如果缺乏针对性，光靠阅读和练习是不够的。如果你对所有能想到的科目都一概而论，就无法对任何一个科目进行深入学习。但是，通过设定学习目标并将其分解成每日的小目标，你可以更有效地学习各个科目，而不是仅仅零散地学习。

204

How to Build Daily Habits

如何养成日常习惯

Building habits is another subject that warrants another book in itself. I’ve written

培养习惯是另一个值得单独写一本书的主题。我已经写过

another e-book f or that exact purpose. Changing habits isn’t that difficult, but here are a few tips to get yourself started on building the right habits to improve your self-education efforts:

另一本电子书正是为此目的而作。改变习惯并不难，以下是一些帮助你养成正确习惯、提升自学效果的建议：

1) Set a trial to condition a habit for 30 days. Decide to read forty pages a day for a month. Decide to practice your web-design skills for an hour every day. Decide to set daily goals for your learning over the next thirty day period. Thirty days make a habit.

1）设定一个为期30天的习惯养成试验。例如，决定每天阅读40页，持续一个月。或者，决定每天练习一小时网页设计技能。又或者，决定在接下来的30天里为自己的学习设定每日目标。30天足以养成一个习惯。

2) Be consistent. Set your trial to do the same habit every day, in the same way.

2）保持一致性。设定目标，每天以相同的方式做同样的习惯。

Reading one day, listening to a speaker the next and practicing a third day are too disjointed to become habits.

一天阅读，第二天听演讲，第三天练习，这样的安排太零散，难以养成习惯。

3) Enjoy the habit. If you don’t enjoy it, your habit won’t stick. If you brainstorm a list of ways, it isn’t hard to find ways to enjoy activities like reading, practicing and goal-setting.

3）享受习惯。如果你不喜欢某个习惯，它就无法坚持下去。如果你列出一些让自己享受阅读、练习和设定目标等活动的方法，就不难找到这些方法。

205

4) Pick a time. I like to do morning reading, because it gives me uninterrupted quiet hours where I can focus my thoughts on a particular subject. Picking a specific time each day will reinforce your habit.

4）选择一个时间。我喜欢晨读，因为这样我可以享受一段不受打扰的安静时光，专注于某个特定的主题。每天选择一个固定的时间阅读有助于养成这个习惯。

If you aren’t sure where to find the time to do daily reading or practice, ask yourself how much television you watch or web surfing you do. If you are serious about learning on your own and can’t seem to find the time, TV and StumbleUpon need to be the first things to go.

如果你不确定如何抽出时间进行日常阅读或练习，不妨问问自己每天看多少电视或上网。如果你真心想自学，却总是找不到时间，那么首先应该减少看电视和浏览网页的时间。

如何改变一个习惯。

206

Overcoming the

克服

Frustration Barrier

挫折障碍

Self-education and frustration often go hand-in-hand. Without an instructor who can show you what you’re doing wrong, or a guidebook to tell you the next step, self-education requires more patience than taking classes. While I’ve found classes usually drag at a slow pace, self-education can go too fast.

自学往往伴随着挫败感。没有老师指导你哪里做错了，也没有指南告诉你下一步该怎么做，自学比上课需要更多的耐心。我发现课程进度通常比较慢，而自学又容易过快。

Ultimately, overcoming frustrations in self-education is a matter of motivation. If you are interested in a subject and that subject is important to you, a few speed-bumps won’t keep you from continuing forward. However, I’ve found it useful to have a few methods to overcome the frustration barrier so self-learning can go smoothly.

归根结底，克服自学中的挫折感取决于动力。如果你对某个学科感兴趣，并且这个学科对你很重要，那么一些小挫折并不会阻止你继续前进。然而，我发现掌握一些克服挫折感的方法很有帮助，这样自学才能更顺利。

Here are a few tips for reducing the frustration barrier: 1) Write Down any Obstacles. If I encounter a programming problem I don’t currently know how to solve, I try to write down the problem in as much detail as 207

以下是一些降低挫败感的小技巧：1）记录所有障碍。如果我遇到一个目前不知道如何解决的编程问题，我会尽可能详细地把问题写下来。

possible first. Writing obstacles out thoroughly makes it easier to think through problems.

首先，把所有障碍都详细列出来，有助于更清晰地思考问题。

2) Use Forums. There are online forums for just about any discipline, skill or subject. If you are having trouble understanding an idea, or are looking for books to explain it, online forums can be incredibly helpful. Search online for answers first, but keep forums as a tool in case you get stuck.

2）利用论坛。几乎任何学科、技能或主题都有相应的在线论坛。如果你难以理解某个概念，或者正在寻找相关的书籍，在线论坛会非常有帮助。首先在网上搜索答案，但也要把论坛当作一个工具，以备不时之需。

3) Get How-To Manuals. If you are trying to teach yourself a skill (doing your taxes, programming, graphic design, etc.) how-to manuals are invaluable. For a tiny fraction of the price of a full course, they can be an excellent reference if you get stuck.

3）购买操作手册。如果你想自学一项技能（比如报税、编程、平面设计等等），操作手册就非常宝贵。它们的价格远低于完整课程，而且在你遇到困难时可以作为极好的参考资料。

4) Attack From a New Angle. If you hit a roadblock in your understanding, try coming at the idea from a different viewpoint. Spend time working on other concepts and come back to it after you have learned more.

4）换个角度思考。如果你在理解上遇到障碍，试着从不同的角度看待这个问题。花些时间研究其他概念，等你掌握了更多知识后再回头解决它。

208

Setting Learning Goals

设定学习目标

One of the biggest challenges with self-education is that there is little structure.

自学最大的挑战之一是缺乏结构。

There are no goals, few plans and little direction. Although this loose format makes it easy to explore what you want to learn, instead of what are told you need, it also makes it harder to stick with. Without structure, it requires far more internal discipline to keep going through minor obstacles.

没有目标，计划寥寥，方向也模糊不清。虽然这种松散的模式便于探索自己想学的东西，而不是别人告诉你应该学的东西，但也使得坚持下去更加困难。缺乏结构，就需要更强的自律性才能克服小障碍。

I’ve found it helpful to create learning goals to give yourself an extra push. Here are a few example goals you could set to give the learning process more structure:

我发现设定学习目标很有帮助，可以给自己额外的动力。以下是一些你可以设定的目标示例，它们能让学习过程更有条理：

- Read a certain amount of books each year.

每年阅读一定数量的书籍。

- Work towards a project that requires learning.

- 参与需要学习的项目。

- Be able to do something before a deadline. Example: Be able to compose a song, complete your financial statements or speak in Latin before June 3.

- 能够在截止日期前完成某项任务。例如：能够在6月3日前创作一首歌、完成财务报表或用拉丁语交流。

209

The idea of giving yourself forced deadlines and constraints might not sound like fun. Won’t goals just suck off the spontaneity of the moment?

给自己设定强制性的截止日期和限制听起来可能不太有趣。目标岂不是会扼杀当下的自发性吗？

I’ve found the opposite is true. Having too much structure can be suffocating (as I’m sure many feel about formal education). But too little can make learning boring and aimless. Setting your own learning goals allows you to set the right amount of structure so you can explore new ideas, but also educate yourself in a systematic fashion.

我发现事实恰恰相反。过多的结构化学习会让人感到窒息（我相信很多人对正规教育都有这种感觉）。但结构化程度过低则会让学习变得枯燥乏味、漫无目的。设定自己的学习目标，既能让你拥有适度的结构，从而探索新思想，又能系统地进行自我教育。

A few tips on setting your learning goals:

设定学习目标的一些建议：

1) All Goals Need to Be Written. A goal that isn’t written down, doesn’t exist.

1）所有目标都需要写下来。没有写下来的目标，就等于不存在。

Write down your goal as a few sentences, along with a deadline.

用几句话写下你的目标，并设定一个截止日期。

2) Make it Objective. At any point along your progress, you should be able to easily decide whether you have achieved your goal. “Learning more” isn’t a goal, just a whim.

2）设定目标时要保持客观。在学习过程中的任何阶段，你都应该能够轻松地判断自己是否已经达成目标。“学习更多”并非目标，而只是一时兴起。

3) Set Difficult, But Achievable Deadlines. Giving yourself deadlines forces you to take action instead of just procrastinating. If the deadlines are too easy, they won’t inspire action until you are too far behind. If the deadlines are too hard, you’ve just created a recipe for frustration.

3）设定具有挑战性但可实现的截止日期。给自己设定截止日期能迫使你采取行动，而不是拖延。如果截止日期太容易，在你落后太多之前，它们不会激励你采取行动。如果截止日期太难，你只会徒增挫败感。

210

4) Break it Into Daily and Weekly Actions. Your goal should be broken into daily and weekly increments. A goal you need to complete today has more urgency than one due in a few months.

4）将目标分解为每日和每周行动。你的目标应该分解为每日和每周的小步骤。今天需要完成的目标比几个月后才需要完成的目标更紧迫。

5) Review Your Goals Regularly. Check over your goals at least once a week to see how you’re making progress.

5）定期回顾你的目标。至少每周检查一次你的目标，看看你取得了哪些进展。

需要帮助设定目标吗？您可以点击此处阅读我的九篇目标设定系列文章，了解更多信息。

Self-Education Summary

自学概要

Self-education has enormous potential if you are willing to pursue it. Getting the right habits and creating a structure for learning can be initially difficult, but afterwards those habits can be put to use towards any goal you might have.

如果你愿意投入，自学蕴藏着巨大的潜力。养成良好的学习习惯并建立学习体系起初可能比较困难，但之后这些习惯可以帮助你实现任何目标。

I’ve collected various resources for self-education you might find useful to get started:

我收集了一些自学资源，你可能会觉得它们对入门很有帮助：

EHow.com - 提供各种主题的操作指南文章。

FreeEd.net - “Free education on the Internet” according to their website.

FreeEd.net——根据其网站介绍，该网站提供“互联网上的免费教育”。

Portal to Free Online Courses – This article links to many major universities which offer free courses online.

免费在线课程门户网站——本文链接到许多提供免费在线课程的知名大学。

◦ Part IV ◦

第四部分

Summary

概括

of

的

Holistic Learning

整体学习

Getting Started

入门

Holistic learning isn’t something you can read over once and then master. It is a combination of a strategy along with various tactics, all designed to improve the way you learn. Practicing these methods along with experimenting on your own can give you more options.

整体学习并非读一遍就能掌握的。它结合了策略和多种技巧，旨在提升你的学习方式。实践这些方法并进行自主探索，可以让你拥有更多选择。

Where you take holistic learning is up to you, but if you aren’t sure where to start, here are a few suggestions:

如何进行整体学习取决于你，但如果你不确定从哪里开始，这里有一些建议：

Analyze Your Strengths and Weaknesses

分析你的优势和劣势

After reading through the holistic learning strategy, the first step should be to pinpoint where your strengths are and what you might have trouble with. Some of these weaknesses can be avoided (through picking courses that highlight your strengths), while others need to be compensated for.

通读整体学习策略后，第一步应该是找出你的优势和可能存在的不足。有些弱点可以通过选择能发挥你优势的课程来避免，而另一些则需要弥补。

You probably already have a good idea at what subjects you are skilled at (math, 214

你可能已经很清楚自己擅长哪些科目（数学，214）。

history, art, science, etc.). Now you should spend time asking yourself what points in the learning strategy and types of information you have the most difficulty with.

历史、艺术、科学等等）。现在你应该花时间问问自己，在学习策略和信息类型方面，你遇到的最大困难是什么。

For myself, I know that my strengths are in abstract and concrete information. I have a highly visual style of learning, which is reflected in many of my descriptions throughout this book. My strongest phase in the holistic learning sequence has always been the Explore phase, although practice has improved my ability to acquire and debug.

就我个人而言，我知道我的优势在于抽象和具体的信息。我的学习方式非常注重视觉呈现，这一点在本书的许多描述中都有所体现。在整体学习法中，我最擅长的阶段一直是探索阶段，尽管实践也提高了我的知识获取和解决问题的能力。

My weaknesses would be with arbitrary information. Learning the tools mentioned in the techniques portion of this book have helped greatly, but trying to store lists of facts, dates or definitions hasn’t been my specialty. Knowing my strengths and weaknesses in learning help me highlight where I can use my strengths and learn new techniques to smooth over any flaws.

我的弱点在于对杂乱无章的信息的处理。学习本书技巧部分提到的工具对我帮助很大，但记忆事实、日期或定义列表并非我的强项。了解自己的学习优势和劣势，有助于我明确发挥自身优势的领域，并学习新的技巧来弥补不足。

Start a Mind Challenge

发起思维挑战

The Mind Challenges are set up for the purpose of building new habits. Many of these methods are initially slower, if you aren’t used to them. Taking on a challenge for the next 2-4 weeks, can build up your speed and effectiveness using them. Eventually you will need to tailor your approach to suit your goals.

这些思维挑战旨在帮助你养成新习惯。如果你不习惯这些方法，一开始可能会比较慢。在接下来的2-4周里，尝试完成一项挑战，可以逐步提高你的速度和效率。最终，你需要根据自己的目标调整方法。

215

Here are a few important tips to make sure that the holistic techniques stick: 1) Commit for at least 3 weeks. There might be several techniques you want to explore from this book. But unless you spend at least three weeks working through a Mind Challenge, you won’t be able to turn the new method into a habit.

以下是一些确保整体疗法有效实施的重要提示：1）至少坚持三周。本书中可能有很多你想尝试的疗法。但是，除非你至少花三周时间完成一项思维挑战，否则你无法将新方法变成习惯。

2) One at a time. Don’t try to take on several challenges at once. Focusing on one challenge at a time, for the entire duration, will have a bigger shift.

2）一次只处理一个问题。不要试图同时应对多个挑战。在整个过程中，每次只专注于一个挑战，才能取得更大的成效。

3) Metaphor, Visceralization, Diagramming first. Those techniques form the core of the holistic learning system. Pick one of these for your first challenge.

3）首先运用隐喻、内省和图解。这些技巧构成了整体学习系统的核心。选择其中一种作为你的第一个挑战。

4) Use the bonus material. Included with this book are six printouts designed to help you with the Mind Challenges. Printing these off or creating your own can give you a template to make learning the new techniques easier.

4) 利用附赠材料。本书附有六份可打印资料，旨在帮助您应对思维挑战。您可以打印出来或自行制作，作为学习新技巧的模板。

5) Document your progress. Keep a one-sentence

5）记录你的进展。用一句话概括。

journal for your Mind Challenge. This means writing 1-2

为你的思维挑战写一篇日志。这意味着要写1-2篇。

sentences about your progress with the technique. This will make it easier to commit and will also help you to

用句子记录你运用这项技术的进展。这将使你更容易坚持下去，也有助于你……

troubleshoot any problems that might come up using the trial.

使用试用版排查可能出现的任何问题。

216

Setup a Better Studying Routine

建立更有效的学习习惯

Most of the focus of this book has been on mental activities to save studying time.

本书主要关注的是如何通过脑力活动来节省学习时间。

Better studying methods using a better strategy. If your study habits are sloppy, you might be wasting hundreds of hours, even if your learning strategy is fine.

更好的学习方法和策略。即使你的学习策略没问题，但如果你的学习习惯很懒散，你也可能浪费数百小时。

Here are a few productivity ideas you might want to consider: 1) Do you study a little bit each day or just cram before the final? Taking time to study every day can save you far more time in the long run than trying to study all at once. I tend to do my reading for the upcoming week on the weekend all at once.

以下是一些提高效率的小建议，或许你可以考虑一下：1）你是每天学习一点，还是考前临时抱佛脚？每天抽出时间学习，从长远来看比一次性全部复习要节省更多时间。我通常会在周末一次性把接下来一周的阅读内容全部看完。

Spending just a few hours a week on the weekend saves me from all-night cram sessions later.2) Are your notes and textbooks organized? While I’m a fan of the learn-it-once approach, sometimes you need to review. If all your material is scattered and unusable, this will waste time. Less mess means less stress.

每周周末花几个小时复习，就能避免之后熬夜苦读。2）你的笔记和课本整理好了吗？虽然我推崇“一次学会”的学习方法，但有时候复习也是必要的。如果你的资料散落各处，难以查找，就会浪费时间。资料越整洁，压力就越小。

3) Are you focused during your study sessions, or plagued with distractions? I study by myself without music, IM, cell phone messaging or any form of human contact. Putting myself into sensory deprivation keeps me focused on studying. If 217

3）你在学习时能集中注意力吗？还是容易分心？我独自学习，不听音乐，不看即时通讯软件，不发手机短信，也不与任何人接触。让自己处于感官剥夺状态能让我专注于学习。如果217

Becoming more productive and efficient is another topic, which I write about frequently on my own website as well as being the subject of various books. Here are just a few resources you might want to consider if you are trying to get more done in less time:

如何提高效率和生产力是另一个话题，我经常在自己的网站上撰写相关文章，这也是多本书籍的主题。如果您想在更短的时间内完成更多的工作，以下是一些您可能想要参考的资源：

Productivity Websites

生产力网站

ScottHYoung.com - 我的网站，致力于提高效率、学习和习惯养成。

ZenHabits.net - 化繁为简，提高效率。

Lifehack.org——最大的效率提升网站之一。

PickTheBrain.com - 生产力和动力。

StudyHacks – 学生效率提升工具

StevePavlina.com – 为聪明人提供个人发展服务。

218

Productivity Books

生产力书籍

Getting Things Done - The classic by David Allen.

《搞定一切》——大卫·艾伦的经典之作。

The Power of Full Engagement - Energy management.

全力投入的力量——能源管理。

Zen To Done - A spin off of Getting Things Done, this one focuses on slowly building productive habits.

禅式做事——《搞定一切》的衍生方法，专注于循序渐进地培养高效习惯。

How to Be a Straight-A Student & How to Win at College – Both classic books that can help you become more productive and handle the challenges of learning. Definitely worth reading!

《如何成为全A学生》和《如何在大学取得成功》——这两本经典著作可以帮助你提高学习效率，应对学习挑战。绝对值得一读！

Decide What You Want

决定你想要什么

No technique, method or trick can replace motivation. If you don’t have a reason to learn, get good grades or know your subject, the best you can do is drag yourself to class. I would never say I’ve loved every class I’ve taken. In fact, I’ve hated classes even after getting an A.

任何技巧、方法或诀窍都无法取代动力。如果你没有学习的动力、没有取得好成绩的动力或没有掌握学科知识的动力，你所能做的最好的事情就是勉强自己去上课。我从没说过我喜欢上过的每一门课。事实上，即使拿了A，我也讨厌某些课。

However, I’ve always been motivated by learning. New ideas and subjects fascinate me, even if the classroom format they are presented in do not. That drive to learn has made using the holistic learning strategy far easier in the long run.

然而，我一直以来都对学习充满热情。新的想法和课题总能让我着迷，即便我并不欣赏它们的课堂呈现方式。正是这种学习动力，使得我能够更轻松地运用整体学习策略。

219

Nobody can make you interested in a class you find boring. No strategy can make you learn something you don’t want to. If you’re only chasing a piece of paper from a prestigious University, instead of the knowledge and ideas that paper represents, then I don’t think any strategy can be helpful.

没人能让你对一门你觉得无聊的课产生兴趣。任何策略都无法让你学习你不想学的东西。如果你只是为了追求名牌大学的文凭，而不是文凭所代表的知识和理念，那么我认为任何策略都无济于事。

Find your reason for learning. Even if the reason is as simple as curiosity, find a reason to want to know.

找到你学习的理由。即使理由很简单，比如好奇心，也要找到想要了解知识的理由。

220

Recap of Major Concepts

主要概念回顾

At over 200 pages, this book has covered a lot of material. This recap of all the material can serve as a reference if you want to review any ideas or refresh your understanding.

这本书超过200页，内容非常丰富。这份内容概要可以作为参考资料，方便您复习巩固或巩固已有的知识。

Holistic learning is a strategy based on weaving information into webs, instead of bludgeoning yourself with rote-memorization. The foundation of this strategy is: 1) Constructs - The sum total of all connections that represent your knowledge about a subject. These are the cities of your mind.

整体学习是一种将信息编织成网络而非死记硬背的策略。该策略的基础是：1）建构——构成你对某一主题知识的所有联系的总和。这些联系就像你思维中的城市。

2) Models - Compact units of information that form the seeds of constructs. These are metaphors, visceralizations and diagrams. Models are the major intersections in the roadmap of your constructs.

2）模型——构成概念雏形的精简信息单元。这些模型包括隐喻、形象化描述和图表。模型是你构建概念路线图中的主要交汇点。

3) Highways - Connections between different constructs. These aid in creative thinking.

3）高速公路——连接不同结构之间的桥梁。这有助于创造性思维。

“Thinking outside the box” perfectly describes the act of thinking beyond the current constructs you have.

“跳出思维定式”完美地描述了跳出现有思维框架进行思考的行为。

221

Holistic learning works in a sequence of five steps. These steps aren’t always followed one-by-one, but this is the path they usually take:

整体学习分为五个步骤。这些步骤并非总是按顺序进行，但通常是遵循以下路径：

1) Acquire - Receiving information through your senses.

1）获取——通过感官接收信息。

2) Understand - Get the surface of information.

2）理解——掌握信息的表面。

3) Explore - Connect that basic idea to others. Exploration works in three main ways: a) Depth Exploration - Exploring the background of an idea.

3）探索——将基本想法与其他想法联系起来。探索主要有三种方式：a）深度探索——探索某个想法的背景。

b) Lateral Exploration - Exploring associated ideas.

b) 横向探索 - 探索相关想法。

c) Vertical Exploration - Exploring the idea as it relates to different constructs.

c) 纵向探索 - 探索该想法与不同结构之间的关系。

4) Debug - Prune away false connections.

4）调试 - 删除虚假连接。

5) Apply - Take an idea and give it meaning beyond immediate uses.

5）应用——将一个想法赋予其超越直接用途的意义。

Information is similar to digestion. The process is the same regardless of what you ingest. But the inputs can be very different. Taking into account different information types can help you plan your learning efforts. There are five major types of information: 1) Arbitrary - Facts, dates, lists, rules and sequences. They have little logical grouping or depth.2) Opinion - Information gathered for the sole purpose of supporting or defeating your argument. Volume is important here, rather than being able to memorize.

信息与消化类似。无论摄入什么，过程都相同。但输入的信息却可能千差万别。考虑不同类型的信息有助于你规划学习。信息主要分为五种类型：1）任意信息——事实、日期、列表、规则和顺序。这类信息缺乏逻辑性和深度。2）观点信息——收集信息的唯一目的是为了支持或反驳你的论点。这类信息注重的是数量，而不是记忆力。

3) Process - Information in the form of skills. Requires practice, but is easier to remember.

3）过程——以技能形式呈现的信息。需要练习，但更容易记忆。

222

4) Concrete - Ideas that are easy to visualize. These are often practical ideas that are easy to experience.

4）具体化——易于形象化的想法。这些通常是易于实践的想法。

5) Abstract - Ideas that are difficult to experience. Math, philosophy and physics are some of the most abstract fields.

5）抽象——难以体验的概念。数学、哲学和物理学是最抽象的领域之一。

Summary of Techniques

技术概述

Speed Reading

速读

1) Use a pointer.

1）使用指针。

2) Practice read.

2）练习阅读。

3) Use active reading to improve learning while reading.

3）运用主动阅读来提高阅读时的学习效果。

Flow-Based Note Taking

基于流程的笔记法

1) Don’t write notes in a rigid hierarchy.

1）不要按照僵化的等级制度来写笔记。

2) Create associations between briefly written ideas.

2）将简短写成的想法联系起来。

Metaphor

隐喻

Look for a story, image or process that mirrors what you are studying.

寻找与你所研究的内容相呼应的故事、图像或过程。

223

Visceralization

内脏化

1) Create a mental image of what you are studying.

1）在脑海中构建你所研究对象的图像。

2) Add other sensations and emotions to this image.

2）为这幅画面添加其他感觉和情绪。

3) Look for ways the image does not apply or does not fully cover the subject to prevent errors later.

3）检查图像是否不适用或是否完全涵盖主题，以防止以后出现错误。

Diagramming

图解

Create flow, concept or picture diagrams to link together several ideas onto the same source.

创建流程图、概念图或图片图，将多个想法联系起来，形成同一个来源。

Link Method

链接方法

1) Create a sequence of symbols that are easy to visualize.

1）创建一系列易于可视化的符号。

2) Create “links” between each item by visualizing a bizarre scene that combines the two.

2）通过想象一个将两者结合起来的奇异场景，在每个项目之间建立“联系”。

3) Create a link between the first sequence item and a trigger.

3）在第一个序列项和触发器之间创建链接。

Peg Method

钉板法

Same as link method except you link each idea to a list of 0-12 rhyming symbols you can recall easily.

与链接法相同，只是将每个想法与一个 0-12 个押韵符号的列表联系起来，以便于记忆。

224

Information Compression

信息压缩

Three main forms:

三种主要形式：

1) Mnemonics - Using words to compress several ideas into a single idea.

1）记忆术——用词语将几个概念压缩成一个概念。

2) Picture Compression - Create a picture that links several ideas under a single theme.

2) 图片压缩 - 创建一张将多个想法联系在同一主题下的图片。

3) Notes Compression - Rewrite a vast quantity of notes onto just a few pages.

3）笔记压缩——将大量笔记重写到几页纸上。

Practical Usage

实际应用

Look for ways to apply the idea in your daily life.

想办法将这个理念应用到你的日常生活中。

Model Debugging

模型调试

Practice questions in your subject regularly and look for potential errors in your holistic web.

定期练习你所学科目的题目，并检查你的整体思维导图中可能存在的错误。

Project-Based Learning

基于项目的学习

Set up projects of 1-3 months that will force you to learn new concepts. This is a useful exercise for self-education, where there is less structure to guide you.

设定一些为期 1-3 个月的项目，迫使你学习新概念。这对于缺乏指导的自学来说是一种有效的练习。

225

The Productive Student

高效学生

1) Manage Your Energy

1）管理你的能量

- Stay in shape, eat healthy and don't work without sleep.

保持健康体形，饮食健康，不要熬夜工作。

- Schedule a day off each week.

每周安排一天休息时间。

2) Don't “Study”

2）不要“学习”

3) Nuke Procrastination

3）核弹级拖延症

-Set up a Weekly and Daily Goals list to keep focused.

-制定每周和每日目标清单，以保持专注。

4) Batch smaller tasks into groups.

4）将较小的任务分组处理。

5) Be organized.

5）要有条理。

-Keep a calendar, to-do list and carry a notepad with you at all times.

- 随时准备一份日历、待办事项清单，并随身携带记事本。

Self-Education

自学

Self-education can be cheap, fast and rewarding but it also has challenges. Namely, it has less structure and is more difficult than formal education. The main ways you can improve your ability to teach yourself are:

自学成本低、速度快、收益高，但也面临一些挑战。例如，自学缺乏系统性，难度也高于正规教育。以下是一些提高自学能力的主要方法：

1) Improve your habits

1）改善你的习惯

2) Overcome the frustration barrier

2）克服挫折障碍

3) Set learning goals to track progress.

3）设定学习目标以跟踪进度。
